_about: Unity-only gameplay numbers (NIGHT8 U2-07; CLAUDE.md rule 5): mechanics the web game never had. GameConfig reads this file as the `design.` prefix next to PortExport/config.json and refuses to start if config.json ever gains a `design` key. Tests read this repo copy; SKYGRIND/Sync Port Data copies it to Assets/StreamingAssets/Design/ for the Player. Each section's `_why` says why the web has no such number. With every design flag off, the game is the web's.

movementTuning._why: GG 2026-10-26 (a quick fix from play): the Unity game's jump is 50% higher. The web's jump.height (1.5 m, PortExport/config.json) stays exact for the golden vectors; MovementTuning71.Apply scales it in the Survival boot only. The web has no such number.

ultra71._why: GG 2026-10-28: the jump lower (5.07 -> 4.0 m, apexTime 0.702 -> 0.6235 so gravity stays 20.58). GG 2026-10-26: movement almost a 1:1 copy of ULTRAKILL. Each value is ULTRAKILL's (Research/2026-10-26-ultrakill/movement.md: the wiki and a mod author's read of the decompiled NewMovement.cs) scaled x0.5143 to the 1.8 m body; times kept. Applied over the web's movement in the Survival boot only (MovementTuning71); the web's config and the golden vectors are unchanged. Off: -skygrindNoUltra71 (then movementTuning.jumpHeightMult applies). jump.doubleJumps is NOT set (ULTRAKILL has none; SKYGRIND keeps its double jump: PRINCIPLES rule 1, GG's call). Not mapped: air accel (a different model), eye height, body radius. Not applied: the slide values (floorSpeed 12.34, jumpBoostMaxSpeed 37, jumpHorizontalMult 1.0): with them the slide bounce (verbs37 row 13) went RED on 4 of 5 levels (Logs/feel/n71-polish3); without them it passes (n71-polish4). NIGHT72 N5 (the parity lab, Research/2026-10-27-wave72/N/evidence/n5-lab-2.txt): ground.friction and ground.accel 31.07 = ULTRAKILL's 25 % lerp per 8 ms tick at the 120 Hz step ((1 - 0.75^(8.333/8)) x 120): the Quake model with friction = accel is that lerp exactly; the walk stop and the 95 % accel fall from 0.34 s / 0.14 s to 0.067 s / 0.092 s (ULTRAKILL's own ticks: 0.088 s). Air accel NOT changed (3.6 would reach the cap in 0.27 s as ULTRAKILL does, but an optimal air strafe then gains 18.7 m/s per jump against 9.9 now and ULTRAKILL's 3.5: the Mover has no per-axis cap, and Mover.cs is not tonight's).

bright71._why: GG 2026-10-26: the rooms, the boss rooms most, are too dark. Game/Bright71.cs: the ambient / fog floor (UnityTuning.Bright71*) and no boss exposure cut. Off: -skygrindNoBright71.

parry._why: PERFECT PARRY (DESIGN-RESEARCH: ULTRAKILL's parry is offensive; DOOM: The Dark Ages' windows are 200-600 ms). The web's parry is one flat window (any punch during a wind-up). A punch in the last perfectWindow s of a wind-up heals to max HP instead of punch.parryHeal, freezes for perfectHitstop s instead of punch.parryHitstop, and pays the style award PERFECT PARRY (perfectPoints, the web's PARRY base x2) instead of PARRY.

director._why: PEAK FADE (Booth, GDC 2009: SUSTAIN PEAK, then PEAK FADE until a natural break, then RELAX). The web's director decays intensity always and starts RELAX with the peak's enemies still alive. With peakFade on: no intensity decay while a token holder is committed within engagedRange m; after PEAK, PEAK_FADE spawns nothing until intensity < fadeBelow and at most fadeEngaged enemies are engaged nearby (capped at fadeMaxTime s); then RELAX. With peakFade off, the directorMath golden vectors run unchanged.

n20._why: NIGHT20 U3-34.6 / U3-34.9 (GG: "you can kind of just camp out"; the additions backlog's A2 THE HUNT, A4 THE ELITE, A5 twists): the web's director has no special rounds as rituals and no height-aware camp score, so these are Unity-only. campHighStart s: the camp score starts after this on an unreachable perch (8 s on the ground: the web's); recycleAfter s: a husk that can't reach you on screen is recycled out of sight with its HP kept (CoD BO3, KF2). Builder E owns the numbers; off: NIGHT19's director. Builder E (first pass, 2026-10-06; Core/Enemies/Director20.cs, Research/2026-10-06-enemy-routes.md 5.4): an unreachable perch is a node no walker from the floor reaches over the grid's links (a breadth-first pass from the map's player spawn node, with the routes layer's links when design.routes is on, refreshed at most every checkEvery s on a miss); there the camp score rises over campHighRise s (the web's riseTime 6) and counts while you shoot (the ground rule's dealt-damage and kill-chain reliefs are what made perches free); the HUNTERS spawn first on a high node routed to you (the perch itself), a squad with no routed ground node spawns at the nearest floor that fits (no dead perches), and no spawn node under the top of a solid is used (Zones sampled 16 under the SE spire); recycleKinds are the melee walkers (the SPITTER and the DRONE hit you from where they are), checked every checkEvery s for view (the director's viewHalfAngle and line of sight) and route; the web's director.highKinds (DRONE, LANCER) spawn on high nodes (director.js spawnSquad). NIGHT20 (builder EN, THE FARM stall P2 found: seed 21, round 6, 3 DRONEs still 45+ s 63-66 m out, two pinned at y 39.4 under the map's 40 m roof; the round never cleared; ASSIST on: 9 of 20 farm runs timed out): drone.js's climb looks down from climbProbeHeight (40 m) over a blocked probe, which under the Survival map's roof barrier lands on the roof, so a blocked drone climbs to 43.6 m and pins itself there with no horizontal speed. With the block on, a drone's climb looks down from under the first roof above its probe (so it clears the wall it met), a climb that gains no height for droneClimbStall s lets go and does not re-latch for droneClimbHold s, and the failsafe also takes a DRONE that stays further than droneFar m from you without closing droneGain m for recycleAfter s (on screen or off: a flier has no watchdog) and sends it back on a high node with its HP.

lab._why: The LAB (NIGHT8 U2-16; DESIGN-RESEARCH section 4, decision D-03): research proposals that change an earlier GG decision, as opt-in A/B toggles for Demo Day. The web has none of them (it removed close-kill heals in 3.0; its freshness has no DULL; its state multiplier is flat; READY starts at survival.readyFrom; the squad interval is flat). The toggles are settings (lab.* booleans in the settings JSON, the LAB tab), all off by default; a run reads them at its start; a run with any on is stamped LAB on the results and never stored as a personal best. With every toggle off the game is the web's.

toggles.name: CLOSE-KILL HEAL
toggles.desc: A punch or gauntlet kill, or any kill within 4 m, heals 15; regen climbs at 12 HP/s

toggles.name: FRESHNESS TEETH
toggles.desc: FRESH weapons pay x1.5 style; a DULL tier under 2.5 pays nothing

toggles.name: STYLE RAMP
toggles.desc: Style ramps to x3 over 1 s of air, slide or wall ride; the ground resets it

toggles.name: READY FROM ROUND 1
toggles.desc: Hold BUY in any break to start the round now

toggles.name: SQUADS TIGHTEN
toggles.desc: Squads come x0.96 faster each round, never under 1 s apart

toggles.name: ULTRA HEALTH
toggles.desc: 35% of each hit is hard damage no heal fills until it drains (faster from AIRBORNE); your hits within 4 m heal you

closeKill._why: DESIGN-RESEARCH 4.1 health from aggression (Doom's push-forward combat, ULTRAKILL): a kill up close heals, and regen slows to compensate. range is the KillEvent distance (the shot's length).

freshness._why: DESIGN-RESEARCH 4.2 freshness with teeth (ULTRAKILL: FRESH x1.5, STALE x0.5, DULL x0). The web's tiers are FRESH x1.1, USED x1, STALE x0.5 (style.freshness, 0..10 with freshAt 7.5 and usedAt 5); dullAt continues that 2.5 spacing.

styleRamp._why: DESIGN-RESEARCH 4.3 style ramps with movement (ULTRAKILL). The web's state multiplier is a flat style.stateMult (1.2) in the air, dashing, wall riding, slamming, sliding or swinging. Here it climbs from that to rampMax over rampTime s of those states without a break, and is 1 on the ground as on the web.

ready._why: DESIGN-RESEARCH 4.4 READY from round 1. The web's survival.readyFrom is 3.

squads._why: DESIGN-RESEARCH 4.4 a squad interval that tightens per round: director.squadInterval x perRound^(round-1), never under floor s. The web's interval is flat (2.2 s).

ultraHealth._why: ULTRA HEALTH (NIGHT11 U3-24.9; Core/UltraHealth.cs), a LAB toggle, off by default: D-18 (ULTRAKILL's health as the default) stays GG's call, and the LAB is where a proposal that changes an earlier call goes (D-03). The web has neither half: its health regenerates (regen.delay 4 s, regen.rate 25 HP/s) and it removed close-kill heals in 3.0. ULTRAKILL's health (NIGHT11-RESEARCH.md B.1, B.2 and C.5; https://ultrakill.wiki.gg/wiki/Health , https://ultrakill.wiki.gg/wiki/Difficulties): hardShare: 35% of each hit (Standard) becomes hard damage, and every heal and regen fills only to max - hard; a hit sets the timer to timerBase (1 s) when it isn't running and every hit adds damage / timerDivisor (1/20) s; once it runs out, hard damage drains at drainByRank HP/s by the style rank (0..4: DULL COOL BOLD AIRBORNE SAVAGE) while the timer runs timerRateByRank x as fast; from wipeRank (SKYGRIND) it is wiped at once. The rank mapping: ULTRAKILL drains 15 below Supreme, 40 at Supreme (timer x2), 50 at SSadistic (x2.5), 60 at SSShitstorm (x3) and wipes at ULTRAKILL; SKYGRIND has 6 ranks, two fewer above its base three, so AIRBORNE (A, rank 3) takes Supreme's 40 / x2, SAVAGE (S, rank 4) SSShitstorm's 60 / x3 (SSadistic's 50 / x2.5 is dropped) and SKYGRIND (SS, rank 5) ULTRAKILL's wipe. The blood heal: a player hit within bloodRange m (the player's distance to the hit point; ULTRAKILL publishes no radius, so the LAB's close-kill 4 m) heals blood[weapon], bloodHead[weapon] on a headshot: ULTRAKILL heals a set amount per attack and hit spot, not a share of the damage (a punch 10 / 20 / 30, a hitscan head 30, a pellet 3, a nail 1); here the punch and PULSE GAUNTLET 20, KESTREL 10 (30 on a headshot; its ricochet 10), THUNDERCLAP 10 per enemy hit (its pellets are summed per enemy), STITCHER 1 per nail, LONGWAVE 30, COMET 0 (an explosion's blood doesn't heal in ULTRAKILL); every other source (secondary damage, impact waves) heals nothing. A parry heals to the cap (max - hard; ULTRAKILL's parry is a full refill). Regen stays (ULTRAKILL has none; the A/B changes one thing at a time) and fills only to the cap too.

box._why: THE MYSTERY BOX (NIGHT10 U3-13.8, decision D-20; Core/MysteryBox.cs). The web game never had one: it is Call of Duty Zombies' box (ZOMBIES-ULTRAKILL-RESEARCH.md section 2.1). CoD's numbers: price 950; the teddy ladder by the number of pulls since the box last moved (teddyPulls are each band's last pull: 1-3 0%, 4-7 15%, 8-12 30%, then 50%); a teddy refunds the price and moves the box to another spot (pulls start over). Fire Sale is not ported; SKYGRIND has no ammo, so there is no Max Ammo analogue. Unity-side picks, not CoD's: revealTime (the cycle, one gun per cycleTime), offerTime (the gun waits, then sinks), teddyTime (the bear shows), moveTime (the box is gone before it lands), seedSalt (the box's Mulberry32 is runSeed ^ seedSalt, 0xB0C5). The pool is every catalog gun (not melee) the loadout fires and the player doesn't own. spots: feet, yaw (the front faces (sin yaw, 0, cos yaw), as data.perkSpots), zone id; the first is in the starting zone (LANDING). Chosen by collider casts on the Survival map (a scratch probe through Tools/CoreHarness, the C# collider: the map Octree plus the core at 'flat'): each floor is y 0 by rays down from 3 m and from 39 m, flat over a 1 m radius (8 rays, spread 0); a capsule of radius 1 m from the floor to 2.2 m touches 0 triangles and overlaps 0 map boxes; open sky (the ceiling ray hits the 40 m barrier); the whole 1 m disc is inside its zone; the nav grid node under it is reachable from the player spawn on walk and drop links; at least 4.5 m from every perk machine, the forge, the zone gate buy spots, the trap switches, and away from the pads, hold spots, the spawn and the ARMORY wall. LANDING (-8.4, 0, 30): against the west slab's inner face (1.1 m behind, at -x), the ramp side 1.5 m to its south, faces +x into the landing, seen from the spawn eye (13.1 m), 7.5 m from THE GRINDER's gate buy spot. THE GRINDER (19, 0, 22.9): against the ARMORY's outer south wall (1.1 m behind, at +z), faces -z into the grinder, on the core (flat all run). SLAB GARDENS (0, 0, -46.9): against the south outer wall (1.1 m behind), centred between the two covers (4 m each side), faces +z toward the grinder, 6.4 m from QUICK (which stands 9 m up).

ultra._why: THE ULTRAKILL ALIGNMENT (NIGHT10 U3-13.9, decision D-17, GG 2026-10-03: ON; Core/Ultra.cs). The web keeps its own rules, and ULTRAKILL's (its wiki; ZOMBIES-ULTRAKILL-RESEARCH.md sections 2.2 and 4 #3) differ: freshDamage false: the arsenal's FRESH (lerp(0.65, 1.25) on damage and points on the web, weapons.arsenal) multiplies points and style only, never damage (ULTRAKILL's freshness changes style only; players call freshness on damage inconsistent); PRIMED, CROSS / combos and the statuses keep their damage. styleBreakPause true: the style meter does not drain during a break, or while no live enemy is within style.trickEnemyRange (the web drains style.drainBase + drainPerRank x rank every step, breaks included). parryRefillsDash true: a parry refills the dash pips (ULTRAKILL refills stamina; the web's punch.js and melee.js parries already call mover.restoreStamina(), so true is the web's rule too and false is the A/B). parryHitstop 0.25: a parry freezes 0.25 s (ULTRAKILL) instead of the web's punch.parryHitstop 0.06; a PERFECT PARRY keeps design.parry.perfectHitstop. Without this section (the golden sets, the replays) every rule is the web's.

power._why: THE POWER SWITCH (NIGHT11 U3-24.6; Core/Power.cs). The web game never had one: it is Call of Duty Zombies' power switch (NIGHT11-RESEARCH.md A.1 and C.3: one switch a few doors deep turns several systems on at once, the run's first goal; Kino der Toten's is 4 doors deep, about 4,250 points, thrown around round 3, Der Riese's 'after around round 5': https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/boards/960188-call-of-duty-black-ops/57125185 , https://call-of-duty-nazi-zombies.fandom.com/wiki/Forum:Kino_der_Toten_Solo_Strategy ; BO7 brings switches back: https://dotesports.com/call-of-duty/news/black-ops-7-ashes-of-the-damned-turn-on-power). It wakes the web's own power systems: traps.js's traps can be bought only with the power on, and protocol.js's relays wake at the first round begin with the power on and the round at least protocol.wakeRound (the web's pacing kept; the power is the extra key). THE FORGE stays open from round 1 (the web's rule, as BO6's Liberty Falls keeps Pack-a-Punch open: https://www.dexerto.com/call-of-duty/black-ops-6s-liberty-falls-has-finally-fixed-zombies-biggest-problem-2966268/). enabled false: no switch and the web's rules (traps always buyable, the PROTOCOL at protocol.wakeRound). The switch: hold E, free (price 0), perks.reach; powerOn {owner} (port-only) and the web's banner. spot: feet, yaw (the front faces (sin yaw, 0, cos yaw)), zone. Chosen by collider casts (a scratch probe through Tools/CoreHarness on the C# collider: the map Octree plus the core at 'flat', every gate open; design.box's checks). HEIGHTS is 2 gates from the spawn (the gate graph from maps/survival.json's zone buy spots: LANDING -> SLAB GARDENS 1000 -> HEIGHTS 1500 = 2500 points; ISLANDS, 3 gates, gave 0 spots: 884 candidates not flat over 1 m, the 1096 flat ones none wall-backed with every feature 4.5 m away). In HEIGHTS 439 spots were wall-backed (a wall 1.0-1.6 m behind, 3 m open in front) and 4.5 m from every feature: 436 on the spire tops and ledges, which no nav route reaches (the 2.5 m ledge steps are over ai.grid.jumpUp 2.2 m), and 3 at a skybridge's end whose 'wall' is the 0.5 m lip of a spire ledge, 4.56 m from a pad landing. So the switch stands free on the west skybridge (-42, 9, 4.5): floor y 9 by rays down, flat over a 1 m radius (8 rays from 3 m up, spread 0), a 1 m capsule from the floor to 2.2 m touches 0 triangles and overlaps 0 map boxes, 16 of 16 up-rays open, the 1 m disc inside HEIGHTS; nav node 6115 is reachable from the player spawn on walk, drop, jump and gap links plus pad 2's launch ((-26.5, 0, 0) -> (-39.5, 9, 0), the pad that HEIGHTS's west gate wakes): one pad ride after the gate; nearest features: pad 2's landing 5.15 m, the ISLANDS gate spot 6.02 m and its buy point 7.26 m, the west HOLD ring 11.72 m (9 m below). Faces +x (yaw pi / 2), toward the landing and the arena. The checks it gives up is the wall behind; the ones a player feels (reachable, clear, flat) hold.

zombies._why: THE SWARM ROUND'S DROP (NIGHT11 U3-24.3; Core/SwarmDrop.cs). The web's swarm rounds (directorMath.isSwarmRound: 8, 13, 18 ...; director.rounds.swarmFrom / swarmEvery / swarmOffset) have no warning and no reward. CoD Zombies' dog rounds (NIGHT11-RESEARCH.md A.2 and C.4): a warning when one starts (fog and 'Fetch me their souls!'; BO6: a music sting and green fog), and the last kill always drops a Max Ammo (BO6 calls them Max Ammo rounds): https://www.codzombiesguides.com/bestiary/hellhound/ , https://callofduty.fandom.com/wiki/Special_Round . SKYGRIND has no ammo, so the drop is the web's kill-drop roll, forced. swarmDrop true: a swarm round opens with a banner and swarmRound {round} (port-only); on its roundClear one power-up, its type drawn from the run's power-up stream (powerUps.js spawn with no type), lands at the round's last player kill: swarmDrop {round, type} (port-only); a swarm round with no player kill drops nothing. false: nothing (the web's swarm round). No number of its own: the schedule stays the web's.

exfil._why: EXFIL (NIGHT11 U3-24.7; Core/Exfil.cs). The web game has no ending but death. CoD Zombies' exfil (NIGHT11-RESEARCH.md A.3 and C.2): Cold War offers it from the end of round 10 at a radio at the spawn, then every 5; BO6 from round 11, every 5 (11, 16, 21 ...): about 90 s to reach the site, then 35 kills in about 85 s at round 11, the demand growing with the round, and failure ends the run (https://www.treyarch.com/game-intel/2020/10/Black_Ops_Cold_War_Zombies_Gameplay_Guide , https://game8.co/games/Call-of-Duty-Black-Ops-6/archives/481913 , https://gamerant.com/bo6-cod-call-of-duty-black-ops-6-zombies-exfil-exfiltration-guide/); frequent, safe exfils made Cold War feel too easy (https://lv1gaming.com/call-of-duty-cold-war-zombies-is-too-easy-and-thats-a-problem/), so here it ends the run either way. In the break before round R (R >= from, (R - from) % every == 0) the radio (hold E, free, perks.reach) calls it (exfilCall); round R is then the exfil and can't clear while it runs: at its begin the site is picked (exfilStart); REACH: stand within siteRadius m of the site (the HOLD ring's 4 m, objectives.radius) and siteHeight m of its floor within reachTime s (exfilReach); HORDE: kills player kills within killTime s, the director at full pace and its queue topped up from the round's own squad plan (directorMath.planSquads for round R on a Mulberry32 of the run seed ^ seedSalt) whenever fewer enemies remain than kills are still needed; success (exfilDone) ends the run as a win (RESULTS: EXFIL; records keep an exfil flag), failure (exfilFail: 'time' in REACH or HORDE, 'death') as a death (EXFIL FAILED). The kill demand grows per later exfil (a Unity-side pick: BO6 publishes no table): kills + killsPerExfil x ((R - from) / every) = 35 at 11, 45 at 16, 55 at 21. The site: sites[((R - from) / every) % 3], else the next one whose zone is open (the radio isn't offered while none is): SLAB GARDENS at 11, THE GRINDER at 16, HEIGHTS at 21, again from 26. Spots by collider casts (a scratch probe through Tools/CoreHarness on the C# collider: the map Octree plus the core at 'flat', every gate open; design.box's checks). radio (-4, 0, 42.9), LANDING: flat over 1 m, a 1 m capsule from the floor to 2.2 m touches 0 triangles and overlaps 0 map boxes, it backs onto the LANDING terrace's face (1.1 m behind, +z), faces -z into the plaza (4.4 m to the near cover), 4.94 m from the player spawn and seen from its eye, nav node 10636 on walk and drop links; nearest other features: pad 4's landing 7.67 m (6 m up), the SLAB GARDENS gate spot 8.51 m. sites, each a 4 m disc: flat on rings at 1, 2, 3 and 4 m (8 rays each), 1 m capsules at its centre and on rings at 2 and 3 m (12 each) touch nothing, no map box overlap, the disc inside its zone, the nearest HOLD ring over 9 m away: SLAB GARDENS (43.5, 0, -12), the east band, 15 of 16 up-rays open over the disc (the north-east skybridge's end overhangs one edge; no SLAB GARDENS 4 m disc is under fully open sky, the bands run under the skybridges), nav node 4370 on walk and drop links, nearest feature the east HOLD ring 14.15 m; THE GRINDER (-10.5, 0, -8), on the core (flat all run, as design.box's GRINDER spot), 16 of 16 open, node 4694 on walk and drop links, seen from the spawn eye, nearest MEND 16.01 m; HEIGHTS (-40, 24, -40), the north-west spire top, 16 of 16 open, nearest the ISLANDS gate spot 12.54 m (6.5 m down): node 911 is on no nav route (the spire's 2.5 m ledge steps are over ai.grid.jumpUp 2.2 m), so the third exfil is a climb (pad 3 to the 10 m ledge, then the ledges, as the web's PLATE on the north-east spire top) and its horde is fought below.

contracts._why: CONTRACTS (NIGHT12 U3-25.7; Core/Contracts.cs; agent E1 fills this block). Port-only contracts beside challenges.js's 24 badges, to 30-40 in all, each unlocking variety, never stats (the web's own rule in unlocks.js): Research/2026-10-03-retention.md P3 and section 5 #1 (Vampire Survivors' first unlock at 1 minute reaches 97.8% of players; Hodent: show the locks). Mechanical texts only (D-32). enabled false: only the web's 24. first: the first unlock, FIRST FIFTEEN (15 kills, any weapon): round 1 sends director.rounds.base + perRound x 1 = 9 enemies and round 2 sends 12, so a first run reaches it in round 2; it grants 'daily' (opens the DAILY on the run setup; the web's flag also unlocks the INTEREST mod). webEarn: the two literals of the web's main.js earn() (round10 once round 10 begins, forge3 once 3 guns are forged in one run; config.js has no key for them; the earn triggers work with enabled false). webUnlocks: the web badge that shows main.js's round10 flag as its unlock (STYLE TAX). flagNames: the label of a flag that is no finish and no mod. list: 15 port-only contracts (39 with the web's 24) on P3's cadence (the first unlock in under 5 minutes, then one every 1-2 runs), counted from the port's events tonight (kinds: kills, round, power, wallBuys, boxPulls, slideKills, airKills, forgeRun, protocol, secretRelay, exfil (heat: on that HEAT rung or higher), daily, grade; also headshots, weaponKills (weapon), gates, perks); they never expire (section 4: no FOMO). Unlocks are variety only: the web's locked MODS by their flags (BEAT MONOLITH and WIN A TRIAL GOLD can't happen in the port, so FIVE DEEP grants monolith (SHRAPNEL) and BOX REGULAR grants trialGold (CROSSFIRE)); THREE FORGED, THE PROTOCOL and HIDDEN RELAY show main.js's own forge3 / protocol / secretRelay triggers as locks; the web unlocks GRAPHITE, ARCTIC, DUSK BRASS and MIRROR with trial medals and the port has no trials, so the port flag finish.<id> opens one for every gun: GRAPHITE at 500 kills (FIVE HUNDRED), DUSK BRASS at an exfil (WAY OUT), ARCTIC at an S grade (TOP MARKS), MIRROR at an exfil on HEAT 3 (WHITE HOT); MASTERY opens the first three sooner, one gun at a time. HEAT rungs are opened by Heat (an exfil on rung N), never here.

heat._why: HEAT (NIGHT12 U3-25.9; Core/Heat.cs; agent E2 fills this block). An opt-in difficulty ladder (Research/2026-10-03-retention.md section 5 #3: Balatro Red Stake 43.8%, Brotato Danger 5 36.5%, DRG Hazard 4 34.2%; Destiny 2 fell 80%+ after raising base difficulty, so the base game never gets harder). Rungs 1-3 are the web's mutators only (D-31). enabled false: no ladder on the run setup. rungs: rung N plays the mutators of rungs 1..N (cumulative: HEAT 3 = GLASS CANNON + SPEED DEMON + NO REGEN), each rung adding one readable rule (Research P2: 'each rung adds one readable rule'; its text is config.mutators.kinds.<id>.name / desc; LOW GRAVITY stays a fun toggle). scoreMult: the rung's own multiplier on the points earned (Heat.ApplyRung: the Economy boost 'heat', the way the web's SPEED DEMON boosts points with economy.setBoost; it stacks with SPEED DEMON's own x1.25 as every boost does); 1.25 / 1.5 / 2 rise with the rung because Hades' Heat and Balatro's stakes pay in score and a badge, never in stats (Research P2), and they are dyadic, so any product of boosts is exact. The web has no ladder, so it has no such numbers. An EXFIL on rung N opens rung N + 1 (profile.heat).

grade._why: THE GRADE CHASE (NIGHT12 U3-25.8; Core/Payoff.cs; agent E1 fills this block). p: ULTRAKILL's P-rank as a 'P' grade for an exfil at S grade with an SS peak and no down (Research/2026-10-03-retention.md section 5 #7). false: the web's grades only. pGrade and pPeak: the run's grade and the style peak's letter the rule needs (config.style.ranks' SS is SKYGRIND, the top rank); an exfil is Exfil.Win; no down means no revive used (RunStats.revived).

onboarding._why: THE FIRST RUN (NIGHT12 U3-25.11; Core/Tips.cs Onboarding; agent E2 fills this block). save._why: SAVE & QUIT (NIGHT13 U3-26.10; NIGHT14-RESEARCH.md section 4: BO6's rules, 'a feature players have been asking for since 2008'; Research/2026-10-04-comparables.md 0.6: 'No save system... Lose hours of playtime'). The web has no save or suspend (its localStorage holds only settings, records and challenges). With enabled on: solo, one slot, once at least minRounds rounds are cleared, at a round break only, never downed or during an exfil; SAVE & QUIT in PAUSED writes the run snapshot beside the profile and goes to TITLE; RESUME on TITLE loads it and deletes it; a file of another snapshot version is discarded with a log line. enabled false: no button, no file (the web's game).

autopilot._why: THE AUTOPILOT (NIGHT14 U3-27.5): the web's bot (botBrain.js, RIVAL's brain) driving the player's own body in SURVIVAL, as the web's attract loop drives it in the duel (main.js :702-721). The web has no SURVIVAL bot, so it has no target choice for a horde, no shopping, no gun choice past the duel's two guns and no MODS / FORGE choices: these numbers are new. difficulty picks config.bot's tables (easy | normal | hard). shopping is the order a break's shopping walks (Buyables ids: weapon:<id>, perk:<id>, forge; the first one affordable with the gates on the cheapest way to it, a gate bought first when its zone is locked). takeFirstMod takes the MODS draft's first card; forge appends THE FORGE (the gun in hand) to shopping when it isn't listed. targetSwitchMeters: a new target must be this much nearer than the current one (no flicker; one in line of sight beats one out of it). shopGiveUpSeconds: a shopping goal not bought after this much trying is dropped for the run (a machine the bot can't reach). guns.near / guns.far: the guns the bot takes in hand by distance (the first one owned; near below bot.shotgunRange - gunHysteresisMeters, far above bot.shotgunRange + gunHysteresisMeters, botBrain.js's own hysteresis, a literal 1 in the web's code). graphCandidates: without line of sight, the nearest this many enemies by straight distance are costed on the nav graph (A*), the cheapest one taken. rngSalt: the brain's rng (Math.random in the web) is a Mulberry32 stream from the run seed XOR this salt (NIGHT14 rule 8). A HOLD round (objectives.js) is unknown to the web's bot: the bot walks to the ring until within holdInsideShare of objectives.radius and holds it there, firing without moving; on the way it fights an enemy in sight within holdFightMeters first (the brain walking to the ring fires at nothing); holdHeightMeters is objectives.js's own inside height (|dy| under 2.5, a literal in the web's code). With enabled false the autopilot can't start (the farm and the attract refuse). shopRetryRounds: a goal given up after shopGiveUpSeconds is tried again this many rounds later (NIGHT14 review B-7: dropped for the whole run, one unreachable spot ended the bot's shopping).

n20._why: NIGHT20 P0-2 (the bot tells the truth; Research/2026-10-06-additions-backlog.md P0-2, QUEUE-first-fifteen U3-28.3): NIGHT19's farm measured the bot, not the game. 7 of 24 normal runs timed out on round 6 standing 4.5 m from the HOLD ring (the bot counted itself in only within holdInsideShare of objectives.radius, its nav stopped short of the ring, and inside it stood still and could not dodge), and 0 of 9 runs that reached round 11 called an exfil. With enabled: inside a ring is the game's own test (objectives.js: the full objectives.radius, |dy| under holdHeightMeters); when the nav stops short, or within approachMeters of a ring or a buy point (the nav graph's nearest node can sit metres off: NIGHT20's trace had the bot turning between it and the exfil radio until the break ran out), the bot walks the last metres straight; inside (or within ringReturnMeters of the centre with an enemy in sight within holdFightMeters) the brain aims and fires, moves freely within holdKeepShare of the radius from the centre and walks back past it (aim kept; no dash or slide there, and a jump only while moving toward the centre: one jump's air carried the bot out of a 4 m ring at 9 m/s). exfilFrom: in the first break at or after this round that offers the radio (design.exfil.from / every), the bot calls it (BO6's exfil is offered from round 11; a player who reaches it mostly takes it), walks to the site in the REACH phase by the same ring rule (design.exfil.siteRadius) and fights the HORDE; 0 never calls. exfilWalkRemaining: in the round before that break, once this many enemies or fewer are left (the director's remaining), the bot waits at the radio fighting what comes (running there with the last enemies chasing lost 9 of 40 bots in round 10 over 72 seeds; a 10 s break can't cross the map: NIGHT20's farm missed the call from 88 m away; a player heads for the radio on the last zombies); at most exfilWaitSeconds a round, then it hunts the last ones (NIGHT20's farm timed out once waiting at the radio for enemies that never came). Opt-in: THE FARM (and so THE MARATHON) calls AutopilotInput.TellTheTruth; an autopilot built elsewhere (THE CHASE, THE CLIMB's STAND, the attract) stays NIGHT19's, so the frozen judges don't move. The game's rules and numbers are untouched; the fingerprint has no bot in it. Off: NIGHT19's bot.

The web's RESULTS has no map. enabled false: no track, the old RESULTS.

aimAssist._why: AIM ASSIST DEFAULTS (NIGHT15 U3-28.7; GG, 2026-10-05: "auto aim is too strong"). The web defaults both the mouse (settings.aimAssist) and the pad (settings.padAimAssist) to 'snap' (a 12 deg cone, a 240 deg/s pull and a lock: config aim.*); shooters give the mouse no assist and the pad a slowdown plus light adhesion (MAP-RESEARCH.md section 5: Destiny 2, Apex, DOOM Eternal). Here a new profile starts with the mouse at `mouse` and the pad at `pad` ('assist': the web's mildest mode, a 6 deg cone with friction 0.55); snapStrength is unchanged. A saved setting still equal to `migrateFrom` (the old default) moves to the new default once (the settings file's _version 2, migration 'assist15'); a saved 'assist' or 'lock' is a player's choice and stays. The fingerprint run keeps the web's 'snap' (its baseline).

The web's radial picker is mouse-only (keyboardMouse.js), its rumble runs only with VIBRATION on (off by default) at full strength, and it has one neutral glyph set. Here VIBRATION starts on (vibrationDefault) with a RUMBLE row (0..1, rumbleDefault, scaling config.gamepad.vibration's motor strengths); the wheel opens while the NEXT WEAPON button is held wheelHold s (a tap stays NEXT WEAPON) or while a button bound to WEAPON WHEEL is held, the right stick past wheelStickDeadzone picks a sector, and releasing takes it.

Builder P owns it; off: NIGHT18's layout and prompts.

n20._why: NIGHT20 U3-34.4 (GG 2026-10-06 evening: "the right bumper could be used to switch weapons as well, just scroll through weapons"): the web's pad has no RB cycle, so these are Unity-only. layout v3: RB = NEXT WEAPON (a tap scrolls; held wheelHold s it opens the wheel, as Y did), Y = SPECIAL + ARCLINE (v2's two rows swapped); a saved v2 equal to the v2 default becomes v3, a customised v2 keeps its buttons unless it never touched RB and Y. Builder P owns the numbers; off: NIGHT19's v2 pad.

maps._why: MAPS (NIGHT15 U3-28.5): the web has one SURVIVAL map; GG asked for a new one (2026-10-05: "a map overhaul ... built to maximize movement and replayability"). The run setup's MAP row lists these in order: id, TITLE's label and the file (PortExport/ for the web's map, Design/maps/ for a Unity-authored one, each with a byte-identical Player copy under StreamingAssets). The old arena keeps its game and its fingerprint.

move._why: NIGHT16 U3-29.4 (GG 2026-10-05: "I want movement to be a little more balanced like you can't you know spam slide over and over"): the web's slide is free speed. A slide press snaps the speed to slide.floorSpeed (11.6 m/s, 1.45 x ground.walkSpeed) at once (mover.js startSlide), a held slide never drops below it on flat ground (stepSlide: friction only above the floor), and every slide-jump multiplies the speed by slide.jumpHorizontalMult up to jumpBoostMaxSpeed, so holding or mashing slide beats walking everywhere. The web never had these limits. Three rules, each with its own flag (on by default) and a LAB row (the settings move.slideCharge / move.slideDecay / move.hopFalloff; a run reads them at its start; automation uses these defaults) so GG can switch each one off; with every flag off the Mover is the web's (the golden vectors and the replays run the web's config, where this block is absent). Starting values from NIGHT16.md; FEEL-DESIGN.md section 3 records any retune and its measurement (SimHarness spam).

slideCharge._why: The snap up to slide.floorSpeed needs a charge: one charge, back rechargeTime s after the slide ends (the clock holds full while any slide runs). An uncharged slide keeps its entry speed (no burst, never a loss); a slide entered at or above the floor uses none; the press always slides (no lockout). Titanfall 2 / Apex: the slide boost has a 2 s cooldown (FEEL-DESIGN.md section 2). rechargeTime 2 (NIGHT16 builder M, SimHarness spam on a flat plane): slide tapped every 0.15 .. 2.0 s = 1.00 .. 1.04 x a walk's 10 s distance; a recharge-timed rhythm (slide 0.6 s, walk the recharge) 1.11 x (1: 1.19 x; 3: 1.09 x).

slideDecay._why: On flat ground, after sustainTime s of sliding the slide's floor eases from slide.floorSpeed toward ground.walkSpeed over decayTime s. A downhill slide is untouched (the slope boost still pays: DRYDOCK's slipway keeps its 28.8 m/s); uphill as the web.

hopFalloff._why: Each slide-jump within chainWindow s of the last landing gets a horizontal multiplier step lower than the one before (1.2, 1.05, 1.0, then 1.0: never below minMult); slide.jumpBoostMaxSpeed stays the cap. A well-timed first hop still pays in full. step 0.15 (NIGHT16 builder M, SimHarness spam): a slide-hop chain from walk speed peaks at 14.6 m/s (target 15; step 0.1 peaked at 15.3, the web's at 24).

impact._why: NIGHT16 U3-29.5 (GG 2026-10-05: "if you hit a punch or a certain attack or gun hit or head shot its like ultrakill where the game will almost pause or go slomo"): tiered impact freezes and a little slow-mo, drawn by the Game layer (Game/ImpactFrames.cs through SurvivalGame's loop: time and pictures only, never Core state, so the composed fingerprint stays EQUAL). The web freezes only on a player kill (feel.hitstopTime 0.04), a melee hit above feel.momentumHitstopAt (feel.momentumHitstop 0.045) and a parry (punch.parryHitstop; the port's design.ultra.parryHitstop 0.25 and design.parry.perfectHitstop 0.15, inverted: the better parry froze shorter); it never slows. The longest request wins (the web's hitstop). A budget keeps a horde from stuttering. HIT FREEZE (OFF / LIGHT / FULL) and SLOW-MO (ON / OFF) are settings with these defaults; REDUCED MOTION turns the slow-mo off. Starting values from NIGHT16.md; FEEL-DESIGN.md section 3 records any retune and the ledger that measured it (SimHarness impact).

freeze._why: Freeze seconds per moment (the longest request wins). NIGHT18 U3-31.3 (builder X; NIGHT18.md M4, the freeze ladder, measured as HELD sim steps at 120 Hz in the reel's 60 fps telemetry: a freeze holds 2 x floor(seconds x 60) steps plus 0 or 1 on the kill's own frame, the partial last frame unheld): hit 0-2 (a body hit has no tier), body kill 6-8 (kill 0.058: 6-7), headshot kill 10-13 (headshotKill 0.096: 10-11), punch kill 11-14 (punchKill 0.108: 12-13), a 5-kill blast >= 18 within a 160 ms cap (kill + killPerExtra x 4 = 0.158, capped at killCap 0.155: 18-19). The values sit off the frame edges (0.05 is exactly 3 frames and read 6 or 7 by rounding). NIGHT17's table is design.impact.n17.freeze (the FeelAB off side). Unchanged: heavyHit (a rocket's direct hit, a rail hit, a shotgun shot landing heavyPellets or more pellets in one body), headshot, punchHit (the momentum hit's feel.momentumHitstop stays a floor), parry (design.ultra.parryHitstop), perfectParry (longer than a plain parry: design.parry.perfectHitstop 0.15 stays the sim's own request). The sim's own kill request (feel.hitstopTime 0.04) is covered (the longest wins). killPerExtra / killCap: a step with N kills of the player's freezes kill + killPerExtra x (N - 1), at most killCap (ImpactRules.KillFreezeSeconds). The budget (perSecond 0.2) still fits the capped blast; it wins over the ladder (SimHarness impact).

n17._why: NIGHT18 (NIGHT18.md rule 2, the same-build A / B): NIGHT17's freeze table exactly as it shipped (u3-n17), the FeelAB off side. Game/ImpactFrames.cs builds Core's ImpactRules from design.impact.freeze (FeelAB on) or from this block (off), and swaps it in place on a flip (ImpactRules.UseFreezeTable). Only the freeze tiers differ; the cooldowns, the budget, the slow-mos and the settings are design.impact's for both sides.

freeze._why: Freeze seconds per moment (the longest request wins). kill: the web's feel.hitstopTime (the sim still requests it), raised to 0.05 by NIGHT17 round 3 (its reviewer: the body kill, the most common, held one frame and read as the weakest event; the longest request wins, so the sim's 0.04 is covered). heavyHit: a rocket's direct hit, a rail hit, a shotgun shot landing heavyPellets or more pellets in one body. punchHit: a punch or gauntlet hit (the momentum hit's feel.momentumHitstop stays a floor). parry: design.ultra.parryHitstop. perfectParry: longer than a plain parry (fixes the inversion: design.parry.perfectHitstop 0.15 stays the sim's own request, and this longer one wins in the loop). killPerExtra / killCap (NIGHT17 round 5, its reviewer: one THUNDERCLAP blast killing 5 husks froze 40-57 ms, less than one headshot): a step with N kills of the player's freezes kill + killPerExtra x (N - 1), at most killCap (5 kills: 0.15 s); the sim's own hitstop request is untouched (ImpactRules.KillFreezeSeconds, ImpactCountTests).

cooldown._why: The shortest real time between two freezes of one tier (s): a horde's kills can't chain into a stutter. A request inside its tier's cooldown is skipped and logged. any (NIGHT16 review finding 1): the shortest time between the starts of any two freezes when the later one is budgeted (a parry is exempt but still starts the gap): automatic headshots and a horde's kills froze 50, ran 55 ms, froze 50, a third cut to 20 ms, then nothing for 0.75 s every second (a 3-hitch chop); at 0.5 no rolling second holds three freezes (SimHarness impact) and the rest is evenly spaced; the rolling minute's perMinute already averages 1.5 kill freezes a second. parry / perfectParry (finding 3): a parry inside it (a chain at the punch's 0.35 s cycle) gets the web's punch.parryHitstop instead (budgeted): a perfect-parry chain froze ~46 % of real time (the review), now under 30 % (ImpactRulesTests.ParryChain, a 20 s chain).

budget._why: Frozen time at most perSecond s in any rolling second and at most perMinute of real time over a rolling minute (a fraction). perSecond 0.12 -> 0.2 in NIGHT17 round 5, so a capped multi-kill freeze (freeze.killCap 0.16) fits a rolling second; the cooldowns and the any-gap still space the freezes. A request over budget is skipped (or cut to what is left) and logged. Parries are exempt (rare, earned, and the moment GG asked for). maxFreeze: no single freeze is longer, whatever the tiers say (FEEL-DESIGN.md section 2: Smash caps hitlag at 0.5 s; ULTRAKILL's major hitstop is 0.25 s).

slowMo._why: The sim steps at 120 Hz as always, only fewer steps per real second (scale x real time), held for hold s of real time, then eased back to 1 over ease s. Slow-mos never stack (the strongest wins) and start at most one in any minGap s; none while DOWN, paused or in a menu.

settings._why: The defaults of the HIT FREEZE (off | light | full) and SLOW-MO rows; LIGHT scales every freeze (the web's included) by lightScale; OFF freezes nothing (the sim's own requests drain at once). The automation (the smoke, the AUTOPILOT, the farm, the attract, the tour) runs at full so the gates exercise it.

stamina._why: NIGHT17 U3-30.4 (GG 2026-10-05: "you should start out with only one bar ... you should be able to Sprint and it uses your [stamina] bar ... you can either choose the boost or hold a Sprint ... you can still boost even if the bar is not fully filled, it just won't be as much of a boost"): the web has three dash pips (dash.maxPips 3, pipCost 1, regenPerSec 0.7) and no sprint. These rules turn the pips into one continuous bar shared by the boost (the dash) and a new sprint, each rule with its own flag (on by default; a run reads them at its start; automation uses these defaults). With every flag off the Mover is the web's (the golden vectors and the replays run the web's config, where this block is absent). Starting numbers from NIGHT17.md U3-30.4 and Research/2026-10-05-overhaul.md section 3 (Vanquish, ULTRAKILL, Halo, DOOM Eternal); builder M records any retune and its measurement (SimHarness spam / verbs).

bar._why: One bar of 1.0 at the start instead of dash.maxPips 3 (GG: start with one bar). VIGOR (dash.vigorBonus pips on the web) adds bonusBars more. The HUD shows the bar under the crosshair (Ui's stamina bar), never the pips.

boost._why: The boost (the web's dash) fires on the press (no input lag: a hold only continues into the sprint) and costs up to cost bar. With less than its cost it still fires, its duration scaled by fill / cost with the speed unchanged (dash.speed 24 m/s: a slower dash feels mushy, so the distance scales instead), never below floor of the full boost (8 of 30 steps at 120 Hz); a fill of fullAt x cost or more counts as full so nobody waits for the last pixel. Its invulnerable steps scale with the duration. A dash-jump costs dashJumpExtra more (the web's dashJump.extraPipCost 1 pip of 3). dashJumpExtra kept at 0.25 (NIGHT17 builder M, spam with refill.rate 0.5): 0.5 (a boost's whole cost, the web's pip) gave the web's 1.86 x walk on the dash-jump chain but left an empty bar after every dash-jump (the web leaves one of three pips to dodge with); 0.25 leaves a quarter bar (a half-length boost) at 2.17 x walk.

sprint._why: Holding the boost key after the boost (STAMINA KEY: one key; Vanquish's boost into a slide) runs at speed m/s on the ground (under the slide's slide.floorSpeed 11.6, over ground.walkSpeed 8: the slide stays the fastest free move), draining drain bar/s while held and moving. It ends by itself when the bar is empty, with no lockout. Halo Infinite's sprint is ~8 % over a walk; this one is 31 %.

refill._why: The bar refills at rate bar/s (the web's 0.7 pips/s of 3 = 0.23 of the whole per s) once delay s have passed since the last spend (emptyDelay s if a sprint emptied it). Never while boosting or sprinting. rate 0.5 (NIGHT17 builder M, SimHarness spam on the flat plane; was 0.8): at 0.8 the bar paid for a full boost every ~1.3 s (dash on each charge 1.45 x walk, the web's 1.35 x) and the dash-jump chain ran at 24 m/s for good (2.56 x walk, the web's 1.86 x); at 0.5 a boost comes back every ~1.65 s, the web's ~1.68 s (1.35 x, equal), the dash-jump chain 2.17 x, and the sprint rows don't move (they spend the bar the boost left). One bar refills in 2 s.

rewards._why: Aggression pays for motion (ULTRAKILL's parry refill, DOOM Eternal's resource kills): a kill adds kill bar, a slam's landing slam, a parry parry (the whole bar).

n19._why: NIGHT19 U3-33.7 (GG 2026-10-06: "maybe it'll use a little bit less stamina ... I like the idea of starting out with less and then you have to get more"; "if you're using controller you should be able to sprint using the left stick when you press it down"): the web has no sprint and no stamina bar, so it has none of these numbers. ownKey gives the sprint its own key (InputFrame.sprint: L3 on the pad, read by the Mover's sprint hook) besides the boost key's hold. drain replaces sprint.drain (0.4 -> 0.3 bar/s: a full bar sprints 3.3 s; the SPRINT DRAIN switch); the kill reward is split by range (Research/2026-10-06-weapon-sandbox.md 24: a kill within nearRange m adds killNear, beyond farRange m killFar, between them rewards.kill); a slam pays only when it hits (slamOnHit). Builder E owns the numbers; off: NIGHT18's stamina. The web has none of these numbers: no falloff (its THUNDERCLAP deals full pellets to 60 m), no shotgun parry, no combos past arsenal.js's CROSS / COLLAPSE / OVERLOAD. shotgun: falloffStart / falloffEnd m and falloffMin: each pellet deals full damage to falloffStart, then linear down to falloffMin x at falloffEnd (point blank, steep: Research 5); parryRange m: a blast at a body in its wind-up within it is a parry (ULTRAKILL's shotgun parry: the punch parry's heal and stamina refill); minCompress: the web's literal 0.25 in weapons.js (the least compress that fires the double blast); coneWavePushTime s: the web's literal 0.25 in weapons.js coneWave (the THUNDERCLAP variant's push). pop: radius m (the sphere around a live rocket or grenade a KESTREL shot must cross; rockets fly 30 m/s, so wider than their 0.2 m body) and mult (POP: x radius and damage, ULTRAKILL's core eject + shot is x2). launch: kinds (the bodies a COMET blast throws up, at the web's momentum.shock.quake.launch 10 m/s) and airshotMult (any hit on a launched body still up: ULTRAKILL's airshot 3.5 -> 7, x2). conductor: radius m, base + perNail x the nails in the body (up to max) dealt to every body in the radius by a ZAPPER or LONGWAVE hit on a nailed body (ULTRAKILL's conductor: 2-6 by 1-90 nails, scaled to SKYGRIND's 9-damage nails). swapCancel: window s (the gun you left fired within it before your swapped-in gun's first hit) and mult (on top of the web's PRIMED +35 %). The web has no segments, no round-end refill and no earned heals but the parry's, so these are Unity-only. Builder E (first pass, 2026-10-06): a punch kill earns punchKillHeal, not both heals; the kill's distance from the player's eye (the stamina rule's); the timers in whole steps. Off: the web's regen (NIGHT19's). Measured STRICT + 1 with BLOOD PRICE's heal off: in-round 0.25, the break's share 67 %; with it on, BLOOD PRICE (the web's mod, +3 per kill per stack) alone is 0.37 of the damage: the lead's call.

slideBites._why: SLIDE BITES (builder M): the slide hits what it passes through. Unity-only: the web's slide never hit anything (Turbo Overkill's slide is the evidence). The five numbers below are Unity-only, each with its why.
slideBites.damage_why: A bite's damage per contact: 22 is a little over half a husk's 40 hp (config husk.hp), so one slide through a husk leaves it staggered and a second kills; a swarmer (10 hp) dies on the first. The web had no slide damage to take it from.
slideBites.radius_why: Metres from the slide's path to the enemy's centre line, on top of the enemy's own radius (a husk 0.4): 0.9 + 0.4 = 1.3 m reach, a body's width either side of the player; under style.closeCallDistance (2 m), so a bite kill is always a close kill.
slideBites.cooldown_why: Seconds before the same enemy can be bitten again: 0.5 keeps one pass to one bite per enemy (a slide is 1-2 s; a 11.6 m/s pass clears an enemy in 0.2 s) while a long slide that circles back bites again.
slideBites.stagger_why: Seconds a surviving enemy stands still after a bite (Enemy.Stun, the punch's staggerTime is 1 s): 0.6, so the bite reads as a trip and the next one lands.
slideBites.points_why: Style points of the named SLIDE BITE bonus per bite: 15, the same as config style.bonus.closeCall, since a bite kill is also paid as a close kill.

stamp._why: THE STAMP (builder S): round grades with a round P on the run P rule's thresholds (design.grade.p), the inked rank stamp, the RESULTS card off POINTS. Unity-only: the web had no round grade (it grades the run: runMoments.js gradeOf). The round's score (Core/Grades21.cs) = damageWeight x (1 - damage taken / (damageFull x max HP)) + rankWeight x (peak style rank / top rank) + timeWeight x the clear's pace (1 at or under the par, 0 at slowMult x par; par = parFlat + parPerKill x the round's kills); the letter is the first of config.results.grade.bands (S .85, A .7, B .55, C .4) it reaches, and a round P is design.grade.p's rule on the round (grade S, peak SS, no revive used). Each number is Unity-only because the web has no round grade.
stamp.damageFull_why: share of max HP at which the damage part reaches 0: a round that took 60 % of max HP scores 0 on damage (ULTRAKILL's level grade counts damage taken the same way; the player's whole bar is 100 HP, health.max)
stamp.parFlat_why: seconds of par before any kill: the walk to the first enemy and the squad's telegraph (the round's break is not counted)
stamp.parPerKill_why: seconds of par per kill: the director's squads spawn on a telegraph and the autopilot clears a round of 9-30 husks in about 25-60 s (NIGHT20's farm); 2.5 s a kill is a clean fast clear
stamp.slowMult_why: the clear's pace reaches 0 at this x the par (3 x: a round cleared at three times par is a slow one)
stamp.inTime_why: UI: the inked stamp's entrance on a round clear, s. NIGHT22: 0.16 -> 0.28 (NIGHT22.md U3-36.4: the entrance is 200-300 ms; M9's own target is 90-300 ms; RESEARCH R1's 400 ms is for a large dialog and small elements take 250 ms, so 0.28 is our tuning). The scale eases out (OutQuad) from fromScale and is within 3 % of rest at 85 % of the time, so M9's settle time reads about 240 ms; the alpha rises over the first half, so nothing shows whole on its first frame
stamp.fromScale_why: UI: the stamp's scale on its first frame (it slams down from 2.4x to 1x; far from rest, so M9 never reads a pop-in)
stamp.holdTime_why: UI: how long the stamp stays after its entrance, s, before it fades (the round's break is 8 s: it is gone before the next round's count)
stamp.outTime_why: UI: the stamp's exit, s (NIGHT22.md U3-36.4: 150-200 ms; RESEARCH R1: exits about 1.5x faster than entrances, small elements leave in 150 ms; 0.18 is our tuning, a fade with a small shrink)
stamp.outScale_why: UI: the stamp's scale at the end of its exit (it shrinks a little as it fades, so it leaves instead of blinking out)

deadline._why: DEADLINE (builder S): a kill-or-die timer twist round (Mullet MadJack). Unity-only: the web had no such twist. A fuse (Core/Deadline21.cs) runs for the round: kills refill it, a slide kill and a slam kill the most; burning out is one heavy hit (never the run: it leaves 1 HP at the least) and a shorter fuse; the round's points double. DEADLINE is one twist among the five of design.adds.twists (the row's draw adds it with its weight; off: NIGHT20's four-twist draw).
deadline.fuse_why: seconds of fuse at the round's start: long enough to find the first squad (a round's first kill comes 8-15 s in), short enough that standing still costs a hit within one wave
deadline.killRefill_why: seconds a plain kill gives back (Mullet MadJack's hourglass: every kill buys time)
deadline.slideRefill_why: seconds a kill made while sliding gives back: the verb the twist asks for (more than a plain kill)
deadline.slamRefill_why: seconds a slam kill gives back, the most: the slam is the costly verb (the airborne dive)
deadline.hitFrac_why: the burn's hit, as a share of max HP: heavy (half the bar) and never the run (the hit stops at 1 HP)
deadline.burnFuse_why: seconds of the fuse after a burn: shorter than the first, so standing still costs again within five seconds (NIGHT21 lead: 10 -> 5 and the first fuse 25 -> 18 s so the KITE at round 10 survives 30.3 s of 63.2 s, 48 %, 10 seeds)
deadline.pointsMult_why: the round's points multiplier (an Economy boost 'twist', as LETHAL's): the reward for playing with a fuse
deadline.weight_why: the twist's weight in the draw (the four others weigh 1): 1, one twist among five, because Mullet MadJack's reviewers name the constant timer as fatiguing
deadline.tickEvery_why: seconds between the fuse's deadlineTick events (the HUD bar reads the share every frame; a tick is for GG's sounds)

grind._why: THE GRIND (builder W): the web's endless mode (src/modes/endless.js; numbers in config.json endless) on SURVIVAL's core. Only Unity-only numbers (the core's reshape presets) are added here.
grind.presets_why: Unity-only: the web's endless left its reshape hook as 'Phase 2' (reshape?: (wave) => seconds, never wired), so it has no list of shapes. These are CoreGrid.PresetHeights' own names (the web's coreGrid.js presets); each wave's reshape draws one on the run's Mulberry32, never the shape the core already wears, so every wave's heights differ. 'flat' is the run's start and is left out.
grind.telegraphTime_why: Unity-only (NIGHT22 U3-36.6; the web's endless left the reshape unwired, so it never warned): the last 2.5 s of the 4 s break show the pillars the next shape will lift as red-orange frames (danger: the floor is about to move under you), and the marks stay through the 1.5 s reshape. ULTRAKILL's Cyber Grind announces what comes before it spawns (RESEARCH.md R6); 2.5 s is long enough to move to a pillar that stays down, short enough that the break still reads as a rest.

challenge._why: CHALLENGE CODES (builder W2, U3-35.9 beyond row 5): one short code on TITLE and RESULTS that holds a run's seed, HEAT rung, mutator set, mode and target round; pasting it plays the same run (Core/Challenge21.cs). Unity-only: the web had a bare seed code (seeds.js seedCode) and nothing else. The code is the fields packed into bits, a checksum over them, and the whole written in an alphabet of 5 bits a character.
challenge.alphabet_why: Unity-only: 32 characters, 5 bits each, with the look-alikes left out (no I, L, O, U): 0 and 1 stand for O and I / L when a code is typed by hand, and U is left out so a code never spells a word by accident.
challenge.length_why: Unity-only: 12 characters = 60 bits, the room the fields need (seedBits 31 + heatBits 4 + mutatorBits 4 + modeBits 2 + targetBits 7 = 48, plus checkBits 10 = 58) with 2 spare bits that must read 0; shown as three groups of four (XXXX-XXXX-XXXX) so it can be read aloud.
challenge.checkBits_why: Unity-only: 10 bits of checksum: a mistyped or guessed code passes by chance 1 in 1024.
challenge.seedBits_why: Unity-only: the game's seeds are 0..2^31-1 (main.js startSurvival, Seeds.Max), so 31 bits hold every seed.
challenge.heatBits_why: Unity-only: the HEAT rung 0..15 (the ladder has far fewer rungs, heat.rungs).
challenge.targetBits_why: Unity-only: the target round 0..127 (0: no target); the ladder's best rounds sit well under it.
challenge.groupSize_why: Unity-only: the characters shown in a group, a hyphen between groups (UI only; a typed code may have any hyphens or spaces).

n22._why: NIGHT22 U3-36 (GG 2026-10-07: 'Prioritize building an iteration polishing accuracy all of.'): the six sim-visible NIGHT22 rows, one block each (design.n22.<row>.enabled), all off in the shared commit; a row is turned on only when its contract passes. Off (--off22 / -skygrindOff22): NIGHT21's game bit for bit. The NIGHT21 rows' fixes keep design.n21.*; Unity-only numbers live here with a why.

duskClock._why: THE DUSK CLOCK (the lead; W2 never launched): the sky sinks per round toward violet and cyan by round 15, never magenta or red-orange (rule 8). Render-side only, shipped materials only. Unity-only: the web's sky was fixed. The four colours are the round-15 sky as web-style 0xRRGGBB numbers: a deep violet-blue zenith, a blue-violet mid, a violet horizon (the dusk's orange glow gone) and a violet-grey fog; none is within 40 of (255, 0, 255) and none is red-orange.
duskClock.lastRound_why: Unity-only: the share reaches 1 at round 15 (NIGHT22.md: 'by round 15'); round 1 is the dusk as shipped (share 0).
duskClock.easeSeconds_why: Unity-only: the sky moves to the new round's share over 3 s of frame time, so a round change is a drift and not a snap (the HUNT's shift takes 2.5 s).
duskClock.lightScale_why: Unity-only: at round 15 the key light is 55 % of its shipped intensity. The first Player reels (n22-1 .. n22-3) showed the sky dome is only a dark strip between this map's walls, so recolouring it moved the frame's mean luminance by 0.2 of 255; the light is what the player sees fall.
duskClock.ambientScale_why: Unity-only: at round 15 the hemisphere (ambient) light is 60 % of its shipped value, so the shadows deepen with the key light. Same measured reason as lightScale.

haptics._why: HAPTICS (builder M): distinct pad patterns for the shockwave, ARCLINE attach and yank, kills and DOWN on the existing Rumble; VIBRATION off silences all. Unity-only: the web rumbled only on hurt / kill / parry (config.json gamepad.vibration).

patterns._why: Each pattern is a list of [strong, weak, ms] steps (flat triples): strong is the low-frequency motor, weak the high-frequency one, 0..1 before the RUMBLE strength; a step of 0, 0 is a pause. Unity-only: the web had one pulse per event. Values are by feel and are not measured on a pad; they are distinct from each other and from the web's hurt [0.3, 0.5, 90], kill [0, 0.25, 45], parry [0.45, 0.2, 70].
patterns.shockwave_why: The THUNDERCLAP's blast: a heavy boom that decays (strong first, weak fading), the longest of the combat patterns so it reads as the player's own big move.
patterns.attach_why: The rope biting: a sharp high-frequency tick, a gap, then a short body thump, so it reads as 'caught' and not as a hit taken.
patterns.yank_why: The ARCLINE's yank (arclinePull): a quick pull then a snap, between the attach tick and the shockwave in weight.
patterns.kill_why: A kill: shorter and brighter than the web's kill pulse [0, 0.25, 45] so a crowd's kills do not smear into one buzz; weak motor only.
patterns.down_why: DOWN: the longest and heaviest pattern, two thumps and a long fade, the only one over a second in all.

directed._why: DIRECTED STEPS (leftover 1, builder M): THE HUNT / THE BEACON show a step list (the beacon's with its spot's distance and side). RENDER SIDE ONLY (Core/Directed22.cs listens to the bus; Game/UiDirected22.cs draws it in cyan, never red): no sim change, no fingerprint re-record, N22OnPath stays false. Unity-only: the web had no step list. Its distances use perks.reach and design.adds.hunt.ringMin/ringMax, no new number.

trickChain._why: TRICK CHAIN (leftover 4, builder M): distinct movement tricks inside a chaining window pay a rising style bonus. The smallest blast radius: it adds one named style bonus (the existing styleBonus event, as SLIDE BITE does) per new distinct trick; no points rule, no Mover change, no random draw; every handler returns at once with the row off. A sim change when on (so the tape's n22 bit 2 records it). Unity-only: the web's tricks each paid alone.
trickChain.window_why: Seconds after the last NEW trick (the web's style.trickRepeatWindow is also 3) in which the next distinct trick still chains. 3 s: a slide into a hop into a slam fits (about 1 s each) and a landing and a look round does not. Tuned by feel, not measured on a player.
trickChain.basePoints_why: The style points the SECOND trick of a chain pays (the first pays only its own trick award). 10 is the size of the wallJump and dashJump awards in config style.tricks (5 to 15), so a chain link pays about one more trick. Style points are then scaled by the meter's own rank rules like any bonus.
trickChain.rise_why: Each further distinct trick pays basePoints x (1 + rise x (n - 2)): the multiplier rises by this much per link (0.5: x1, x1.5, x2 ...). Tuned by feel.
trickChain.maxLinks_why: The chain stops rising at this many distinct tricks (a cap, so a long run of tricks cannot pay without limit). About eight distinct trick names exist (the style.tricks keys, slam, a rope swing), so 6 is most of them.

overdrive._why: OVERDRIVE (leftover 5, after TRICK CHAIN): a charged state fed by the chain. A sim change. Unity-only.

n24._why: NIGHT24 U3-38 (GG 2026-10-08: the linear turn, 'a linear boomer shooter ... focus on the boss fights'): the nine NIGHT24 rows, one block each (design.n24.<row>.enabled), all off in the shared commit; a row is turned on only when its contract passes. Off (--off24 / -skygrindOff24): NIGHT22's game bit for bit. Unity-only numbers live in each row with a _why.

padY._why: Pad layout v4 (builder R, GG 2026-10-08: 'the Y ... should also be able to switch weapons'): Y (tap) = NEXT WEAPON, a hold on Y opens the weapon wheel, RB = SPECIAL + ARCLINE (the v2 default); RB's old scroll is dropped. Input layer only: no sim change. Unity-only: the web had no pad.

shotgunTune._why: THE SHOTGUN's slower fire interval (builder R, GG: 'the shotgun is not balanced it just fires a little too fast'): the THUNDERCLAP's interval grows by the measured default +30 %. A sim change when on (fingerprint path). Unity-only tuning of a web number; the web value stays in PortExport/config.json.
shotgunTune.intervalMult_why: Unity-only (NIGHT24 DECIDE D-8; the web has one fixed 0.9 s): the THUNDERCLAP's shot-to-shot time is multiplied by this. Measured today: 0.408 s (49 steps at 120 Hz), because NIGHT20's retune (design.arsenal.n20.tune.shotgun interval x0.45) shortened the web's 0.9 s; x1.30 makes it 0.525 s (63 steps, now longer than the 0.45 s viewmodel pump), still faster than Dusk and ULTRAKILL (0.9 s; RESEARCH S1-S7).
shotgunTune.damageMult_why: Unity-only: the pellets' damage is scaled by the same 1.30 so the damage per second is unchanged (slower, not weaker: GG said it fires too fast, not that it hits too hard); applied once to the summed pellets of a shot in Loadout.Damage.

bigPick._why: The BIG PICK (builder F, GG: 'sparing ... every five or 10 rounds ... a big buck ... a free mystery box spin or 1000 points'): SURVIVAL offers 2 or 3 big cards every 5 rounds, no reroll, no percentage cards; the old modDraft pool is kept behind design.mods.legacy (off). A sim change when on. Unity-only: the web's draft was small percentages. Numbers: firstRound / every = the rounds whose clear opens a pick (5, 10, 15 ...: 'every five or 10 rounds', D-7); cards = 3 per pick (D-7: 2 or 3); defaultCard / defaultSeconds = the card taken when nobody presses (the contract: a default pick after 6 s); points = the +POINTS card (GG: 'a big buck ... 1000 points'); multRounds / multValues = x2 from round 10, x3 from round 20 (the contract); armorSeconds = the shield FULL HEAL + ARMOR grants from the next round's start (the port has no armor plates: a timed shield is its armor); campaign = the CAMPAIGN gets one BIG PICK at each layer's end (D-7), none by round; seedSalt = XORed with the run seed for the card shuffle; legacy = the old percentage draft on (design.mods.legacy is read too; the web had no such switch).

chargeFist._why: The hit-fed charged fist (builder F, GG: 'charge it up by hitting enemies over time ... flick air kind of movement boost ... only how many enemies you hit or kill'): kills and hits fill a charge, never time; a tier-1 flick costs a third of it, a full flick all of it. A sim change when on. The flick is an impulse through the existing API; Mover.cs is untouched. Unity-only (the web had no charge). Numbers: gain.* = charge per fist hit / fist kill / other-weapon kill (R3 section C2 start 0.02 / 0.08 / 0.03, retuned by the harness `fist` so a fist-only bot needs 25-35 kills to FULL, D-6); tiers = the three notches (D-6); jumpMult = the flick's reach in jump distances (R3 C6: 0.5 / 1.0 / 2.0-2.5); jumpDistance = J, the horizontal reach of a jump measured on the Mover by the harness `fist` (it fails if this drifts from the measurement); speed = the impulse in m/s at each notch (tuned by the harness `fist` so the measured ground reach meets jumpMult x J; a flick the collider cuts is slower in proportion); hurtLoss = the share of the charge a hit on you takes (a third, D-6); lockout = s after a flick before the next (D-13: only against a double punch, the charge is the long cooldown); wallMargin = m kept clear of a wall by the collider cap; minRoom = m of room below which an aimed-into-a-wall flick does not happen and spends nothing; bodyHeight = m above the feet the cap's ray starts from.

reticleArc._why: The cooldown arc under the reticle (builder F, GG: 'a little bar or like a curved bar ... should not be in the way'): about 5 px thin, 15-25 % alpha at rest, in the central 40 % as the one allowed element. View only: no sim change.

links._why: The campaign's traversal links (builder L): reach = metres (horizontal and vertical) at which a link's exit counts as reached and clears the room. Was typed in Campaign24.cs (rule 5); the web has no campaign.

campaign._why: MODE: CAMPAIGN (builder L, GG: 'a linear boomer shooter ... focus on the boss fights similar to ULTRAKILL'): layer 1 = rooms with locked doors, encounters, checkpoints, LIMIT rooms and a boss room, built from a plan file (Design/levels). Changes only the campaign mode's run; SURVIVAL and THE GRIND are unchanged. Unity-only: the web has no campaign. retryDelay: s of game time from a death to the room restarting (the contract says within 1.5 s; health.downTime is 1.5, so the restart beats the DOWN screen); waveGap: s between a wave's last death and the next wave (a breath, so a room reads as waves); minSpawnDist: m, an enemy never appears closer to the player than this at its room's nodes (the last node tried ignores it); limitBonus: style points a cleared LIMIT room pays (about one rank-up of the meter, GG: a limit is a challenge worth paying for); parMultiple: the bot's clear budget is this x a room's par (the contract's 4x).

limitFlags._why: The extra LIMIT flags (builder R, NIGHT24 leftover 1; GG: 'a few arenas that LIMIT your weapons or movement'): a room's limit list may also name noSlide, noJump (one key each stripped from the input frame, Limit24.Strip) and meleeOnly (the gauntlet alone, as pistolOnly keeps the KESTREL alone). Off: those three names are masked away when a room is entered, leaving pistolOnly / noDash as built first. Unity-only: the web has no rooms.

rank._why: Room ranks (builder R, NIGHT24 leftover 2; DESIGN-PILLARS 3 every run is readable, ULTRAKILL's S-ranks): each cleared room gets S / A / B / C by its time over its par (Campaign24.RankOf), each death in the room drops deathDrop letters (never below C); the layer's closing stamp text lists the letters and the overall rank. Numbers are Unity-only: the web has no campaign. Off: no ranks, no stamp text.
rank.sShare_why: Unity-only: a room cleared within its par is an S (par is the designer's clean-run time; the bot's gate is 4 x par).
rank.aShare_why: Unity-only: up to 1.5 x par is an A.
rank.bShare_why: Unity-only: up to 2.5 x par is a B; slower is a C.
rank.deathDrop_why: Unity-only: each death in the room costs one letter (a clear after two deaths cannot beat a B).

directed._why: The campaign's door cue and room banner (builder F, leftover 4): hideWithin = m from the room's exit at which the DOOR OPEN cue hides (the door is in reach); bannerSeconds = s the 'ROOM 2 - NO DASH' banner stays after a LIMIT room starts. View only, behind the campaign block (and so --off24). Unity-only.

wyrm._why: The WYRM, layer 1's boss (builder B, GG: 'a crazy worm boss ... slithers really easy though and is really fast'): a segmented serpent tested by oriented-box rays; contact damage and knockback from piece boxes; no collider change. Changes only the boss room. Unity-only.

body._why: DESIGN24-bosses.md section 1: 24 body boxes + head + tail on a head-position ring buffer (piece i reads i x spacingSteps back); spacingSteps 13 is 2.4 m at the base 22 m/s (a box is as long as the gap to its neighbour, so a lunge stretches it and never leaves a hole). Head 3 x 3 x 4 m, body 2.5 m tapering to 1.2 m. The web has no worm.

hp._why: One shared pool (the Destroyer rule: no shot is wasted): body x1, head x2, exposed core x3. The pool is sized so a bot that shoots the revolver (25 per 0.4 s) at the harness's reaction and aim limits kills it in about 4 minutes of game time; a human target is 2.5 to 3.5 min (DESIGN24 section 1). Phases at 66 % and 33 %.

speed._why: Base 22 m/s (the player's sprint is about 9 m/s, boosted movement 20 to 35 m/s: really fast, but a master can ride it), +25 % in phase 2 and again in phase 3 (the Wall of Flesh ramp). The lunge pass runs lungeMult x faster than the phase speed; the dive's underground leg is a path of fixed length, so its hidden time shrinks with the phase.

contact._why: Never cheap: body contact hurts little, head contact hurts, the lunge head hurts most. Player health is 100. The cooldown (0.8 s) stops a worm that sweeps over you from draining you in a few steps; the push throws you clear of the box (the boxes are not solid to the player: a contact is damage plus a push). Radius = the player's capsule (body.capsuleRadius 0.35).

tells._why: Every attack has a tell of 0.5 s or more and no two resolve inside resolveGap (0.5 s): the lunge's line shows lunge s ahead, the dive's marked wall spot and floor crack show dive s ahead (1 s or more: GG's 'marked'), the spit's body ports glow spit s ahead, the core's roar shows core s ahead.

spit._why: Phase 2 and 3 spit barrage from body ports (a spiral by the golden angle, every 10th aimed at you): count projectiles per volley, one volley every every2 / every3 s while the worm coils or loops (never during a lunge or a dive).

shards._why: Terrain-cross shards: 5 shards burst inward from the wall spot when the head erupts from the wall.

core._why: The core exposes on the head after a roar tell, from phase 2: it opens for open s every every s (phase 2) / every3 s (phase 3, longer). A hit on the core is x3. The core sits on the head's back, radius r, offset (0, up, back) from the head centre.

intro._why: The worm rises from a floor hole (the emerge pattern); it takes no damage and does no contact harm until it is out and the first coil starts. spawnClear is the DESIGN24 floor: it never comes within 6 m of the player spawn.

tailShed._why: Leftover 6, the tail-shed sub-boss (DESIGN24 section 1, 'skip if late'): at the 66 % and 33 % beats the last pieces cut loose and stay where they fell as a target with their own HP; shoot it down before it regrows (regrow s) and the worm loses those pieces for good and takes bonus (a share of its max HP) as a bonus. Off by default (enabled): a sim change in the boss fight only. The web has no worm.

marks._why: The marked spots and flashes (rule 5: the numbers the fight shows, none typed in Wyrm.cs): crackR / exitR the floor circles' radii (m), exitOffset how far in front of the wall the eruption's circle sits, lungeWidth the lunge line's width, crackHold / lungeHold how long the view keeps a marker after its event (s), flash / volleyFlash the white flashes' radii. The web has no worm.

room._why: Where layer 1 (and the reel) puts the worm's room in the world: far from the SURVIVAL map so the two never overlap (Unity-only, the web had no worm); salt xors the run seed for the worm's stream, as design.adds.bulwark.salt does.

monolith._why: MONOLITH through BossKit, first slice (builder B, NIGHT24 leftover 8; MONOLITH-PORT-PLAN.md): the web's boss (config.boss: every gameplay number is the web's, read from PortExport) as a standalone arena fight, no Grinder reshape, adds or floor sink yet. Read directly (no N24Blocks bit; gated by --off24) so a later layer 2 can switch it. salt xors the run seed for the boss's action stream (the web draws Math.random). Unity-only.

room._why: Where the reel puts MONOLITH's room in the world: far from the SURVIVAL map and from the worm's room (x 400). Unity-only.

lighting._why: The room lighting kit (builder L, GG: 'better lighting'): a room accent colour and a guide light on the way to the exit; shipped materials only; dusk palette (cyan player-usable, red-orange danger only). View only. Unity-only; art polish comes later (GG). Numbers (all Unity-only, the web had no rooms): accents = the rooms' trim colours in order, repeating (cyan 0x36e0ff, mint 0x58f0b8, blue 0x5aa0ff: cool and player-side only, no red-orange, no magenta); trim = the emissive strip along a room's floor edge (width, height, inset in m, brightness = the neon material's HDR multiplier); roomLight = one soft point light at the room's middle in its accent (intensity, range m, height m) so a closed room reads as lit, not black; guide = one point light that stands at the exit of the room you are in and pulses (intensity, range m, height m, pulse Hz) toward the way on, cyan because it is the way you can use.

prewarm._why: The boot prewarm pass (the lead, GG: 'I don't understand why it's so laggy switching'): a hidden pass at boot (Canvas.ForceUpdateCanvases, TMP glyphs, shader first use) so the first switch does not hitch. View only. Unity-only; measured by the hitch tour. Numbers (builder F): glyphs = the characters added to every theme font (printable ASCII plus the middle dot and the multiplication sign the UI uses); screenFrames = frames each big screen stays awake at alpha 0 so its layout and TMP meshes build (2 is one build and one settle); shaderWarmup = also call Shader.WarmupAllShaders (a first-use compile, a one-off cost at boot).

n25._why: NIGHT25 U3-39 (GG 2026-10-08: the teaching campaign, melee while firing, the PULSE, no shotgun shockwave, the worm aimed at the player): the six NIGHT25 rows, one block each (design.n25.<row>.enabled), all off in the shared commit; a row is turned on only when its contract passes. Off (--off25 / -skygrindOff25): NIGHT24's game bit for bit. Unity-only numbers live in each row with a _why.

hitchFix._why: The first PLAY of a session hitched 250 ms (GG: 'I don't understand why it's so laggy switching'). Player build n25-3 marks (Hitch24.Mark in StartRun): N20StartRun +138 ms cold, ~0 warm: the route layer (RouteLayer.Build over the nav grid) was built on the first run start. With this on, SurvivalSim.PrebuildRoutes25 builds the same layer at boot, and the first run start takes it when the map and grid are the same ones (else it builds as before). Unity-only: the web has no such layer. No sim state changes (the fingerprint and the state hash are pinned by tests).
hitchFix.hud_why: Player build n25-6: the first PLAY frame was 247.8 ms and R.Ui was 173.4 ms of it (the HUD layers are inactive on TITLE, so the first PLAY built every HUD text mesh, layout and glyph at once). With hud on, a boot pass (Prewarm25) adds the UI glyphs to the theme fonts and wakes the HUD layers, the lesson line and the menu screens at alpha 0 for `frames` frames while TITLE shows. View only; the sim is untouched.

meleeFire._why: The quick melee and the gun's fire in the same frame (builder C, GG 2026-10-08: 'if you're shooting a weapon and you're trying to melee you can't do both at the same time it's either one action or the other'): the web serialises them (punch.js / weapons.js); with the row on a punch neither waits for nor cancels the gun's cycle, and the reverse. Off (--off25): NIGHT24's serialised rules.
meleeFire.padPunch_why: The cause GG felt (found reading CombatInput -> sim step -> view; Core and the keyboard / mouse reader already run fire and punch together, the harness `meleefire` proves it): on the pad PUNCH sat on R3, the click of the aiming stick, so a pad player could not hold the trigger, aim and punch. With the row on the pad layout is v5: PUNCH on RB (the right index finger rolls RT -> RB, both thumbs stay on the sticks), SPECIAL + ARCLINE on R3 (design.pad ARCLINE TOGGLE makes it a click). v4 -> v5 migrates once; a customised RB / R3 is kept.

pulseCharge._why: The PULSE GAUNTLET's left click builds power by its own hits and launches the player with a little damage (builder C, GG: 'the pulse is the weapon that should have the actual pulse for the left click that's built based off of how many times you use it'). Numbers (hits per tier, the launch distances, the damage) are added by builder C under this row, each with a _why. Off (--off25): NIGHT24's fist-charge rules.

gain._why: Charge per landed PULSE swing (builder C). Fixed from the harness `pulse`: the notches are design.n24.chargeFist.tiers (0.33 / 0.66 / 1.0), so 0.048 gives 7 / 14 / 21 hits to the three notches (about 3 s of continuous swinging per notch at the gauntlet's 0.42 s cycle). The web has no charge. No kill and no other gun feeds it; time never does.

pulseCharge.damageMult_why: The launch's damage as a share of the gauntlet's swing (weapons.gauntlet.damage 32): 8 / 16 / 32 at the three notches, once per body in the path. GG: 'launch you but also do a little bit of damage'. The distances (0.5 / 1.0 / 2.25 jumps), the impulse speeds, the 3 s lockout, the one air flick and the third lost when hit are design.n24.chargeFist's rows, reused unchanged.
pulseCharge.radius_why: m from the aim line within which a body is hit by the launch (a body's own radius is added): about a husk's width and a half, so a launch into a crowd hits those it passes. Unity-only.

shockwaveOff._why: No shockwave on the shotgun (builder C, GG: 'remove that shockwave effect from the shotgun should not be like that'): the THUNDERCLAP's LT shove (Core/Guns/Shockwave.cs, NIGHT19) is removed; its LT zooms (GG: most weapons zoom). Off (--off25): NIGHT24's shotgun with the shockwave.
shockwaveOff.zoom_why: The THUNDERCLAP's LT zoom (GG's rule 'most weapons zoom: simple zoom'): the same 1.25 x as the STITCHER's (design.zoom.nailgunMag), FOV 62.2 deg. The design.shockwave rows stay in the file but are inert with this row on (Loadout.ShockwaveOn is false, NIGHT19's compress is skipped).

wyrmAim._why: The worm aims at the player and fights a little harder (builder W, GG: 'make it a little more difficult and make sure it's like obviously targeted towards you'): spit leads the target, the lunge locks at its tell and re-aims once, 10-15 % less breathing room per phase, phase 3 overlaps compatible attacks; every tell stays >= 0.5 s. Numbers are added by builder W under this row, each with a _why. Off (--off25): NIGHT24's worm.

spit._why: Spit aimed at WHERE YOU WILL BE (RESEARCH.md S4 move 1; Cuphead-style fairness: the tell is unchanged, the aim is not wasted): every aimedEvery-th spit (NIGHT24: every 10th, at your chest as you stood) now leads your ground velocity over its flight time, capped at leadMax seconds of lead (a long flight is not a prophecy); velMax m/s: a faster measured speed is a teleport (a respawn) and is read as 0. Web has no worm. Unity-only.
