lunge._why: The lunge line locks onto YOU at the tell's start (the head's path is rebuilt through a spot on the line from the lunge's start toward where you stood, the NIGHT24 length kept, cut where it would pass clamp metres short of a wall) and re-aims ONCE at the lunge's midpoint, turning at most reaimMaxDeg toward you (a read-able correction, not a homing missile; the drawn line does not move). Every tell keeps its NIGHT24 seconds (>= 0.5 s). Unity-only.

gapCut._why: 10-15 % less breathing room per phase (RESEARCH.md S4 move 3): the head's speed is raised by 1/(1-cut) in each phase, so the TIME between attacks shrinks by cut while every tell keeps its seconds (a tell is drawn from distance / speed and the distance scales with speed), and the spit's interval shrinks by cut too. p1 / p2 / p3 = 0.10 / 0.125 / 0.15.

overlap._why: Phase 3 overlaps two compatible attacks (RESEARCH.md S4 move 4): the spit barrage (small hits) also runs during the dive and the lunge patterns, so its tell overlaps theirs. Never two lethal ones: the lunge, the dive's eruption and the squeeze keep resolveGap (0.5 s) either side of each other AND of every volley (the NIGHT24 gate is untouched). Same attack count (47). p3: true turns it on.

hp._why: Kill-time target for the composed human bot 3:30-4:30 (NIGHT25.md; NIGHT24: 3:01 mean): the pool is multiplied by mult so the fight is longer, not the attacks (the attack count stays 47). Set from the composed sim's printed mean, see WYRM-AIM in the commit message.

room._why: GG's 'the arena is bugged out' (WYRM-TRIAGE.md): the worm's room (Design/maps/wyrm-arena.json at design.n24.wyrm.room.origin) was collision only, so a human in THE FURNACE stood over an empty sky. The view now draws its boxes (the map's stone colours) and lights it; a VIEW fix, always on (not behind the enabled flag: nothing on the sim path changes). Unity-only numbers (the web had no worm): lightHeight m above the room's floor, lightRange m (the room is 60 m across, 30 m high), lightIntensity (before the project's 1/pi light scale; CampaignLighting24's room light is 6 at range 38), lightColor 0xcfc6ff the pale violet-white boundary tone (rule 8: not red-orange, which is danger only).

tutorial._why: Layer 1 as a six-stage TUTORIAL (builder L, GG: 'it should really be a tutorial for this first map and don't be afraid to break it up into stages'): look and walk, jump and slide, wall and air, the pistol, the fist, a first fight; each stage is Exposition / Validation / Challenge (RESEARCH.md S2), a respawn at the stage's start, no fail state. Off (--off25): NIGHT24's layer 1.

bosses._why: Generic campaign boss rooms (builder W, NIGHT25: levels 6 and 9 need bosses): a plan room with `boss: "wyrm" | "bulwark" | "monolith"` fights that boss in its own room far from the map (Campaign24 world hook BeginBoss(id) / BossIsDefeated(id); SurvivalSim.Boss25.cs). enabled turns the BULWARK and MONOLITH rooms on (the worm's room stays behind design.n24.wyrm) AND the phase-start retry for them: a player death inside the room restores the boss to the START of its current phase (HP at the threshold, the same seed stream), as the worm's retry does under design.n25.wyrmAim. Read directly (no N25Blocks bit; --off25 / --off24 turn it off). Default off: the lead flips it.

bulwark._why: THE BULWARK's boss room (Core/Enemies/Bulwark.cs, every fight number is the web's from PortExport bulwark.* through design.adds.bulwark): arena = Design/maps/bulwark-arena.json (44 m across inside, 20 m high: bulwark.arenaHalf 18 + 4 m), origin = where the room sits in the world (far from the map, the worm's room at x 400 and MONOLITH's at x -400), salt xors the run seed for its action stream (design.adds.bulwark.salt does so in SURVIVAL), no hatch adds in a room (the husks cannot walk an off-map room). Unity-only: the web had no BULWARK room.

final._why: THE FINAL BOSS = THE ELDER KILN WYRM (builder W, NIGHT25 level 10; GG: 'a difficulty spike': the worm's big brother): the SAME Core/Enemies/Wyrm.cs as a harder variant selected by a plan room's `boss: "final"`. Every number is a multiple of (or replaces) the worm's design.n24.wyrm row, TUNED so the human-lag bot (WyrmBot, composed sim) kills it in 5:00-6:30 (`wyrm25 --final`: 4:54 / 6:14 / 5:23, 1-2 deaths; the lead's first guess x2 HP and x1.25 speed killed the bot 0 of 3 in 14 min): hpMult x1.2 on the pool, speedMult x1.0 on the base speed, phaseMult 1.12 (the worm: 1.25; each of the FOUR phases is only 12 % faster than the last), spitDamageMult x0.5 (the aimed spit and the lunge lock already spike the fight), the tail-shed on (design.n24.wyrm.tailShed's numbers: it cuts loose at each beat), FOUR phases at phases = [0.75, 0.5, 0.25] of the HP (the worm: 0.66, 0.33; phase 4 runs as phase 3 with the speed x phaseMult once more), a fifth pattern SPIRAL in paths (Design/bosses/wyrm-final.json: wyrm.json x1.25 plus the helix), its own arena (Design/maps/wyrm-final-arena.json: wyrm-arena x1.25: 75 m across, 4 pillars, 3 platforms) at room.origin (x 1200), name 'ELDER WYRM' on the bar and its pips (one per phase still to come). Every tell keeps its seconds (>= 0.5 s) and no two lethal attacks resolve inside resolveGap (0.5 s): the NIGHT24 gates are untouched; the aimed pass (design.n25.wyrmAim: lead, lunge lock, gap cut, phase-3 overlap) applies when it is on. Needs design.n25.bosses.enabled. Unity-only: the web had no worm.
final.name: ELDER WYRM

rival._why: RIVAL PRIME, the V2-style duel (builder W, DESIGN24-bosses.md section 3; GG: 'I wanted to feel like V2 where it is a difficulty spike'), behind its OWN switch (enabled, default off; it also needs design.n25.bosses.enabled). A plan room with `boss: "rival"` fights it alone in Design/maps/rival-arena.json (52 m, four cover pillars) at room.origin (x 1600), salt xors the run seed. The web's numbers are PortExport rivalPrime.* (hp 3000, p2At 0.5, copyMult 1.15, actionEvery, the dash / volley numbers, the weights); the rows below are the port's own (the web fired its guns with no tell and had a 0.45 s shape): name = the bar and the intro card; minTell 0.5 s = no tell is shorter (the web's shapeTime 0.45 is raised to dash.tell / volley.tell / burst.tell, all >= minTell); dash {tell s, push m/s: the strike's shove}; volley {tell, damage per orb, life s, radius m}; burst {tell, shots per burst, interval s, damage per shot (the hitscan along its aim), range m, cooldown s after the burst}; p2Cadence x0.8 on the gap between actions in phase 2; headRadius m of its head sphere; killTime s of the finisher; hpMult x on the web's 3000; spawn = its start (x, z) in the room. Unity-only: the web's rival had no room of this kind.
rival.name: RIVAL PRIME

monolith._why: MONOLITH's boss room: the first slice (Core/Enemies/Monolith.cs, design.n24.monolith: arena Design/maps/monolith-arena.json at design.n24.monolith.room.origin x -400, salt design.n24.monolith.salt) fought from a campaign boss room. Only the room's light is new (Unity-only; the room is 52 m across, 16 m high): lightHeight m above the floor, lightRange m, lightIntensity before the 1/pi light scale, lightColor 0xcfc6ff (the pale violet-white boundary tone: not red-orange, which is danger only).

curriculum._why: Levels 2-10 as plan files that each teach one new thing (builder L, GG: 'I'd like this to have 10 levels and they should all build up to each other'): the table is Design/levels/CURRICULUM.md. order = the CAMPAIGN's play order by level id (Core/Curriculum25.cs): the tutorial (needs design.n25.tutorial), layer1 = level 2 THE KILN (the id stays layer1 so NIGHT24's tests and tapes keep working), level3 ... level10 (need this block); a level whose block is off is skipped, so with both blocks off the CAMPAIGN is NIGHT24's layer 1. Off (--off25): only NIGHT24's layer 1.

lesson._why: The tutorial's lesson rule (builder L, Core/Lesson25.cs; Unity-only: the web has no tutorial). punchFireSteps = fixed steps (120 Hz) within which a landed punch and a shot count as 'together' for the punchWhileFiring lesson (GG: 'shooting a weapon and ... melee ... both at the same time'): 30 steps is a quarter second, about one gun cycle of the KESTREL, so a player who fires and punches in the same breath clears it and one who alternates slowly does not.
lesson.maxTopUps_why: The most times a room respawns its last wave because a lesson that needs an enemy (targets hit, husks dead, a punch while firing, the charged flick) is not done and the enemies are dead (builder L, a guard: the tutorial's stage 1.5 took 1-2 top-ups on the bot, and a human who never lands the lesson would otherwise get waves for ever). After this many the pending enemy lessons are passed over and the room clears on its waves (the event lessonTopUpCap). 12 is about three minutes of husks at the waveGap; tutorial.plan.json asks for at most 3 hits-worth of enemies.

bosses._why: NIGHT26 builder B: the three new boss rows (GG 2026-10-08: the worm is too hard for a first boss, so an easy one first; a chase boss on ice at level 2; the worm at level 3). Every number is Unity-only (the web had no hulk, no glacier and no proximity aggro), each group has its _why. Applied by Tools/night/n26b-config.py.

hulk._why: THE SLAG HULK (builder B, contract hulk; Core/Enemies/Hulk26.cs, Design/bosses/hulk.json, Design/maps/hulk-arena.json): level 1's EASY boss. enabled gates the room (boss key hulk), the rest of the groups are numbers. room.origin is where its room sits in the world (the worm is at x 400, MONOLITH -400, the BULWARK 800, the ELDER WYRM 1200); salt xors the run seed.
hulk.name: SLAG HULK

room._why: Where the room sits and its one light, in the pale violet-white boundary tone (rule 8): a smaller room than the worm's, so a nearer, dimmer light.

hp._why: GG: an easier boss first. 1500 HP in one shared pool (the contract), phases at 66 and 33 % (the worm's marks), back and head x2 (GG's Terraria rule: weak points pay), body x1; shellFront 0.4: the SLAG SHELL, a body hit from any side while it is not stunned lands x0.2 (the head and the back plate are never shelled: circle behind it or wait for the stun; the bot's kill time needs it, the pistol alone does 62 damage a second); guardHead 0.5: its arms are up while it walks, so a head hit then lands x1 (the head is x2 again the moment it slams, charges, recovers or is stunned: shoot it when it attacks). Both are needed because the pistol alone does 62 damage a second: with the contract's 1500 HP and the plain x2 / x1 the human-lag bot killed it in 36 s, the contract wants 60-90 s; stunMult 1 (the stun already drops the shell and the guard: that is the payoff for dodging the charge) (the stunned hulk is hittable x1 everywhere).

move._why: Slow on purpose (the sprint is about 9 m/s, the hulk walks 3.2): you can always walk away from it. phaseMult 1.2 per phase speeds the walk, the turn, the ring and the charge. turnRate 2.2 rad/s: it turns slowly enough that circling it keeps you behind it (the back plate is a weak point). standoff 3 m: it stops walking this close.

slam._why: ONE telegraphed slam (contract): tell 0.8 s (a circle at its feet of tellRadius 3.5 m), then a shockwave ring runs out at 9 m/s to 16 m, 1.4 m thick and 1 m tall: JUMP it (a standing player is hit; a jump apex is above 1 m). damage 18 of the player's 100, recover 1.4 s. It only slams when you are within range 10 m (else it walks closer). In phase 3 a second ring follows 0.9 s behind (ring2Delay: two jumps, never two hits inside 0.5 s).

charge._why: ONE telegraphed charge (contract): tell 0.8 s, a line (width 3 m) to the wall or pillar it will hit, LOCKED when the tell starts (sidestep it), then 15 m/s in a straight line; it stops at the wall, stunned for 2 s (the contract), then recovers 1 s. A hit does 22 and throws you sideways (push 10). maxLength 30 m (longer than the room: the wall always stops it).

cycle._why: Slam, charge, slam, charge, with a walk between: the seconds of walking before the next attack in phase 1, 2 and 3 (shorter as it angers). Nothing resolves inside tells.resolveGap (0.5 s) of the last attack: the walk is never shorter than that and the cycle holds the next tell until it has passed.

tells._why: The night's rule: every tell >= 0.5 s and no two lethal attacks resolve inside resolveGap (the worm's 0.5 s). The slam and the charge tell 0.8 s (the contract's floor).

contact._why: Touching it hurts a little (8 of 100) with a 1 s cooldown, so standing in its legs is a mistake but not a death; the push throws you clear (the boxes are not solid to the player: damage plus a push, as the worm's).

body._why: footRadius 1.4 m: the circle the walk and the charge keep off walls and pillars (the torso is 2.6 m wide). dieTime 2.5 s: the finisher before bossDown. spawnZ -6: where it stands in the room (arena-local z, the player enters at z +10 facing it).

glacier._why: THE GLACIER (builder B, contract glacier; Core/Enemies/Glacier26.cs, Design/maps/glacier-course.json; GG: 'speed skating to get this boss ... dodge these telegraph attacks and get close to the boss and do damage', pistol only). Switch: design.n26.level2 (n26.level2 on). room.origin is where tile 0 sits in the world (the worm 400, MONOLITH -400, BULWARK 800, ELDER WYRM 1200, HULK 1600).
glacier.name: THE GLACIER

course._why: The course: tileLen 40 m, half-width 12, lanes at x -7 / 0 / 7 (rails at +-3.5), a window of windowBack tiles behind and windowAhead ahead of the player's tile (+ the player's own: 8 tiles = 320 m: the contract's course length, recycled), a checkpoint every 4 tiles (160 m).

room._why: Where tile 0 sits in the world, the run-seed salt, and the one light (pale violet-white boundary tone, rule 8) that follows the player along the course.

hp._why: One pool; phases at 66 / 33 % (the worm's marks); the hull x1, the engine block on its back x2 (shoot it from behind, as you chase it). Tuned so the headless bot (pistol, close-range bonus) closes and kills in 2:00-3:30.

gap._why: The GAP METER (DESIGN24-bosses.md section 2; the contract's numbers): starts at 60 m, the boss can be hurt only at 25 m or less, a soft fail at 80 m (back to the checkpoint, the boss keeps its HP).

speed._why: The boss pulls away at base m/s (the player's sprint is about 9 and a boost strip adds 6, so you close in by skating well) x phaseMult per phase; it rubber-bands in ONE direction only: x (1 + rubber x clamp((gap - rubberNear) / (rubberFar - rubberNear))): faster when you are far, never slower when you are near (the HUD says so). laneMove m/s: how fast it slides between lanes, one lane choice every laneEvery s (from the seeded stream); introHold: it waits this long at the start.

tells._why: Every lane attack tells >= 0.6 s (the contract; the night's floor is 0.5): the sweeping bar 0.7 s (jump), the low bar 0.7 s (slide), the spike wall 0.9 s (be in the open lane: dash into it). Never two resolve inside resolveGap (0.5 s).

attack._why: A lane attack is placed `ahead` m in front of the player (never beyond the boss) and lethal for `life` s after its tell; damage 18 of the player's 100 and a push back; `thick` m thick (and the telegraph's width); every1 / every2 / every3 s between attacks in phase 1 / 2 / 3. Heights (m): the sweeping bar is 0.45 m tall (under a rail's 0.9: any jump clears it), the low bar hangs from 1.15 to 2.8 m (a slide passes under, a standing player does not), the spike wall is 3 m.

closeBonus._why: GG: 'you have to get close': a hit on the boss does up to max x damage at point blank, falling to x1 at `range` m (the gap's hurt line is 25 m): closing in pays. (The pistol is the only weapon in this level: the plan's LIMIT flag.)

body._why: The hull (a long dark skating block 3 x 1.2 x 5 m) and the engine block on its back (2 x 1 x 1.6 m); touching it hurts contactDamage with a cooldown; dieTime s of finisher.

wyrm26._why: LEVEL 3's WORM (builder B, contract wyrm-26; GG: 'it should almost feel a little like Terraria: if the boss is close it might just go after you', 'body hits do lesser damage, more on the head', 'a final harder attack when it coils in the middle', 'an arena that encourages wall riding'; Core/Enemies/Wyrm.cs under design.n26.level3, switch off = NIGHT25's worm bit for bit). paths / arena are Tools/gen-wyrm26.py's copies of NIGHT25's files plus the finale pattern and the wall-ride slabs.

hp._why: mult x the pool (design.n24.wyrm.hp.pool x design.n25.wyrmAim.hp.mult): tuned so the composed human-lag bot kills level 3's worm in 4:00-5:00 with deaths printed (NIGHT25's measured 3:57 with 2 deaths): the body now does half, the aggro and the finale cost the player time.

body._why: GG: 'if you hit the body of it it does damage but lesser damage and it does more if you hit the head'. The body and the tail land x mult on top of design.n24.wyrm.hp.bodyMult (1): body x0.5; the head (x2) and the exposed core (x3) are unchanged.

aggro._why: PROXIMITY AGGRO (RESEARCH.md S5, Terraria's worms): when the player is within radius m of the head or any piece, the head breaks its cycle and dives at him: a tell (tells.aggro, a line from the head to where he stood, LOCKED: sidestep it), then a pass at speedMult x the phase speed through his spot and overshoot m beyond it (clamped inside the room, between yMin and yMax m up, pitch limit pitch degrees), then the cycle restarts the pattern it interrupted. cooldown 14 s between aggros (GG said 6 s, DECIDE26 D-7; eased after the lead found 4-5 bot deaths too punishing), the first one after first s of a fight so the opening cycle reads. Never during an attack's tell, the finale, the dive's burrow or inside the resolve gap of another lethal attack.

tells._why: The night's rule: every tell >= 0.5 s. The aggro re-aim line tells 0.5 s (the floor), the finale's squeeze and its marked gap tell 1.0 s (the contract).

spit2._why: A SECOND SPIT LANE in phase 2 (contract: harder than NIGHT25's): delay s after each volley the body's in-between ports fire a second volley (never inside the resolve gap of a lethal attack): 0.7 s, so it reads as two beats, not one wall.

finale._why: The phase-3 FINALE (a ring squeeze with one marked gap, tell 1 s): contact with the worm while it runs hurts x contactMult (NIGHT25's body contact is 5, the squeeze would never matter): 1.5 means a ring touch is about 8 and a head touch 27: you leave through the gap or jump the ring.

n26._why: NIGHT26 U3-40 (GG 2026-10-08, after his first playtest: the first three levels, platforming, a chase boss, weapon identity, a level select with ranks, the PULSE on the left trigger): the seven NIGHT26 rows, one block each (design.n26.<row>.enabled), all off in the shared commit; a row is turned on only when its contract passes. Off (--off26 / -skygrindOff26): NIGHT25's game bit for bit. Unity-only numbers live in each row with a _why.

wormVisual._why: NIGHT26 builder V (GG 2026-10-08: 'Update the worm boss to use the new Tripo models, and add glow, aura and animation effects'): the KILN WYRM is drawn with the Tripo head / body / tail meshes (Assets/Art/WormBoss, baked into Resources/WormBossParts by SKYGRIND > Worm Boss > Build Prefab) with a red-orange emissive glow, an aura and the attack / hit / death animation (Game/WyrmVisual26.cs, WyrmGlow26.cs; every number in Game/UnityTuning.Wyrm26Fx.cs). View only: the sim, the hit boxes, the piece count and the movement are the same with it off. Off, or the parts asset missing: the blocky boxes of NIGHT24.

pulseLT._why: The PULSE GAUNTLET's blast is the LEFT TRIGGER (builder W, GG 2026-10-08: 'the gauntlet the second weapon it doesn't do the blast attack at all with the left trigger ... it's supposed to charge and build up'): holding LT charges by use (its hits), releasing launches the player along the aim with a little damage, a 3 s lockout; the left click is a plain swing; R3 punches. NIGHT25 put this on the click: wrong. Off (--off26): NIGHT25's click-charge.

weaponIdentity._why: Every weapon has an LT and a cost, enemies have vulnerabilities, the rocket and the BOUNCER are nerfed, weapons unlock one per level or two (builder W, GG: 'almost all the weapons should really have a left trigger that either zooms in or does something else ... you really don't feel incentivized at all to switch weapons ... the grenade and rocket launcher are a little too broken'). Numbers are added by builder W under this row, each with a _why. Off (--off26): NIGHT25's arsenal and loadout.

identity._why: NIGHT26 D-8 (GG: 'the grenade and rocket launcher are a little too broken, they clear enemies too fast'): the ROCKET and the BOUNCER cost more over the web's numbers (weapons.rocket / weapons.bouncer stay the web's; Core/Guns/Weapon26.cs + Projectiles.ApplyIdentity26 apply these at a run's start). Unity-only: the web's guns are tuned for a Zombies loop where the launcher wins.

rocket._why: D-8: damage -30 % (x0.7), blast radius -35 % (x0.65), a 2.2 s reload (the web's fireInterval is 0.9 s), and the blast hurts you: selfDamage is the HP a rocket at your feet deals (linear to nothing at selfRadiusFrac of the radius). The rocket jump still works (the push is the web's).

bouncer._why: D-8: damage -35 % (x0.65), fuse 2.4 s (the web's 1.6), at most 3 grenades in the air (the web's pool is 12). selfDamage 0: the grenade jump stays free (its cost is the fuse and the pool). cookMax: LT held with the BOUNCER and none of yours in the air counts up to this many seconds into the next grenade's fuse (a cooked grenade bursts that much sooner: an airburst by timing, ULTRAKILL's cook). Less than fuse - 1 step, so a grenade never bursts in the hand.

identity.selfRadiusFrac_why: A blast hurts its owner only inside this share of its (already nerfed) radius, so a rocket at a body 3 m away does not hurt: self damage is for point blank.

weapons._why: Every weapon's LT (GG: 'almost all the weapons should really have a left trigger that either zooms in or does something else'). `lt` is the LT in words (the table is Design/weapons/WEAPON-IDENTITY.md); `zoom` 0 marks a gun whose LT stops being a zoom and is its own alt (read by Identity26 / Loadout.ZoomGun); the zoom magnifications stay the web's (config ads.weapons) and design.zoom / design.n25.shockwaveOff.

revolver._why: KESTREL: zoom is the web's; a charged shot was in the brief and is NOT built tonight.

gauntlet.lt: blast: hold LT (it swings, the hits charge the notches), release launches along the aim (design.n26.pulseLT)
gauntlet._why: The PULSE's blast moved from the click to LT (GG).

shotgun._why: THUNDERCLAP: GG removed the shockwave in NIGHT25.

nailgun.lt: detonate every nail stuck in a body
nailgun._why: STITCHER: NIGHT20 left the detonate on the SPECIAL key and zoomed LT; here LT is the detonate (zoom 0).

rocket._why: COMET: the web's steer, unchanged; a detonate-in-flight was a brief example and is not built (steer is the unique alt).

rail._why: LONGWAVE: the web's scope; the overcharge stays on SPECIAL.

zapper.lt: overload: discharge every shocked body in sight
zapper._why: ZAPPER: the discharge (NIGHT19) on LT instead of a 1.3 zoom (zoom 0).

bouncer.lt: press: airburst the live grenades; hold with none in the air: cook the next one
bouncer._why: BOUNCER: the airburst is the web's; the cook is new (design.n26.weaponIdentity.identity.bouncer.cookMax).

vortex.lt: tap: collapse the orbs; hold: repel (NIGHT20)

rattler.lt: zoom 1.4 when it is ported (the web's ads.weapons.rattler)
rattler._why: RATTLER, DISCUS, CHOIR, PRISM, SUNDER, FLICKER, THUMPER, TETHER are not ported to Unity (Loadout.Fires is false): no LT to build.

vulnerability._why: Enemy-weapon pairing (RESEARCH.md S2, GG: 'every single weapon has a positive a weakness'): a multiplier on what a hit deals, by enemy kind and weapon (or weapon class). Unity-only; read in Loadout.Damage before the kind's own filter. class: single = one body per shot (KESTREL, STITCHER, PULSE), pierce = the LONGWAVE, spread = the THUNDERCLAP, chain = the ZAPPER, area = TORCH / VORTEX, slow = ROCKET / BOUNCER (a shot a flier can dodge).

swarmer._why: SWARMERS melt to anything that hits many (x1.2) and shrug off single shots (x0.6): the brief's 'swarmer x0.6 for single-target'.

drone._why: DRONES fly: a slow shot (rocket, grenade) lands at half (the brief's x0.5); the beam and the arc find them (x1.25).

windup._why: A CHARGER in its wind-up takes x1.5 from the hitscans that can hit that moment (the brief's 'charger windup x1.5').

tank._why: NIGHT29 (GG: 'a tank enemy that can be one shot by the fists'; D-2 / item 11): the level-2 TANK is a husk body with design.n29.tank.hp (600) that the PULSE gauntlet kills in ONE hit (x10 on the heavy swing: weapons.gauntlet.damage 32 x pulse27 damageMult 6 x 10 = 1920, three times its hp; the plain fist, class single, lands x0.4 = 4), the KESTREL lands x0.15 (25 -> 3.75: 160 shots, about a minute, so the room's husks are the pistol's job and the tank is the gauntlet's), every other gun x0.4 by its class. A weapon's own key wins over its class (Vulnerability26.Look). Read only for a body spawned as kind 'tank' (Enemy.tank29), which exists only with design.n29.tank on.

warden._why: The WARDEN's front shield (NIGHT20 blocked every hit that was not splash): now a front hit lands x0.2 (soft) and the RAIL and a PULSE punch land it whole (the brief: 'warden shield x0.2 except rail / punch').

surfaces._why: Ice, mud and boost strips from a level plan's `surfaces` list through the one named Mover change: a public groundFrictionMult (default 1) multiplied into the ground friction call (builder M, GG: 'different surfaces ... speed skating'). Golden vectors and trajectory replays stay exact (default 1). Off (--off26): every surface reads as normal ground.
surfaces.iceFrictionMult_why: x the ground friction on an ICE rect (DECIDE26 D-6, NIGHT26.md: 'about 0.25'): the walk-speed stop takes about 4x the metres, so a skater carries speed and cannot stop on a coin. The web has no surfaces. NIGHT72 N5b (the lead's call, PRINCIPLES 1: the ice slide stays): design.ultra71.set's ground friction is 31.07 (was 6), so the multiplier is 0.25 x 6 / 31.07 = 0.048281: the lab's walk stop on ice stays 4.766 m (it would be 0.872 m at 0.25; evidence n5-lab-4-surfaces.txt, n5-surfaces-solve.txt). Only one ice rect is in the levels (iceline g4's canal); glide30 (ON) keeps glide ice's own decay.
surfaces.mudFrictionMult_why: x the ground friction on a MUD rect (NIGHT26.md: 'mud 2.0'): the stop takes half the metres, the footing is sticky; used sparingly for contrast with ice. The web has no surfaces. NIGHT72 N5b (the lead's call): with ground friction 31.07 the web's 2 would stop in 0.023 m; 0.4685 keeps the walk stop at 0.437 m (the lab, n5-surfaces-solve.txt). The web's mud also capped the walk at 6.67 m/s (friction above accel); under friction = accel nothing caps it, so mud no longer slows the walk (8.49 m/s): no level has a mud rect.
surfaces.boostImpulse_why: m/s pushed once along the strip's direction through Mover.Impulse each time a grounded player enters a BOOST strip (DECIDE26 D-6: 6 m/s, about three quarters of walk speed): the speed-skating kick. The web has no surfaces.

wallRide._why: Wall riding that feels good without a Mover change (builder M, NIGHT26.md, RESEARCH.md S1: speed + a camera cue + a guide line). Four view-only things: a FOV lift while riding, a steeper lean, cyan light strips along long rideable walls. Off (--off26): the web's roll, no lift, no strips (the sim is never touched, so the fingerprint cannot move).
wallRide.fovLiftDeg_why: Degrees the view widens while wall riding, on top of the speed FOV within camera.maxFovBoostDeg: about the sprint's widen (5.95 deg), so a ride reads as speed without the boost's 12 deg punch. Unity-only.
wallRide.fovEaseRate_why: Ease rate (1/s, the camera.fovEaseRate form) of the lift in and out: ~0.3 s to most of the way, so a 1.2 s ride (wallRide.maxTime) shows it fully. Unity-only.
wallRide.rollDeg_why: The lean away from the wall in degrees (the web's wallRide.rollDeg is 10; the pre-tilt before contact uses the same angle): GG wants the ride to be the thing you feel; 14 shows it at 1080p without nausea (REDUCED MOTION still removes it). Unity-only.
wallRide.stripMinLength_why: Metres: a wall box whose long side is at least this gets light strips (a wall shorter than a ride's reach, about 12 m at the ride's entry speed over maxTime, is not a ride). Unity-only.
wallRide.stripHeight_why: Metres above the wall's base: the strip's centre, about the camera's eye (body.eyeHeight) so it runs through the middle of the view while you ride. Unity-only.
wallRide.stripClear_why: Metres of wall that must stand above the strip: a low parapet is not a rideable wall. Unity-only.
wallRide.stripThickness_why: Metres, the strip's width and height (thin trim; the room trim is design.n24.lighting.trim). Unity-only.
wallRide.stripOffset_why: Metres off the wall face so the strip never z-fights the wall. Unity-only.
wallRide.stripBrightness_why: Colour multiplier on the usable cyan (the neon material is unlit emissive; the room trim uses design.n24.lighting.trim.brightness): bright enough to read at dusk from 20 m. Unity-only.

levelSelect._why: The ULTRAKILL-style level select, three ranks (time, kills, style), the aggregate and P rank, the best per level in the profile, CAMPAIGN as the default and first mode (builder L, GG: 'when you click into the campaign which should be the first game mode by the way that should be the default one ... it should be like ULTRAKILL where it kind of shows all the levels what rank you got what time'). Off (--off26): NIGHT25's TITLE and results.
levelSelect.slots_why: Unity-only: the select lists ten slots (GG: levels 8 to 10 in the end; ULTRAKILL's column); a slot past the curriculum's levels shows LOCKED.
levelSelect.playable_why: Unity-only: only the first three levels can be started tonight (NIGHT26: 'we're only going to focus on the first 3'); levels 4+ have plan files but show LOCKED until NIGHT27.
levelSelect.sequential_why: Unity-only: true = a level needs the one before it cleared (ULTRAKILL's progression). Off tonight so a stuck boss never blocks GG's playtest of the next level; the cursor still rests on the first uncleared level.

rank._why: Campaign ranks (builder L, Core/Rank26.cs; GG: 'it should be like ULTRAKILL where it shows all the levels what rank you got what time'): TIME, KILLS and STYLE each D-S by the plan's own `rank` block, else these defaults; aggregate = S 5 / A 4 / B 3 / C 2 / D 1 summed minus 1 per checkpoint restart; P = S in all three with no restart. Unity-only: the web has no campaign.
rank.aggregateMin_why: Unity-only: the least summed points for an aggregate S, A, B, C (D below). 15 is three S; one restart already costs the S (so only P-like runs are S); 12 is three A.
rank.timeShares_why: Unity-only: a level without its own time cuts is ranked by its summed room par x these (S, A, B, C): the same shares as design.n24.campaign.rank (par is the designer's clean time; 4 x par is the bot's gate).
rank.killsDefault_why: Unity-only: percent of the plan's enemies killed for S, A, B, C by default.
rank.styleDefault_why: Unity-only: style points for S, A, B, C by default; NOT calibrated tonight (no bot measured a level's style): each plan's own block is the number to tune.

level1._why: Level 1 THE FOUNDRY: the tutorial shortened, every room at most 28 m wide, a platforming run and a wall-ride hall, ending in THE SLAG HULK (builder L and B, GG: 'for that first map the arena is just way too wide ... platforming sections'). Off (--off26): NIGHT25's tutorial.

level2._why: Level 2 THE ICE LINE: the speed-skating chase on ice, pistol only, THE GLACIER ahead with telegraphed lane attacks and a gap meter (builder B and M, GG: 'the second one to feel like you're speed skating to get this boss'). Off (--off26): level 2 is NIGHT25's THE KILN.

level3._why: Level 3 THE KILN: today's layer 1 rooms trimmed and the worm with proximity aggro, body x0.5 / head x2, a final attack and a wall-riding arena (builder B and L, GG: 'it should almost feel a little like Terraria'). Off (--off26): NIGHT25's worm.

n28._why: NIGHT28 (GG 2026-10-09, on the second boss: 'you can't even create a proper arena ... you can't even curve the surface. You also can't even make the entire floor that skating texture or the physics. It's inconsistent.'): THE GLACIER's rink rebuilt as a REAL curved arena of triangles with ONE ice rule. Every number here is Unity-only (the web had no glacier); the starting values are Research/2026-10-09-wave28/GLACIER-REDESIGN.md section 3.1, to be tuned by the rink28 probe.

rink._why: THE GLACIER's stadium rink (Core/Enemies/Rink28Arena.cs on Rink28Math): two straights joined by two half-circle caps, an island in the middle with two doors, a flat lane round it, a 28 degree bank, a flat lip and a vertical rim wall, all emitted as collision triangles in code (the map JSON cannot hold an arc). Off: the NIGHT27 straight tile course is unchanged.
rink.enabled_why: Off until the lead flips it: with it off the NIGHT27 glacier is unchanged, and golden and the fingerprint are exact. The rink replaces the straight tile course only when this is true.
rink.origin_why: The rink's centre (x, floor y, z) in the sim: the same slot as design.n27.boss2.room.origin, so the room's place in the world, its light and its respawn bookkeeping stay as they were.
rink.straight_why: Length of each straight, m (doc 3.1): the wall-ride lane. A ride lasts wallRide.maxTime 1.2 s, about 19-24 m at 16-20 m/s, so the straight is the right length.
rink.centreRadius_why: Radius of the centre line round each cap, m (doc 3.1): island radius 3 + half the 5.5 m lane. The boss and the spawn follow this line (Rink28Math).
rink.islandRadius_why: Radius of the island's caps, m (doc 3.1): the island is 30 x 6 m with the 24 m straight.
rink.islandHeight_why: Height of the island, m (doc 3.1): taller than a jump (1.5 m), so it blocks sight and the boss's line and you cannot shoot across.
rink.doorWidth_why: Width of each of the TWO doors cut through the island at the middles of its long sides, m (doc 3.1): the cut that turns the loop into a figure with a shortcut.
rink.laneWidth_why: Width of the flat lane on each side of the island, m (doc 3.1).
rink.bankDeg_why: Bank angle, degrees (doc 3.1): normal.y 0.883, inside the Mover's 0.7 floor limit (45.6 degrees), so the bank is GROUND for walking and the slide's slope gravity (slopeBoost 1.6) is the speed engine.
rink.bankRun_why: Horizontal run of the bank, m (doc 3.1); with 28 degrees the rise is run x tan(bank) = 2.39 m (the doc's 2.4).
rink.lip_why: A flat shelf where the bank meets the rim wall, m (doc 4 risk 1): the bank and the rim meet at 62 degrees, in the Mover's dead band between floor and wall, so the corner gets a flat strip instead.
rink.rimHeight_why: Height of the vertical rim wall above the lip, m (doc 3.1). Vertical: wall-ridable on the straights.
rink.facetDeg_why: Each end cap is faceted in steps of this many degrees (doc 3.1): 24 facets per cap, about 1.8 m a facet at the lane edge, every adjacent pair far under the wall ride's 30 degree corner rule.
rink.lid_why: A collision ceiling at the rim top so a pulse launch cannot leave the rink (the view's roof has a skylight; the collision lid has none).
rink.playerStartS_why: Arc coordinate (m, Rink28Math: 0 = the start of the bottom straight) where the player spawns on the lane: on the straight with room to run.
rink.spawnGap_why: The player starts this many metres of arc behind the boss's start (doc 3.6: start gap 30 m; the boss builder places the boss at playerStartS + spawnGap).
rink.streakLinesPerM_why: Skate streak density across the travel direction, lines per metre, on the whole rink's ice material (RinkIce28 shader, world space): the same idea as design.n27.skate27.streakLinesPerM but over the entire floor, not a patch round the feet. Render only.
rink.scratchGain_why: Brightness of the always-on world-space scratches on the ice (so a standing player still sees skated ice, and every metre of floor looks the same). Render only.

glacier._why: NIGHT28 builder B2 (GG: 'the second boss fight, it's just so horrible again ... boring and not fun, doesn't encourage unique gameplay'): THE GLACIER as a LAP CHASE on the rink (design.n28.rink; the arc coordinate is Core/Enemies/Rink28Math.cs). Core/Enemies/Glacier28.cs, doc Research/2026-10-09-wave28/GLACIER-REDESIGN.md sections 3.3-3.6. The web had no glacier, so every number here is Unity-only; each group has its _why. enabled false until the lead turns the plan id 'glacier' over to it (the NIGHT27 glacier stays on file).
glacier.name: THE GLACIER

hits._why: THREE PULSE hits kill it, the pool split in thirds (the HP bar's two marks), whatever the swing's damage (the NIGHT27 rule: a miss costs gap, never health). No HP cut anywhere.

speed._why: THE GAP CONTROLLER on the loop (doc 3.3 / 3.6): the boss flees along the shorter arc from the player at `base` m/s plus clamp(k m/s per metre x (gap - target), +-clampFrac x slideFloor); slideFloor 11.6 is movement.slide.floorSpeed, so the boss is never more than 15 % of it off its base. THE TARGET DEPENDS ON THE GLOVE (the harness showed a fixed 28 m target is a rubber band a sprinting player never crosses, and a glove on its 15 s cooldown has nothing to hit with): glove READY: target targetGap 48 m (above the far side's 42 m, so the boss is in its tired band, base - clamp = 7.76 m/s, and can be run down from anywhere); glove SPENT: target spentTarget 0 (it runs flat out, base + clamp = 11.24 m/s, and pulls away from anything but a clean slider: the cooldown is the boss's lead). The flee direction flips only when the other arc is shorter by more than `hysteresis` m (no oscillation at the far side); a flip is a visible SKID of about skidSeconds (the brake is 2 x base / skidSeconds), then none for flipHoldSeconds s (no chatter when you hover at its tail; a player who has passed it reads a negative gap meanwhile). introHold s: no attacks while it pulls away. The start gap is design.n28.rink.spawnGap (30 m).

gap._why: A PULSE-READY window of windowTime s opens when the gap falls under windowAt m and the glove is ready (GG's brief 12 m / 1.5 s); a window that runs out costs missCost m of gap (the boss runs on, over surgeSeconds s, never a teleport) and NEVER health; armTime s before a window may open again; a hit surges the boss hitBack m ahead the same way.

launch._why: The PULSE blast's lock-on, the NIGHT27 rule (design.n27.boss2.launch): a blast released while the window is open, with the boss within reach m and the throw within coneDeg degrees of the line to it, LANDS. refill: the kill pips a hit (or a clang) gives back (there are no kills on the ice), so three blasts win the fight; the blast's own 15 s cooldown (design.n27.pulse27) paces the hits.

glaze._why: The ICE GLAZE (doc 3.3, DECIDE28 D-2: pistol and shotgun may crack it): the boss wears cyan-lit plates. A PULSE blast that lands while it is glazed CLANGS OFF: no hit, the glove is spent and refilled (refill), and the boss runs clangCost m further away (a surge, never health). Cracking it: `hits` pistol hits per phase (8, 8, 5: it cracks faster later), or ONE charged pistol shot (a hit of at least chargedFactor x weapons.revolver.damage counts chargedHits, so chargeShots27 off still works: 8 plain hits), or a shotgun blast whose hit lands within shotgunRange m. Cracked, it stays open openSeconds s, then re-glazes (the crack count starts over). Guns still never hurt the boss; only the pulse does.

cut._why: THE ISLAND DOOR CUT (doc 3.3): if you go through a door of the island (design.n28.rink.doorWidth wide, at the middle of the island) and the boss's flee direction flips within memorySeconds s of it (you came out ahead of it), that is a CUT: the boss brakes and reverses (the skid), and a pulse hit within holdSeconds s of the flip counts even when glazed, once per phase. The movement verb causes it; no timer opens it.

shards._why: The P1 attack, SHARD TRAIL (doc 3.4): `count` ice shards (size m square, as tall) seeded on the racing line between the boss and you: the decal shows for tell s (0.8 s = 96 steps), then each shard stands for life s and a touch costs damage HP and a push (the lane attacks' damage path). They are placed ahead of your path (leadMetres + your speed x the tell ahead of you, spacing m apart along the line, never on you and never beyond the boss) all at one lateral offset per trail drawn from `lateral` m (the harness showed a lateral per shard covered the whole 5.5 m lane and sent the pilot out over the bank, the long way round the caps), so a line is always free in the lane: the side the trail leaves open, or the bank. No trail while the gap is under minGap. every s between trails.

melt._why: The P2 attack, THAW (doc 3.4): the middle `length` m of a straight turns to meltwater across the lane and the bank. The decal, live and spacing times and the damage are the hazardFloor27 numbers (design.n27.hazardFloor27: telegraphSeconds 1.5, liveSeconds 8, spacingSeconds 20, damagePerSecond 12 in ticks of tickSeconds, a rider whose feet are standHeight m above the floor is safe); the strip is Glacier28's own (that row's state lives in the campaign sim). The safe route is the wall-ride lane on the rim of the straight. The first strip of a phase is harmless (teach, then test). firstStartSeconds s after the phase starts.

columns._why: The P3 ICE COLUMNS (doc 3.4): `count` columns of size m (4 m tall) in a SLALOM: alternate sides at lateral offset +-offset m, spacing m apart along the line, ahead of you; decal tell s (1.0 s), standing for life s; a touch costs damage HP: dash-slalom. every s between P3 attacks (rotation: columns, roller, bar, chasm).

roller._why: The P3 ROLLER (doc 3.4): a boulder of radius m (height 2 x radius) rolling toward you along the lane at speed m/s from ahead metres away, decal tell s (0.6 s), gone after life s: jump it or climb the bank.

bar._why: The P3 LOW BAR (doc 3.4): a bar across the lane and the bank from `bottom` to `top` m above the floor, thick m along the line, decal tell s (0.7 s), standing for life s: slide under it (the slide's capsule is 1 m tall).

chasm._why: The P3 CHASM (doc 3.4): a strip of length m across the lane and the bank where the floor is GONE (decal tell s 1.2, open for life s): touching it on the ground costs damage HP and throws you back out the side you came from; only a jump / slide-jump / LT launch crosses it (the harness measures which). The collision floor is not cut (the arena's triangles are builder A2's): the sim treats a grounded foot inside the strip as a fall.

n29._why: NIGHT29 (GG 2026-10-09, after his playtest of NIGHT28: a complete overhaul of levels 1-3, two bosses that take damage, a fire / melee lockout, a slower shotgun, a CRT overlay, door-free dev toggle): every row is off in the shared commit and turned on only when its contract passes. Off (--off29 / -skygrindOff29, and every older off switch): NIGHT28's game bit for bit. Unity-only numbers each carry a _why (the web never had these systems).

lockout._why: GG: 'you can't fire and melee at the same time ... you have to wait for the shot to finish'; reverses NIGHT25's meleeFire. Policy only: the cycle lengths are read from each weapon's own fire interval and the swing's cycle (nothing typed here). The second input is DROPPED (D-1: GG wants to wait).
lockout.bufferSeconds_why: 0 = the second input is DROPPED (D-1); the rule reads no buffer (Core/Guns/Lockout29.cs), the key is the policy's marker.
lockout.lessonPrompt_why: The tutorial's punchWhileFiring lesson (Lesson25) taught firing and punching together (NIGHT25 meleeFire); with the lockout on it teaches the new order: one, wait for it to end, the other. Five words (CURRICULUM.md rule 5: at most six). Shown in place of the plan's own prompt; the lesson's window grows by the longest cycle (LessonSample.lockoutGap).

shotgun._why: GG: the shotgun 'fires a little too fast'. The web has one fixed interval (weapons.shotgun.fireInterval); this multiplies it. 1.3 is the pick (NIGHT29.md: 1.25-1.4). READ (SimHarness shotgun29, 2026-10-09): the effective shot-to-shot time with design.n24.shotgunTune already on was 63 steps = 0.525 s (the web's 0.9 s x NIGHT20's retune 0.45 x NIGHT24's 1.3); with this x1.3 it is 82 steps = 0.683 s. The viewmodel pump (weapons.shotgun.pumpDelay 0.45 s) is unchanged and no longer overlaps the next shot. The pellets' damage is NOT raised (NIGHT24's damageMult already keeps the per-second number): the shotgun now does 1/1.3 of its NIGHT28 damage per second, which GG asked for (slower); a small per-pump rise only if the bot's time in the shotgun niche drops by more than 15 % (not measured).

tank._why: Level 2's coloured TANK (GG: 'a tank enemy that can be one shot by the fists'): the web's heavy box recoloured, hp high; the vulnerability table (design.n26.vulnerability.tank) says the gauntlet x10, the pistol x0.15. The web has no tank.
tank.hp_why: The hit points of a body spawned as kind 'tank' (Husks.Spawn): 3x the gauntlet's pulse swing is 1920 after the x10 row, so 600 is one hit with room to spare and 160 pistol shots (x0.15). The web's husk has 40. Unity-only (the web has no tank).
tank.color_why: The tank's body colour (a hex as the web's colors.*): a darker, heavier rust than colors.enemy (16730652, the husks' red-orange): still the enemy palette (CLAUDE.md rule 8: red-orange is enemies and danger only; no magenta, no cyan), so it reads as one of them, bigger and darker. Read by HuskView.
tank.scale_why: The tank's body drawn 1.4x the husk's size (view only; the collider is the husk's): a heavy that reads as a heavy at a glance. Unity-only.

boss1._why: THE LANTERN reworked (GG: 'I'm not able to attack the first boss ... floor is lava ... exposed ... slow motion barrier'). Diagnosis: Lantern27.Filter returned 0 unless the shot hit the face looking at the ridden wall. lightDamage = the share of a normal hit any gun does anywhere; full damage only while the core is exposed (the floor live) and the shooter is wall riding. The cycle: tell (the glow shifts, the core opens), live floor, rest. slowScale / slowEaseS: the world slows while the floor is live (D-7: 0.55, 0.2 s; not a time stop). The web has no boss.
boss1.attackTellMinSeconds_why: DESIGN29: every attack shows a tell of at least 0.8 s. Lantern27 had orb tells of 0.6 s after the first attack (design.n27.boss1.orb.tellLater); with this rule on no tell is shorter than this. Applied in Lantern27 only when the NIGHT29 rule is attached.
boss1.lightDamage_why: Round 4 (Player build n29-4): at 0.20 an IMMORTAL floor-standing shooter killed the Lantern in 73 s against the rider's 45 s (only 1.6x; the harness had hidden it behind the floor bot's deaths, which reset the fight). At 0.06 the immortal floor bot is not killed in 145 s (3x the fastest rider's 48 s; bar 0.12 left). Applied to every gun hit when the core is not exposed or the shooter is not wall riding.

boss2._why: THE GLACIER reworked (GG: 'for some reason I still can't damage it ... speed skating ... both of you trying not to be caught'). Diagnosis: Glacier28.Filter let only a PULSE hit in a window land. otherGunFraction = the share of the gauntlet's hit any other gun does at any time (D-8: 0.12); otherGunFloor = the bar share other guns cannot take it below (the last quarter needs the exposed window, so a camper never finishes it); exposedSeconds / catchUpMetres: the window a catch-up opens; frostSlow: the slow of a frost trail; patience*: V2's rule (R1): staying farther than patienceMetres for patienceSeconds speeds the volleys by patienceVolleyMult until the gap closes under patienceCloseMetres. The skate lane's own numbers are added by builder B with their _why.
boss2.otherGunFraction_why: Measured (harness boss29 glacier, NIGHT29 B): 0.12 (the card's start) let a pistol alone take the bar to its floor in about 8 s of fire (a catch-up bot killed in 20 s); 0.01 gives about 10 HP of a 3000 pool per pistol hit, so the floor takes minutes of fire and the catch-up windows do the work (10 seeds: median 89 s, 69-150 s).
boss2.attackTellMinSeconds_why: DESIGN29: every attack shows a tell of at least 0.8 s. Glacier28's roller (the lane charge) told 0.6 s; with the rule on every hazard, decal and tell event is raised to this minimum (Glacier28.tellMin29). The shard volley (0.8) and the frost trail (frost.tellSeconds 0.8) already met it.
boss2.exposedGunFraction_why: Builder B (NIGHT29): during the EXPOSED window (the catch-up) a gun hit does this share of a gauntlet hit and the bar floor does not apply, so a player who catches the boss with the pistol can finish it; outside the window guns do otherGunFraction and stop at otherGunFloor. The web has no boss; 0.3 killed in 20-60 s; 0.07 with otherGunFraction 0.01 gives the 80-120 s band (harness boss29 glacier, 10 seeds, median 89 s).

lane._why: THE SKATE LANE rule (DESIGN29 G, Core/SkateLane29.cs), applied after the Mover each step, outside it. The web has no ice lanes. count lane lines are laid across the flat lane of the rink at spacing m (the rink's flat lane is 5.5 m wide, so 3 lines at 2.1 m fit (the outer lines clear a 3 m shard by its capsule: 2.1 > 1.5 + 0.4); the five-lane arena of card G1 is not built yet: the rule reads count and spacing). Grounded on the ice above snapSpeed m/s the player's lateral position eases to the nearest line at easeRate m/s and the sideways velocity is zeroed (the wall ride's snap look); a ground dash sideways whose sideways share of the speed is at least dashLateralFrac moves to the adjacent line over switchSeconds; speed bleeds bleedPerSecond of itself per second while locked on a lane. Off a lane (under snapSpeed or on the bank) the ice friction x0.25 of design.n26.surfaces stays.

boss._why: The boss skates the lanes (card C2): every laneEverySeconds it picks an adjacent lane line (Mulberry32) and slews to it at laneSlew m/s, so the lane the player is in is not always the boss's. The catch-up needs the SAME lane and a gap under catchUpMetres. Unity-only.
boss.speedMult_why: Scales the boss's skating speed (Glacier28's gap controller, design.n28.glacier.speed) with the reworked rule: the lane lock, the dashes the volleys ask for and the frost trails cost the player speed that NIGHT28's free-steering chase did not, so the boss is slowed by this factor to keep the catch-up reachable. Measured by the harness (boss29 glacier: the player's mean speed vs the boss's).

volley._why: ICE SHARD VOLLEY (card C2): the shards of Glacier28 (design.n28.glacier.shards: 3 shards, 0.8 s tell, 10 damage) now come every volleyEverySeconds from P1 on; patience (staying beyond patienceMetres for patienceSeconds) divides the interval by patienceVolleyMult. A sideways dash dodges (the open side of the trail). Nothing kills under 0.5 s (10 damage per shard).

frost._why: FROST TRAIL (card C2, from P1 on): a slow field laid ahead of the player in the player's lane: length m long, standing lifeSeconds, 0.8 s tell, speed x(1 - frostSlow) inside it (the speed the player entered with); no damage. A lane switch avoids it. Unity-only.

charge._why: LANE CHARGE (card C2, from P2 on): Glacier28's roller (design.n28.glacier.roller: 0.8 s tell, damage, speed) along the player's lane every everySeconds; a jump clears it. Unity-only schedule.

bossHp._why: Boss pools cut to the kill bands (D-5: Lantern 45-70 s, Glacier 80-120 s, worm 3:00-4:00 for a human-lag bot). The cuts are measured by the harness and written here with the before / after line; 1.0 = unchanged until measured.
bossHp.lanternMult_why: Round 4: re-measured with lightDamage 0.06: x0.285 gives a median 67 s over 10 lag-bot seeds (the deaths cost 20 s each; no-death riders 44-48 s, the Player rider 48 s at x0.35). Before: Measured (harness boss29 lantern, wall-riding lag bot, 10 seeds, pistol, organic kills, NIGHT29 B): pool x1.0 kills at about 108 s with no deaths (god-mode read, floor damage 230 per fight); x0.45 gave 66-77 s (median 75, over the band); x0.35 gives a median 62 s (44-67 s, 1 death in 8 of 10 fights: the live floor costs the bot about 25 HP a cycle). Band 45-70 s (D-5).
bossHp.glacierMult_why: Measured (harness boss29 hp): the reworked Glacier's every hit is a share of its pool (otherGunFraction, exposedGunFraction, the third), so scaling the pool leaves the kill time unchanged (x1.00 and x0.50 both median 89 s); its band is met by those fractions, so no cut is needed.
bossHp.wormMult_why: Measured (harness boss29 hp, the composed human-lag bot of `wyrm --composed`, 3 seeds): pool x1.00 killed in a mean 5:09 with 11 bot deaths; x0.70 in 3:40 with 9 deaths (band 3:00-4:00). The cut rides on the n29 boss blocks (boss1 or boss2): the NIGHT29 sim has no separate block for it. NIGHT26's worm (hp pool in Design/bosses/wyrm.json) is otherwise unchanged.

doorFree._why: GG's own dev tool: hold RB 3 s (F8 on the keyboard) and every door of the level stands open; enemies still spawn when a room is entered; the run is UNRANKED and writes no record (D-6). The web has no doors.
doorFree.holdSeconds_why: GG: 'hold the right bumper for like three seconds' (NIGHT29.md item 14; D-6): the unbroken hold that flips the toggle; whole steps (stepsFor). The keyboard's F8 hold is the same number.
doorFree.revealSeconds_why: A normal RB press (punch / switch) must stay unchanged: nothing of the hold shows, and the HUD's ring does not start, before this much holding (NIGHT29.md item 14: 'unchanged inside the first 0.4 s'). Unity-only.

pickups._why: NIGHT29 round 2 (V's finding: the plan's weaponPickup / healthPickup props were drawn but could not be collected). Walking onto a plan pickup takes it: the weapon named in the row (a loadout id or its name, 'thunderclap' = the shotgun) through the loadout and weaponEarned, once (the room award and the unlock table skip a weapon a pickup already gave), or a heal. Tape bit 6 (older tapes read it 0 = off). The web has no pickups on plan rooms.
pickups.reachMetres_why: NIGHT29 round 2 task 1: 'within about 1.2 m of its centre' (horizontal). Unity-only.
pickups.reach_why: The feet band around the prop's centre height (the props float 0.9-1.0 m over their floor): feet from 1.6 m below to 0.6 m above its centre, so standing on its floor counts and a pickup on another floor does not.
pickups.healFraction_why: A health pickup (the rest rooms f6 / i7 / k3) heals this share of max health (a fixed share, never more than the bar); a full bar leaves the pickup there. Unity-only.

roomRules._why: NIGHT29 round 2 (DESIGN29 A and f5): the wall-ride room's STAND-INS (husk bodies that never move by themselves or attack and take damage only from shots fired while wall riding; one strafes) and the fall cost (a fall to a room's respawnY costs a share of max health, never below 1 HP). Tape bit 7 (older tapes read it 0 = off).
roomRules.fallCostFraction_why: DESIGN29 A: 'Fall = a cost of 25 % health and a respawn at the room's start'. Unity-only.
roomRules.standInSpeed_why: The strafing stand-in's speed in m/s between the plan's spanLz ends (the plan gives the span, not a speed): slower than a husk's run, so the slow-mo aim can track it. Unity-only.

crt._why: View only. The retro-TV overlay (GG: 'pixel like ... retro TV vibe with the static ... not too intense ... a little warped'). Starting numbers from Research/2026-10-09-wave29/R4b-crt-lights.md (scaled down from open CRT shader defaults); the final values are looked at on a still. Strength 0-1 scales every effect; the setting's default is 35 %.

lights._why: View / validator row: every light fixture is a socket in the plan (wall, ceiling or pool), flush to a surface or with a collider; none floats in the playable space (GG: lights 'aren't properly placed and you can run through them').

props._why: View row: props are authored rows in the plan; no random scatter (GG: 'objects are randomly placed and it just looks ugly').

doors._why: View row: a door is a frame built from the wall opening; the gap between a door and its room is 0 (GG: 'gaps in between the major doors').

n27._why: NIGHT27 (GG 2026-10-09, after his playtest of NIGHT26: tight arenas with wall lanes, an original wall-ride boss, a pulse-only ice chase, a slower PULSE, charge shots, slow-mo on a wall-ride aim, roofs): the ten NIGHT27 rows, all off in the shared commit; a row is turned on only when its contract passes. Off (--off27 / -skygrindOff27): NIGHT26's game bit for bit. Unity-only numbers live under each row with a _why (a new gameplay number the web never had: its file is design.n27 in this config).

arenas27._why: The first three levels rebuilt tight (GG 2026-10-09: 'the arenas are still way too wide ... a complete overhaul on the first three stages'): rooms at most 24 m wide x 40 m long, enemy counts from a cost budget, two wall-ride lanes per room, the three random LIMIT rooms removed. Mostly level data + a validator rule; the bit gates the campaign's use of the new plans. Off (--off27): NIGHT26's rooms.

budget._why: The enemy COST BUDGET the validator holds every wave to (R1 rule from Cyber Grind's wave points; the web has no such number: its waves were a director's random picks, never a hand-authored room script): a wave's points are waveBase + wavePerIndex x its index in the room (0-based), and the sum of its enemies' costs may not exceed them. Numbers are starting values to be tuned by a measurement (the bots' clears).
budget.wallFasterPct_why: R1 rule 9: the wall lane must be at least this percent faster (in time) than the floor route for a combat room to pass (NIGHT26's flue: 3.2 s against 8.6 s).
budget.wallLaneSpeed_why: Metres per second along a wall lane: a ride entered off a dash (dash.speed 24) keeps its horizontal speed (wallRide.gravityMult 0.15 only slows the fall; wallRide.minSpeed is 8), so 22 with some loss at the contact. An ESTIMATE, not a Mover measurement: the bots clears check it.
budget.wallLaneSegmentPenalty_why: Seconds lost per wall jump that chains a ride past wallRide.maxTime (1.2 s): the pause of the jump and the re-contact.
budget.laneClear_why: Metres from a long wall that must stay free of boxes along a lane (the player's body plus the lean).

hazardFloor27._why: A floor strip that damages for a limited time (telegraph, live, spacing) so the wall lane is the safe route (GG: 'areas where you're forced to wall ride because the terrain might damage you temporarily'). Numbers under this row, each with a _why. Off (--off27): the strip is plain floor.
hazardFloor27.standHeight_why: Metres: feet at most this high above the floor are 'on' the strip; a wall rider (feet above it) is safe, which is what makes the wall lane the safe route. Unity-only.
hazardFloor27.tickSeconds_why: Damage lands in ticks of this many seconds (12 HP/s x 0.25 = 3 HP per tick) so the hurt event, the style reset and the HUD arrow fire 4 times a second, not 120.
hazardFloor27.telegraphSeconds_why: R1 starting values (the web had no floor hazard): 1.5 s of warning, 8 s live, 20 s from one start to the next (a 10.5 s break); each is a `test` number tuned by the harness line.
hazardFloor27.firstStartSeconds_why: The first telegraph starts this long after the player enters the room (so the room's first seconds show the strip safe, then warn).

pulse27._why: The PULSE GAUNTLET: a heavy swing every 2.5 s, five KILLS fill five pips (cap one stored charge), only a full charge enables the LT blast + a short self-boost (GG: 'the pulse needs to attack much slower ... after you charge it, after say killing five enemies, then you unlock the left trigger'). Off (--off27): NIGHT26's pulseLT (7 landed hits per notch).
pulse27.swingSeconds_why: The click swing's cooldown (GG: 'attack much slower'; NIGHT27 scope row 5: 2.5 s = 300 steps). The web's gauntlet.cycle is 0.42 s. Unity-only.
pulse27.damageMult_why: The heavy swing's damage as a multiple of weapons.gauntlet.damage (32 -> 192): 0.42 s / 2.5 s = 0.168, so x5.95 keeps the gauntlet's damage per second where NIGHT26 had it (the weapon-identity band, harness `weapons`); the swing lands as one big hit instead of six small ones. Unity-only.
pulse27.pips_why: Kills of yours (any weapon, and PulseCharge27.AddKill from the bosses' sentries) that fill the glove: 5 pips, one kill each (GG: 'after say killing five enemies'). Hits never fill them. The charge stored is capped at one full glove. Unity-only.
pulse27.blastCooldownSeconds_why: Seconds before the LT blast can go again (CORE.md: a movement / crowd-control verb needs a long cooldown, 15 s or longer). The pips can fill meanwhile; the blast waits. Unity-only.
pulse27.boostSeconds_why: The self-boost's length (NIGHT27 scope row 5: 0.4 s): the boost speed is added to your velocity along the aim in equal parts over these steps. Unity-only.
pulse27.boostSpeed_why: Total speed (m/s) the boost adds along the aim: about NIGHT24's second notch (design.n24.chargeFist.speed[1] 15.4), a lunge, not the full-notch 33. Unity-only; tuned by the harness `pulse27`.
pulse27.blastRange_why: m along the aim the LT blast reaches in front of you (the eye's line). Unity-only.
pulse27.blastRadius_why: m from the aim line within which a body is hit by the blast (a body's own radius is added): the same 1.5 m as design.n25.pulseCharge.radius. Unity-only.
pulse27.blastDamageMult_why: The blast's damage per body as a multiple of weapons.gauntlet.damage (64): a push with some bite, once each; the blast's own kills never refill the pips. Unity-only.

chargeShots27._why: RT held on the PISTOL and the SHOTGUN: a tap fires as today, a hold past a threshold charges and fires on release, with a long cooldown after a charged shot (GG: 'the pistol, when you hold the right trigger, it'll do a charge attack but it's on a longer cool down. Same thing with the shotgun'). Off (--off27): the normal shot only.
chargeShots27.holdSeconds_why: RT held this long (whole steps) on the pistol or the shotgun starts a charge; a tap fires at the press as today (NIGHT27 scope row 6). Unity-only.

revolver._why: The KESTREL's charged shot: a hold past holdSeconds charges for fullSeconds more, the release fires it: damageMult x a normal shot, through `pierce` bodies, then cooldownSeconds before the next charge (a normal shot is never blocked). Unity-only: the web has no charge shots.

shotgun._why: The THUNDERCLAP's charged blast: charge fullSeconds more after the hold, the release fires a normal pellet volley at damageMult x with a forward knock (knockMult x the gauntlet's), then cooldownSeconds. Unity-only.

boss1._why: Level 1's boss is THE LANTERN: a hovering shielded box whose shield is down only on the face that looks at a wall the player is riding (GG: 'the first boss fight is way too much like the Cerberus ... original, requires actual uses of our current gameplay mechanics'). Off (--off27): THE SLAG HULK. Core/Enemies/Lantern27.cs, Design/maps/lantern-arena.json (Tools/night/gen-lantern.py). Every number below is Unity-only (the web had no lantern); each group has its _why.
boss1.name: THE LANTERN

room._why: Where the courtyard sits in the world (the worm 400, MONOLITH -400, BULWARK 800, ELDER WYRM 1200, HULK 1600, GLACIER 2000), the run-seed salt, and the one soft point light (pale violet-white boundary tone, rule 8) over the ring.

arena._why: The courtyard's size as the sim reads it (Design/maps/lantern-arena.json: inner half-width 16 m = 32 m across, 12 m high): the orbs die at the inner wall.

hp._why: One pool; phases at 66 / 33 % (the worm's marks); the last finisherAt of it is the CORE: a gun lands x finisherGunMult there (a slow finish by guns, so the fight never waits on a charge), the PULSE x finisherPulseMult (the 5-kill charge's payoff). Pool tuned so the pistol bot with wall rides kills in 75-100 s (harness lantern).

body._why: The box hovers hoverY m up (a player on the floor shoots up at it, a player riding is level with it); half = its half size (2.4 m cube); turn1-3 rad/s: the plate turns to you SLOWLY, so a hop to the far lane opens a window while it catches up (slower each phase); introHold s: no damage while it rises; dieTime s the finisher.

shield._why: segments: the ring's eight wall segments (sector i = directions [i, i+1) x 45 deg from +x); grace s: the face stays lit this long after you leave the wall, for the shot already in the air (a ride lasts at most wallRide.maxTime 1.2 s).

orb._why: The slow readable orange orbs (red-orange: danger only): speed 9 m/s (the sprint is about 9), radius, damage 14, life s; the fan (three orbs, fanDeg apart) in phase 1, the ring (ringCount radial orbs at two heights, lowY jump / highY duck) from phase 2, the rain (rainCount orbs fall on decals of radius rainR from rainHeight at rainFall m/s, spread around you) from phase 3. Telegraph: the first attack of a fight 0.8 s, later 0.6 s (GG's brief). every1-3 s of rest between attacks, recover s after.

walls._why: Phase 3: every retractEvery s a run of retractCount neighbouring segments warns for retractTell s (floor decal) then drops for retractTime s: you chain rides around the ring along the ones that stay.

sentry._why: Phase 3 drops five small SENTRIES that orbit the ring (orbit m, speed rad/s, low / high m): their kills fill the PULSE's five pips (the teaching of the kill-charge). hp 40: two pistol shots.

boss2._why: Level 2's boss is THE GLACIER as a pulse-only chase on a curving ice course with the original body (GG: 'you can only attack him if you are able to catch up to him and hit him with the pulse'). Off (--off27): NIGHT26's glacier. Core/Enemies/Glacier27.cs. Every number below is Unity-only (the web had no glacier); each group has its _why.
boss2.name: THE GLACIER

course._why: The same 40 m ice tile as NIGHT26 (Design/maps/glacier-course.json: three lanes at x -7 / 0 / 7, low rails, wall lines), a window of windowBack tiles behind and windowAhead ahead of the player's, a checkpoint every 4 tiles. Straight in the SIM; the curve is view data (curve below).

room._why: Where tile 0 sits in the world (GLACIER 2000, LANTERN 2400), the run-seed salt, and the one light (pale violet-white boundary tone, rule 8) that follows the player along the course.

hits._why: THREE PULSE hits kill it (GG: only the pulse): the pool is split in thirds (the HP bar's two marks), whatever the swing's damage; no gun, and no hit outside the window, ever lands.

speed._why: THE GAP CONTROLLER (R2 rules 11-17): the boss's speed = baseFrac x top + clamp(k x (gap - targetGap), +-clampFrac x top). top m/s is the player's top speed on the ice (the sprint is about 9 and a boost strip adds 6); clampFrac 0.15: the controller never moves the boss more than 15 % of the player's top speed off its base, so it is catchable and never a timer. targetGap m is where it settles when you hold the line (targetStep m further each phase: it runs further ahead as the fight goes on; a player who runs PAST it meets its fastest speed); k m/s per metre of gap error. laneMove / laneEvery: how fast and how often it slides between lanes; introHold s: no attacks while it pulls away.

gap._why: The chase starts at gap.start m; a PULSE-READY window of windowTime s opens when the gap falls under windowAt m (GG's brief: 12 m, 1.5 s); a window that runs out costs missCost m of gap (the boss skates on) and NEVER health; armTime s before a window may open again; a hit surges the boss hitBack m ahead; at failAt m you go back to the last checkpoint (the boss keeps its hits).

launch._why: THE PULSE LAUNCH's lock-on: the launch itself reaches about 5 m (Fist24: 2.25 jump distances) while the window opens at a 12 m gap, so a launch released while the window is open, with the boss within reach m and the throw within coneDeg degrees of the line to it, LANDS (GG: 'a PULSE launch that lands on the boss counts'). refill: the kill pips a hit gives back (the pips fill only from kills and there are none on the ice: without it only one launch exists), so three launches win the chase.

tells._why: Every lane attack tells >= 0.6 s (a floor decal 0.75-0.8 s, GG's brief 0.7-0.8): the low bar (slide) and the sweeping bar (jump) 0.75 s, the roller 0.8 s (jump), the icicle fall 0.8 s (be in a wall column). Never two lethal attacks inside resolveGap.

attack._why: A lane attack is placed `ahead` m in front of the player (never beyond the boss) and lethal for `life` s after its tell; damage 12 of the player's 100 and a push back; `thick` m thick. Heights (m): the sweeping bar 0.45 (any jump), the low bar from 1.15 to 2.8 (slide). Phase 2 adds the ROLLER (a log rolling across the lanes at rollerSpeed m/s, rollerH m tall: jump it); phase 3 adds the ICICLE FALL (ceiling spikes icicleTop m tall over all but icicleSafe m of each wall: ride or hug the wall). every1-3 s between attacks per phase.

body._why: The skater's hit box: one large blocky body on one blade (GG: 'just switch back to the original [model] because it doesn't look good'; DECIDE27 D-3: the web's blocky enemy style, rebuilt as the web's models are), boxW x boxH x boxL m; dieTime s of finisher.

curve._why: The course bends in the VIEW only (Glacier27Curve; the sim and collider stay straight so golden and replays are untouched): each 40 m tile turns the heading by up to maxTurnDeg degrees (~22, from (run seed ^ salt, tile index)); tiles is the ring the view recycles. viewOn true: the tiles, the boss, the attacks and the camera bend (GlacierView.BendCamera), the sim stays straight.

slowAim27._why: View row: world time eases to a fraction while wall-riding AND aiming, with a screen cue (GG: 'if you aim a weapon while riding the game kind of temporarily slows down a little bit'). Read directly (no tape bit): the loop driver's accumulator dt only, never the sim.
slowAim27.scale_why: World time share at full slow-mo while wall-riding AND aiming. R1 range 0.65-0.85; the web has no slow-mo of this kind, so this is a Unity-only design number (a starting guess: GG's 'a little bit'), tuned by a paired blind frame set.
slowAim27.easeInS_why: Ease into the slow (R1 rule: 130 ms) so the drop never snaps.
slowAim27.easeOutS_why: Ease back to real time (R1 rule: 100 ms), a little quicker than the way in.
slowAim27.cueVignette_why: Vignette intensity at full slow (R1 rule: 0-0.25). The cue is one global Volume blended by slow01; a render number the web never had.
slowAim27.cueChroma_why: Chromatic aberration at full slow (R1 rule: 0-0.15). Render only.
slowAim27.cueSaturation_why: Colour-adjustments saturation at full slow (R1 rule: -15). Render only.
slowAim27.cueFovDeg_why: Extra vertical FOV at full slow (R1 rule: +4 deg), added after the camera feel. No border speed lines (GG banned them).

skate27._why: View row: the ice skate feel (speed FOV, roll, floor streaks, dust, blade trails) with no border streaks (GG: 'there's also no skate effect: I want it to feel like you're really dashing from right to left'). Render only: nothing here touches the sim; the numbers are R3 topic 2 starting guesses, tuned by the floor-pixel-motion measure and blind pairs.
skate27.fovMaxDeg_why: FOV added at 1.5 x run speed (R3: 0 at run speed to +10 at 1.5 x).
skate27.fovCapDeg_why: The skate FOV on top of the camera feel never exceeds base + this (R3 cap).
skate27.fovFullMult_why: Speed, in run speeds, at which the FOV add is full (R3: 1.5 x).
skate27.fovOutS_why: FOV ease out (R3: 0.4 s): a slow settle after a skate.
skate27.rollDeg_why: Camera roll at full lateral speed (R3: 4 deg), render only.
skate27.rollSlideDeg_why: Camera roll at full lateral speed in a slide (R3: 6 deg).
skate27.slideEyeDrop_why: Eye lowered in a slide, m (R3: 0.05-0.08), render only.
skate27.streakLinesPerM_why: Floor streak lines per metre across the travel direction (R3: 2.5).
skate27.streakWidth_why: Line width as a share of the line spacing cell (R3: 0.04 m).
skate27.streakScrollK_why: Scroll speed = player speed x this (R3: 0.3), so the lines slide under the feet.
skate27.streakLoShare_why: Share of top speed where the streaks start (strength 0).
skate27.streakHiShare_why: Share of top speed where the streaks are full (strength 1).
skate27.streakGain_why: Peak line brightness (additive, pale violet-white boundary tone).
skate27.dustCount_why: Ice dust motes near the feet (R3: 40-80).
skate27.dustRadius_why: Radius around the player the motes live in, m.
skate27.carveAngleDeg_why: A heading change above this in one step sprays the carve (R3: 60 deg).
skate27.trailLifeS_why: Blade trail life (R3: 0.25 s); two thin additive trails.
skate27.shakeRad_why: Camera shake amplitude at top speed, radians (R3: 0.002).

roof27._why: View row: a ceiling over every room and link of levels 1-3, vertex AO, emissive strips, gradient ambient + fog, a skylight slot over boss arenas (GG: 'there needs to be a roof ... almost like indoors'). Render only; the sim collider is untouched; the numbers are R3 topic 3 starting guesses.
roof27.ceilingAbove_why: Ceiling height above the tallest non-barrier box of EACH room, m (brief: plan max + 3; the Player reel n27-3 showed sky between lower walls and a level-wide ceiling, so each room closes at its own top + 1; lead 2026-10-09).
roof27.skirtHeight_why: A curtain this tall under each ceiling rect edge closes the gap above the walls (the barriers stand from y 14 on, so the door gaps stay open below it). Render only.
roof27.skirts_why: Curtains under the ceiling edges (skirtHeight). Off: the first version (n27-4) shut the view in black before the ceiling height ignored the walls outside the plan rect was fixed; turn on only after a Player frame shows them right. The ceiling alone closes the wall tops at +0.5 m.
roof27.atmosphere_why: The gradient ambient, the exponential fog and the tighter stone fog far. Off: reels n27-5 showed the whole frame flat violet in both the ON and OFF phases (global state, not the roof meshes); turn on only after a Player frame shows it right.
roof27.ceilingHex_why: Dusk-dark violet (0x33245a, about RGB 0.20 / 0.14 / 0.35 as displayed; the n27-3 reel read 0x1a1050 as near black) of the ceiling's underside; an unlit colour.
roof27.skylightShare_why: Share of a boss room's floor area left open as a skylight (brief: 20-30 %).
roof27.aoCorner_why: AO factor at an inside corner (brief 0.6).
roof27.aoEdge_why: AO factor along a convex edge (brief 0.8).
roof27.aoFalloff_why: Distance in m over which the AO eases back to 1.0 (brief 0.6 m). Baked as gradient vertex-colour strips because the stone mesh is a few huge quads with no vertices to carry AO.
roof27.stripMin_why: Fewest emissive ceiling strips in a room (brief 6-10).
roof27.stripMax_why: Most emissive ceiling strips in a room.
roof27.stripBrightness_why: HDR gain on the strip colour so bloom picks it up.
roof27.boundaryHex_why: Pale violet-white (0xd8d0ff) for boundary strips; cyan (colors.usable) marks the way on; red-orange is never used.
roof27.maxLights_why: Real point lights near the player, counting the room kit's two (brief: at most 4).
roof27.lightIntensity_why: Intensity of each of the two extra strip lights (times LightScale).
roof27.lightRange_why: Range of the strip lights, m.
roof27.fogDensity_why: Exponential-squared fog density indoors (the stone shader's own fog is tightened by fogFarScale).
roof27.fogFarScale_why: Scale on the stone fog's far distance indoors (the stone shader reads the _SkyFogParams global).

tutorial27._why: Level data row: the tutorial rebuilt so no stage repeats a lesson (GG: 'the tutorial section is fine but kind of repeats similar things').

n30._why: NIGHT30 (GG 2026-10-09, after his playtest of NIGHT29: clear weapon rules and a HUD that shows them, lava where pits lie, a circular Lantern that explains itself, glide ice and a level-2 boss that punishes distance, a Wyrm head-punch stagger, LEVEL 4, a gritty look with a HUD that buzzes). Every row is off in the shared commit and turned on only when its contract passes. Off (--off30 / -skygrindOff30, and every older off switch): NIGHT29's game bit for bit. Unity-only numbers each carry a _why (the web never had these systems).

levels._why: The rebuilt levels 1-4 (plans Design/levels/n30/*.plan.json, ids n30-*): while on, design.n25.curriculum.order points at them; off: the n29-* order. A view / flow row (no sim bit: the level a run loads is already on its tape).
levels.order_why: NIGHT30 (builder L): the CAMPAIGN's play order while this row is on (Core/Curriculum25.cs reads it in place of design.n25.curriculum.order): the rebuilt n30 levels, then levels 4-10 as before (n30-span is inserted when its map exists).

rules._why: Item 1, the weapon rules (DESIGN30 section A): one action at a time; a switch waits only for the ACTION in progress (a gun's shot cycle, the punch's swing), never for the whole cooldown; every cooldown (the guns, the gauntlet's heavy swing and its LT blast) runs while holstered. actionSeconds caps how long any action holds a switch (the punch's own punch.cycleTime 0.35 is the model; the web has no switch rule).

glide._why: Item 6a, ICE as a floor tag (R3: ULTRAKILL's gasoline floor; a slide keeps its entry speed and decays slowly): on an ice surface braking is very low, a dash ADDS speed up to a soft cap, a downhill adds speed, steering stays responsive. The numbers are builder S's first picks, replaced by a measured glide line (the web's ice only scales friction).
glide.decayPerSecond_why: The share of the speed an ice glide loses per second with no input, in place of the Mover's ground friction (R3: ULTRAKILL gasoline removes friction, a slide decays slowly; Quake friction 4 halves speed in 0.17 s). 0.12: from 16 m/s about 11 m/s after 3 s, so a glide carries across a room but does not run forever. Measured by glide30.
glide.dashAdd_why: m/s a dash begun on ice ADDS to its entry speed when it ends (scaled by 1 - entry / softCap, so it pays most when slow and nothing at the cap); the Mover alone ends a dash at max(walk, entry): no gain once fast. R3: pumping pays. Target (NIGHT30.md item 6): one dash on ice gains at least 20 %. Measured by glide30.
glide.softCap_why: m/s: above it the glide speed loses capDrag of the excess per second, and a dash adds nothing (R3: caps are soft and layered; ULTRAKILL slide caps at 3x base). 30 m/s is 3.75x walk, above the 24 m/s dash.
glide.capDrag_why: Per second, the share of the speed above softCap that a glide loses (a drag that bites gradually, not a wall: R3 pattern 4).
glide.slopeGain_why: x gravity along the ice floor's slope (the horizontal part of the floor normal points downhill): downhill adds speed, uphill bleeds it (R3: gravity is the accelerator; Tribes / Apex). 1 = the full gravity component.
glide.turnRateDeg_why: Degrees per second the glide turns the heading toward the move input at speed, the speed kept (R3 pattern 5: a TF-style slide steers at 1.8 rad/s = 103 deg/s; at speed the Mover's Quake acceleration cannot turn you at all). Measured by glide30.

lava._why: Item 3, LAVA not pits (R1: ULTRAKILL's lava burns without a teleport; D-6): a touch costs damageFraction of max health, knocks the player up by knockUp m/s, flashes hurtFlashSeconds, and cannot hurt again for graceSeconds; NO respawn (only a void fall respawns); an enemy that falls in burns and dies. The web has no lava.
lava.enemyBurnSeconds_why: Unity-only (the web has no lava): an enemy whose feet touch lava burns (event lavaEnemyBurn, a visible burn) for this long and then dies (lavaEnemyDeath), so it never vanishes silently; 0.8 s reads as a burn without the body lingering.
lava.touchMargin_why: Unity-only: the feet count as touching the lava at or below its surface y + touchMargin m (NIGHT30.md / DESIGN30: 0.05), so a body standing on the lava collider always reads as in it.
