lantern30._why: Item 4, THE LANTERN on a ring of flat panels (DESIGN30 C1 + the reviewer's fix: 16 panels of 22.5 degrees, the Mover's ride turns about 30 degrees at most): the orbs lead the rider, a sweep marks a panel ahead of the rider, platform shots do no damage, two lines teach the rule. Builder B adds its numbers with their _why.
lantern30.tellSeconds_why: The floor's tell before it goes live (DESIGN30 C1: R1's 1-1.5 s tell; Lantern29's 0.9 s read too short in GG's frames): replaces design.n29.boss1.tellSeconds while this row is on (the cycle's rest shortens by the same amount).
lantern30.leadSeconds_why: The fan orbs LEAD the rider: at the moment they fire they turn to the player's position leadSeconds ahead (position + velocity x leadSeconds), so circling at a steady speed is not safe (R1: the strafe circle is a named failure). 0.6 s is DESIGN30's first pick; the rider bot's kill band checks it.
lantern30.sweepEvery_why: Every sweepEvery-th live phase a SWEEP marks one wall panel ahead of the rider (DESIGN30 C1: every second live phase).
lantern30.sweepAheadPanels_why: How many panels ahead of the rider (in its direction round the ring) the sweep marks: a rider at 10-12 m/s covers about two 5.9 m panels in the 1.2 s tell, so the burn lands where it would be; it must jump the seam or drop to a platform.
lantern30.sweepTellSeconds_why: The sweep's red-orange mark before it burns (tells 1-1.5 s, never over 2 s: NIGHT30's boss rule).
lantern30.sweepBurnSeconds_why: How long the marked panel burns (DESIGN30 C1).
lantern30.sweepDamagePerSecond_why: Damage per second to a player within sweepReach of the burning panel, in the hazardFloor27 tick (0.25 s: 7.5 a tick, at most 45 over the whole burn): nothing kills in under 0.5 s.
lantern30.sweepReach_why: How far from the burning panel's face the burn reaches (a rider's capsule is 0.35 m from the wall; 1.5 m catches a rider and a player hugging it, not the platform's front edge 2.4 m out).
lantern30.platformScale_why: The share of a hit that lands from a shooter standing on a platform (DESIGN30 I-3: the platforms are a refuge from the lava, not a firing spot: 0 = no damage).
lantern30.lineSeconds_why: How long a teaching line stays up (the Lesson / boss-line code reads Lantern30.LineNow; event bossLine30).
lantern30.lineMaxShows_why: Each teaching line shows at most this many times per fight (NIGHT30 item 4).
lantern30.lineTell_why: The line on the floor's tell (GG's own words: 'including guidance like get above the lava').
lantern30.lineCore: RIDE THE WALL. SHOOT THE CORE.
lantern30.lineCore_why: The line when the core opens (DESIGN30 C1).
lantern30.platformOrbSeconds_why: A player standing on a platform this long gets a slow ARCING orb (DESIGN30 C1: the refuge is temporary, the threat that sends him back to the wall). The wait restarts when he steps off.
lantern30.platformOrbTellSeconds_why: The lob's landing spot is marked red-orange this long before it is thrown (tells 1-1.5 s, never over 2 s); the spot is where he stood when the tell began, so stepping aside dodges it.
lantern30.platformOrbFlightSeconds_why: The lob's flight from the lantern to the marked spot: slow enough to see it coming (the orb's own damage, design.n27.boss1.orb.damage 14).
lantern30.platformOrbGravity_why: The lob's fall (m/s^2) that bends it into an arc over the floor (the world's gravity is the player's; an orb has none of its own).
lantern30.rainInset_why: Phase 3's rain decals stay this far inside the ring's panel faces (the NIGHT27 clamp was a square, whose corners sit outside the ring).
lantern30.floorScale_why: Shots from the FLOOR land this share of Lantern29's light damage (DESIGN30 C1: light damage from the floor; the platform lands none, the wall in the open core lands full). Round 1's Player reel projected a floor camper at 143 s against a 66.6 s rider (under 3x); x0.5 doubles the camper's time (harness: see the commit).

arena._why: THE LANTERN RING (Core/Enemies/Lantern30Arena.cs, a triangle soup like Rink28Arena, at design.n27.boss1.room.origin): a closed ring of flat wall panels (the Mover's ride turns at most 30 deg per ride; seam30 measured a 22.5 deg and a 30 deg seam: the same ride survives both but bleeds to the 8 m/s ride floor, so neither is clean and the ring keeps DESIGN30 I-4's 16 panels), a closed roof, three platforms against the wall, three heat vents. Replaces the NIGHT27 square courtyard's boxes while design.n30.lantern30 is on.
arena.panels_why: 16 flat panels of 22.5 deg (DESIGN30 I-4; seam30: a 30 deg seam is not clean either).
arena.apothem_why: Centre to a panel's face: 30 m across (DESIGN30 C1: about 30 m), a panel 5.97 m wide.
arena.height_why: Floor to the closed roof (DESIGN30 C1: 14 m tall).
arena.platformTop_why: The platforms' top (DESIGN30 C1: 2.4 m; a running jump reaches about 3.15 m, so a player on the floor can climb one).
arena.platformDepth_why: How far a platform reaches out from its panel (DESIGN30 I-5: against the wall; a rider drops onto one from the lane).
arena.platformInset_why: The gap between a platform's ends and its panel's seams (the platform stays on one flat panel).
arena.platformPanels_why: The three platform panels at about the ring's thirds, none at the south entry (the player enters at panel 4's seam, 90 deg).
arena.laneLow_why: The wall-ride lane strip's bottom on each panel (DESIGN30 C1: y 2-6; a view strip: the whole panel is rideable).
arena.ventPanels_why: The three heat vents' directions (a vent sits in front of each of these panels): the view glows them through the floor's tell (they never glow for nothing: DESIGN30 B f12 question 6).
arena.ventRadius_why: How far from the centre the vents sit on the floor.

glacier30._why: Item 6, THE GLACIER rebuilt (DESIGN30 C2): a closed ice arena two to three times the rink, glide instead of snap lanes (SkateLane29 off on this path), distance punished by homing shards and a lane sweep. Builder B adds its numbers with their _why.
glacier30.farMeters_why: Distance is punished (DESIGN30 C2): a player farther than this (straight line, chest to the boss) fills the patience gauge. Measured (boss30 glacier): DESIGN30's guess of 22 m sat under the chase itself (the boss holds design.n28.glacier.speed.targetGap 48 m along the lap while the glove is ready), so the chaser was volleyed for chasing: 4-10 deaths, kills at 165-233 s; at 40 m the chaser is never far and the bank camper is still reached (out of sight behind the island, and the sweep).
glacier30.speedMult_why: The boss's pace on the bigger lap (x design.n29.boss2.speedMult): the 124 m lap is half again the old 84 m. Measured with the chaser lag bot (6 seeds): 0.80 -> median 63 s, 0.88 -> 80, 0.90 -> 74, 0.92 -> 95 (60-135), 0.95 -> 104 with one seed not killed in 240 s; 0.92 sits in the 80-130 s band (D-5).
glacier30.exposedScaleGlide_why: With builder S's glide on (design.n30.glide) the exposed window lands this share of NIGHT29's damage (the gauntlet's third, the guns' exposed fraction). Measured with the chaser lag bot (boss30 glacier, 6 seeds): glide makes the chase easy (x1.0 / 2.5 s: median 48 s); x0.5 / 2.5 s: 76 s; x0.35 / 2.0 s: 111 s (101-118), inside the 80-130 s band (D-5). Glide off: x1 (NIGHT29's).
glacier30.windowSecondsGlide_why: With glide on the exposed window lasts this long (design.n29.boss2.exposedSeconds 2.5 otherwise): a glider reaches the boss more often, so each catch is shorter.
glacier30.lineVolley: STAY CLOSE. DASH SIDEWAYS FROM SHARDS.
glacier30.lineVolley_why: The Glacier's teaching line on its first homing-volley tells (item 12: a boss explains its rule in at most two short lines on the first tell; the lead's words, through SurvivalSim.BossLine30's budget).
glacier30.hideSeconds_why: Out of the boss's sight (the world's ray from the boss to the player's chest blocked: the island, the bank's lip) this long also fills the gauge (DESIGN30 C2).
glacier30.fillSeconds_why: The gauge fills over this many seconds of far / hidden (DESIGN30 C2: 4 s), then the homing volley.
glacier30.drainMult_why: Back in reach the gauge drains this many times faster than it fills (closing in is rewarded quickly).
glacier30.volleyTellSeconds_why: The homing volley's tell (DESIGN30 C2: 0.8 s; the boss's tells 0.8-1.5 s).
glacier30.volleyCount_why: Shards in a homing volley, fanned over volleySpreadDeg.
glacier30.volleySpeed_why: The shards' speed (m/s): slower than a dash (a sideways dash out-turns them), faster than a run.
glacier30.turnDegPerSecond_why: How fast a shard turns toward the player (deg/s): a straight run is caught, a sideways dash is not (DESIGN30 C2: a sideways dash dodges).
glacier30.volleyLife_why: A shard's life (s); it also breaks on the world (the island, the walls).
glacier30.volleyDamage_why: Damage per shard (five shards: a volley that all lands costs half of a 100 HP player; none lethal under 0.5 s alone).
glacier30.volleyRadius_why: A shard's hit radius (m) against the player's capsule.
glacier30.volleySpreadDeg_why: The volley's fan half-angle (deg) at the throw.
glacier30.sweepEverySeconds_why: A lane-wide frost sweep aimed at the player every 9 s (DESIGN30 C2), whatever the distance: nowhere on the ice is out of reach.
glacier30.sweepFirstSeconds_why: The first sweep comes this long into the fight (the opening chase reads first).
glacier30.sweepTellSeconds_why: The sweep's band is marked this long before it goes live (tells 1-1.5 s).
glacier30.sweepLiveSeconds_why: The band is live this long: one hit (sweepDamage) and the frost's bite (design.n29.boss2.frostSlow) to a player in it.
glacier30.sweepWidth_why: The band's width across the rink (m), centred on the player's lateral position when the tell starts: a glide sideways out of it dodges.
glacier30.sweepHalfLength_why: The band reaches this far either side of the player along the lap (m): braking or racing ahead 8 m also dodges.
glacier30.sweepHeight_why: The band reaches this high above the floor under the player (m): a jump over it dodges too.

rink._why: THE GLACIER's closed rink rebuilt bigger (DESIGN30 C2: two to three times the 28 x 52 rink): numbers here replace design.n28.rink's (Rink28Params.From(cfg, over)); the outer half-width is islandRadius + laneWidth + bankRun + lip = 22 m and the length straight + 2 x 22 = 70 m: 44 x 70 (2.2x the area). The banks stay inside the closed rim and the boss's reach (the volley, the sweep).
rink.straight_why: The straights' length (m): 70 m end to end.
rink.islandRadius_why: The central island (m): a bigger sight blocker, so hiding behind it is a choice the gauge punishes.
rink.islandHeight_why: The island is taller than a standing player's eye (it blocks the boss's sight).
rink.laneWidth_why: The flat ice lane (m): room to glide and to dodge a 4 m sweep band sideways.
rink.centreRadius_why: The lap's centre line (the island's edge + half the lane): where the boss runs.
rink.bankRun_why: The bank's run (m) at the rink's 28 deg: a 2.4 m speed ramp inside the rim.
rink.doorWidth_why: The island's doors (m): the cut stays.
rink.rimHeight_why: The rim wall up to the lid (m).

wyrm30._why: Item 7, the KILN WYRM head-punch stagger (D-8): a gauntlet hit on the head in the last windowSeconds of a charge: hitstopSteps of hitstop, bonusMult damage, a recoilSeconds recoil, then a different attack. The web's worm has no stagger.
wyrm30.recoilBack_why: How far the staggered head recoils, away from the player along the ground (m): the recoil arc's end, clamped inside the room (D-8: the head lodges backward and the body coils back).
wyrm30.recoilUp_why: How high the recoil arc lifts the head at its middle (m): a knockback ARC, not a slide.
wyrm30.headReachMargin_why: The swing counts as ON THE HEAD when the head's box is within weapons.gauntlet.range plus this margin of the eye (the swing already picked the worm; this tells the head from the body).
wyrm30.laneMargin_why: How far off the head's line of travel the player may stand and still be 'charged at' (m, beyond the head's half-width and the capsule's radius): the window opens only for a charge that will hit him.
wyrm30.lateSeconds_why: The window stays open this long past the predicted contact (the contact cooldown's first step: a punch in the same step as the touch still counts).
wyrm30.linePunch_why: The Wyrm's teaching line on its first punchable windows (item 12; through SurvivalSim.BossLine30's budget).

span._why: Item 10, LEVEL 4 THE SPAN (D-3): the ARCLINE grapple in a campaign level (grapple nodes as plan rows; the swing keeps design.n21.arcline's 0.4 s, only the yank its 15 s), the NAILGUN award, THE LOOM. Builder S / B add their numbers with their _why.

loom._why: THE LOOM (DESIGN30 C4 / D; Core/Enemies/Loom30.cs): LEVEL 4's boss in room s8, a blocky crane-spider under the span's deck, four legs gripping the deck's corners (the plan's loomLegs), two joints a leg that are grapple nodes; nails land in full on a joint while you hang on that leg's line or stand by the joint, lightScale elsewhere; its first attack CUT plucks the line you hang on. First pass: the numbers are first picks (no kill band measured yet).
loom.name: THE LOOM
loom.pool_why: Hit points (x the fight's hp scale). Measured with boss30 loom's lag bot (a scripted model: hang on a leg, nails at its joints with a 0.6 hit chance and the nailgun's heat, a 0.35 s reaction to the CUT tell, 15 % of tells missed; 6 seeds): kills at 103.5-115.1 s, median 111, inside the 90-150 s band (D-5) at 2400.
loom.bodyDrop_why: The body hangs this far under the deck's surface (m): under the span, its top just below the deck.
loom.bodyHalfW_why: The body's half width (m): an 8 m block.
loom.legHalf_why: With no loomLegs in the plan, the grips sit at the deck's centre +- this (m): L's 18 x 18 deck.
loom.kneeOut_why: The knee joint stands this far OUT past its grip, over the lava ring (m): the leg arches over the deck's edge.
loom.kneeUp_why: The knee joint's height over the deck (m): near L's static nodes at y 12, so a swing from one reaches it.
loom.hipOut_why: The hip joint stands this far OUT past its grip (m), just beyond the deck's edge.
loom.hipDrop_why: ...and this far UNDER the deck (m): over the lava, so only a swing reaches it; from the deck's edge it is more than fullReach away (the harness prints the distance).
loom.jointRadius_why: A joint's hit sphere (m): the nails' target.
loom.fullReach_why: Standing within this of a joint (m, chest to joint) also lands full damage on it (DESIGN30 D: within 3 m).
loom.lineReach_why: The rope's anchor within this of a leg (m: its grip, knee, hip, the body's side) counts as hanging on that leg's line.
loom.lightScale_why: The share that lands on a joint off its line, and on the body (DESIGN30 D: light damage 0.2 elsewhere).
loom.cutFirstSeconds_why: The first CUT can come this long after the intro (the first swings read first).
loom.cutEverySeconds_why: After a cut (or a dodged one) the next waits this long; it only tells while you hang on a rope.
loom.cutTellSeconds_why: The red tell on your line before it is plucked (DESIGN30 D: a 1.0 s tell; tells 1-1.5 s).
loom.cutDropSpeed_why: The plucked line drops you at this downward speed (m/s), half your swing's horizontal speed kept: grab another node.
loom.introHold_why: No damage and no cut for this long after it rises (its intro card).
loom.legThick_why: The legs' box thickness (m; the view's).
loom.lineStart: HANG ON A LEG. NAIL THE JOINTS.
loom.lineStart_why: The Loom's teaching line when its fight starts (item 12; through SurvivalSim.BossLine30's budget).
loom.sweepFirstSeconds_why: The first SWEEP can come this long after the intro.
loom.sweepEverySeconds_why: After a sweep the next waits this long; it only tells at a player standing on the deck (what stops a player standing there forever: DESIGN30 D).
loom.sweepTellSeconds_why: The leg's red mark across the deck before it sweeps (DESIGN30 D: a 1.2 s tell).
loom.sweepLiveSeconds_why: The sweeping leg crosses the deck (grip to the far corner, about 25 m) in this long: about 17 m/s, slow enough to see it come and jump it.
loom.sweepBarHalf_why: The bar's half width (m) along its travel: it hits a low player only where it is now, so a jump timed over it clears it (harness: a jumper at 4 m is not hit).
loom.sweepHeight_why: The bar's height over the deck (m), shin height: a standing jump's feet peak at 1.18 m (harness), so a jump timed about 0.35 s before the bar clears it; a grapple off the deck too.
loom.sweepDamage_why: The sweep's one hit (x the fight's damage scale): a fifth of a 100 HP player; nothing kills in under 0.5 s.
loom.sweepKnock_why: It knocks a hit player outward at this speed (m/s), toward the deck's edge and the lava: the deck is no place to stand.
loom.sweepUp_why: ...and up at this speed (m/s), so the knock is an arc, not a slide.

teach._why: Item 12 + P0 b / d: the lesson line clears when its room is left or cleared and never shows in a boss fight; a boss explains its rule in at most two lines on the first occurrence of its tell, each at most maxShows times per fight. The web has no lessons.

hud30._why: View only (item 2 + P0 c / e / f): the weapon-state widget (READY / COOLING / CHARGING with a ring and a word), run rows hidden on TITLE / PAUSE / RESULTS, the layout pass. Unity-only view numbers live in UnityTuning.*30.cs.

look30._why: View only (item 8, D-4): HUD scanlines / flicker / glow / buzz (an accessibility off switch), the world quantise + Bayer dither (subtle), pixel block off by default, the Lantern's full-frame wash removed. Unity-only view numbers live in UnityTuning.*30.cs.

n31._why: NIGHT31 (GG 2026-10-10, after his playtest of NIGHT30: 'not a fan of a lot of the bosses', the grapple 'doesn't pull you in', the level-2 boss 'boring, you can camp', the charge shot gone, LT must do something on every weapon, level 1 the pistol only and one weapon per level). Every row is off in the shared commit and turned on only when its contract passes. Off (--off31 / -skygrindOff31, and every older off switch): NIGHT30's game bit for bit. Unity-only numbers each carry a _why (the web never had these systems). Design: Design/levels/DESIGN31.md.

grapplePull._why: Item 1 (DESIGN31 B, D-3): a TAP of the grapple pulls you in (Arcline21's zip on a node or surface: straight at it, rope taut, released at the web's arcline.zip.arrive with the speed kept plus an upward pop); a HOLD is NIGHT30's swing. The web's grapple pulls only toward a hooked big enemy. Builder G adds its numbers with their _why.
grapplePull.speed_why: m/s, the pull-in speed written on the Mover's config.arcline.zip.reelSpeed for a run with the block on (the way Arcline21Rules.Apply writes the zip numbers; golden vectors never hook). GUESS (DESIGN31 B): the web's enemy zip is 34; R2 cites ULTRAKILL's whiplash at about 60 u/s; MEASURED (harness grapple31 B, the press to 30 m of path): 34 m/s 0.942 s, 44 m/s 0.742 s, 60 m/s 0.558 s; 44 and stays under the swing's horizontal clamp (arcline.softCap 42 x 1.2 = 50.4), so the speed kept at the release is the pull's.
grapplePull.tapWindow_why: s: the grapple button up within this time after the press that fired the hook = a TAP (the pull-in); still held = the NIGHT30 swing. GUESS (DESIGN31 B); the hook itself flies 0.06-0.1 s (arcline.hookMin / hookMax), so a tap usually comes up while the hook flies or just after it bites. To check against real pad trigger taps (DESIGN31 R9).
grapplePull.arrivePop_why: m/s added upward to the velocity when a pull lets go at the anchor (the Mover's "zip" release at arcline.zip.arrive 2.6 m; the speed is kept), so a pull to a ledge or a node clears it. GUESS (R2: 4-6).
grapplePull.arriveKeepMax_why: m/s: the HORIZONTAL speed kept after a pull lets go at its anchor (the Mover's own "zip" release), clamped from outside the Mover before the arrival pop; 0 = no clamp. Unity-only (the web's enemy zip kept everything; the web had no pull-in). Why: builder L's harness pull31 (round 3) measured that with the full carry (42-51 m/s) every level-4 gap was crossed by ONE tap from the door (s2 landed at the north wall, s3 at lz 35.6 past the gap's end at 22, s6 past the deck). MEASURED (pull31 and grapple31 at 10 / 12 / 16: see NIGHT31 G round 3): 12, about a dash, drops you short of s3's gap after its first node so the second node is the chain. A cancel BEFORE the arrival (a jump, a dash, a second press) keeps the whole speed: the skilful line.

charge._why: Item 2a (DESIGN31 A, D-4): the charge shot (design.n27.chargeShots27's rules) back on the KESTREL (pierces) and the THUNDERCLAP (slug) with re-picked charge and cooldown times (R3: ULTRAKILL's piercer about 0.5 s charge, 2.5 s cooldown; n27 had 10 s / 14 s). Builder W adds its numbers with their _why.
charge.holdSeconds_why: RT held this long (whole steps) on the KESTREL or the THUNDERCLAP starts a charge; a tap fires at the press as today (DESIGN31 A, NIGHT27's 0.4 s).
charge.autoReleaseSeconds_why: P0 a: a FULL charge still held this long fires itself (NIGHT27 waited for a release forever, so a held trigger killed nothing: the smoke's virtual pad and the attract bot failed). Long enough to aim a full charge, short enough that holding RT never stalls the gun more than hold + charge + this (1.4 s on the KESTREL). Guess, logged.
charge.knockHusksOnly_why: R7 (the 15 s crowd-control rule): the slug's forward knock acts on husks only, never a boss (a knock on a husk is the gun's own hit, as the THUNDERCLAP's volley already knocks).
charge.meleeCancels_why: R8 (the w29 fire / melee lockout): a melee press while a charge builds cancels it, nothing spent.

comboNails._why: Item 2c (DESIGN31 A, the cross-weapon combo; R3: ULTRAKILL's coin and core): a charged KESTREL shot that passes through a body carrying stuck NAILGUN nails detonates them at mult x the nails' detonate damage (the nails go off before the shot's own hit, so they also go off on a kill). Its own switch inside n31.charge (cut first); 1.5 is a guess.

revolver._why: The KESTREL's charged shot (DESIGN31 A): charge fullSeconds after the hold, the release (or autoReleaseSeconds at full) fires damageMult x a normal shot through `pierce` bodies (NIGHT30's numbers), then cooldownSeconds before the next charge (a normal shot is never blocked). fullSeconds 0.5 from R3 (ULTRAKILL's piercer about 0.5 s); cooldown 4 s a guess (R3 piercer 2.5 s, NIGHT27 10 s).

shotgun._why: The THUNDERCLAP's charged blast (DESIGN31 A): charge fullSeconds after the hold, the release fires the pellet volley at damageMult x with a forward knock (knockMult x the gauntlet's; husks only, R7), then cooldownSeconds. 0.7 s and 6 s are guesses (NIGHT27 0.8 s / 14 s).
shotgun.slug_why: DESIGN31 A: the charged THUNDERCLAP is a SLUG: one pellet line along the aim (no spread), the first body before a wall takes a whole volley's damage (pellets x pellet damage) x damageMult (3) with the forward knock x knockMult (husks only, R7). false: NIGHT27's charged pellet volley.

ltAlways._why: Item 2b (DESIGN31 A, D-8): every weapon's LT does something at every moment: the gauntlet's LT before its five pips is a parry that returns a projectile (no crowd control: no 15 s cooldown needed). Builder W adds its numbers with their _why.
ltAlways.parryWindowSeconds_why: The gauntlet's LT parry before its five pips (DESIGN31 A, R6): for this long a spitter glob or a drone orb within the punch's reflect reach (the web's orb.reflectRange 2 m) goes back at its shooter at the web's orb.reflectDamageMult (x2). Guess, logged.
ltAlways.parryCooldownSeconds_why: After a parry press the gauntlet's LT shows COOLING with seconds for this long (R6). A parry moves no enemy, so it is not crowd control (no 15 s rule). Guess, logged.
ltAlways.nailgunZoom_why: R6: the NAILGUN's LT zooms this much while no nail is stuck (design.zoom.nailgunMag's 1.25) and detonates once one is (the slot label ZOOM / DETONATE). design.n26.weapons.nailgun.zoom 0 had left LT without a zoom.
ltAlways.shotgunZoom_why: The THUNDERCLAP's LT zoom (design.n25.shockwaveOff.zoom's 1.25; no shockwave: GG removed it in NIGHT25).
ltAlways.wordSeconds_why: How long the slot shows an LT word that answers a press (PARRY, COOLING): long enough to read at a glance. View timing for the HUD, kept here beside the rule it reports.

unlocks._why: Item 3 (DESIGN31 A, D-1 as the lead changed it): level 1 the KESTREL only; level 2 awards the PULSE gauntlet (room i1); level 3 the THUNDERCLAP; level 4 the NAILGUN; the fist is always there. Off: NIGHT30's start (KESTREL + gauntlet).

start._why: The weapons every campaign level starts with before the earlier levels' awards (Core/Unlocks26.cs Unlocks31.StartFor): the KESTREL only. The fist melee is not a weapon slot and is always there. Off: unlocks.json's start (KESTREL + gauntlet) plus the profile's cleared levels.

levels._why: One row per level id (the NIGHT30 plan ids first; the NIGHT29 and old ids carry the same order so either curriculum works): level n starts with start.weapons plus the `earns` of every level with a smaller n. A row with `room` awards its weapon when that room is entered (Campaign24.Award31: weaponEarned once; a pickup of the same weapon in that room is then taken without a second award). A row without `room` earns as NIGHT30 did (the plan's room award or pickup, else the level's last room through unlocks.json).

n32._why: NIGHT32 (GG 2026-10-10, after playing NIGHT31: 'the bosses have way too much health', 'you can barely hit them', 'you should defeat [them] in like a minute', 'you can just spam the grapple', 'the arenas are so boring', 'the 5th level', 'the 4th level completely overhauled again', 'new arenas on existing levels', 'the first boss fight arena ... needs to be a circle'). Every row is off in the shared commit and turned on only when its contract passes. Off (--off32 / -skygrindOff32, and every older off switch): NIGHT31's game bit for bit. Unity-only numbers each carry a _why (the web never had these systems). Design: Design/levels/DESIGN32.md; research: Research/2026-10-10-wave32/.

bosses32._why: Builder B (DESIGN32 B): every boss dies in about a minute for an average player (band 45-75 s, measured by a seeded sweep and the Player); the identity mechanic becomes a big damage bonus, never the only way to deal damage; no zero-damage state longer than 1.5 s; every hit deals at least 25 % chip; hurtboxes at least 1.3x the model. Builder B adds its numbers with their _why.
bosses32.retune_why: 2026-10-10 20:10 (GG: 'bosses still too tanky!'; Player pilots 47.7 / 56.6 / 76.3 s were near-perfect-aim bot times): new band, pilot p50 25-40 s, p90 <= 45 s, pistol+fist <= 90 s. hpMult lantern 4.7 -> 2.4 (pool 1231), stag 1.15 -> 0.52 (936), wyrm 1.0 -> 0.51 (3063) with gunScale 0.55 -> 0.8 (the worm dies only while surfaced: kill times come in steps of about 6 s), loom 0.7 -> 0.38 (912). The per-number _why lines below keep the 45-75 s history.
bosses32.convention_why: Each boss:`chip` (or the boss's own gun share) is what every hit lands outside the identity window, at least 0.25 (DESIGN32 B: every hit from every weapon in every state deals at least 25 %); `open` is what a hit lands inside the window, open / chip = x2.5 (D-4); window seconds at least max(3, the PULSE's 2.5 s cooldown + 0.75) = 3.25; `hpMult` scales the NIGHT31 pool of each new fight (after NIGHT29's cut). The web never had these bosses: Unity-only numbers, tuned on `boss32 <boss> --seeds 20` (Tools/SimHarness).

lantern.enabled_why: THE LANTERN takes this row's numbers (off: NIGHT31's rule, the other bosses unchanged).
lantern.hpMult_why: THE LANTERN's pool x this (NIGHT31: 1800 x 0.285 = 513, which the rider pilot killed in 19.8 s with 3 breaks but a player with no break could not kill in 200 s): 2257 here, because every hit now lands at least 40 %; sweep (20 seeds, the rider pilot): 3.0 with 6 s open gave p50 34.3 s, 3.6 with 4 s gave 37.6 s, 4.4 with 3.25 s gave p50 46.8 s / p90 49.0 s (Player n32-r2: 45.8 s); with the clamp carry-over (slice 7) 4.4 gave 45.2 s, so 4.7 (pool 2411) gives p50 48.9 s / p90 50.9 s (the pilot breaks the shield often: kept near the band's low edge so a weaker player stays near a minute).
lantern.chip_why: Every hit outside the open core (floor, air, wall ride) lands 40 % (NIGHT31: 1.8-3.6 %).
lantern.platformChip_why: From a platform a hit lands 40 % too (NIGHT31: 0, GG's 'sometimes they can't even take damage in areas').
lantern.open_why: The charged-KESTREL shield break opens the core: hits land 100 % (x2.5 over the chip).
lantern.coreOpenSeconds_why: The open core lasts 3.25 s (NIGHT31: 4; A1 proposed 6, but then the rider pilot spent most of the fight in the window and the pool had to grow past what a no-break player can chip down in 150 s). The rule's floor: max(3, the PULSE's 2.5 s + 0.75).
lantern.rideGraceSeconds_why: A charged shot within 1.2 s of leaving the wall still breaks the shield (NIGHT31: 0.6).
lantern.finisherGun_why: The last 18 % takes guns at 100 % (NIGHT27's finisher cut guns to 0.4 for a PULSE level 1 does not have).
lantern.camp_why: The anti-camp strike (the lead 20:13: punish stillness, not tankier bosses; Lantern31.Camp32): a player slower than campStillSpeed m/s for campStillSeconds gets a strike at his spot after campTellSeconds (event lantern31 campTell / camp), campDamage within campRadius m, then campEverySeconds before the next. At the 30 s pools the edge and far campers took 50 % of the bar before the lava floor killed them.

stag.enabled_why: THE STAG takes this row's numbers (off: NIGHT31's rule).
stag.hpMult_why: THE STAG's pool x this (NIGHT31: 1800; here 2070, because every hit now lands at least 40 %): sweep (StagPilot31, not seeded): A1's 0.722 gave 34.1 s, 1.05 gave 46.6 s, 1.15 gives 53.5 s.
stag.chip_why: Every hit outside the open back lands 40 % (NIGHT31: 5 %).
stag.open_why: Any hit from behind on the open back, and a charged KESTREL shot on a crystal, lands 100 % (x2.5 over the chip; NIGHT31: only the PULSE from behind, and a crystal hit was 5 %).
stag.hitScale_why: The shot's box, head sphere and crystal spheres x1.3 (DESIGN32 B: hurtboxes at least 1.3x the model; Boss31View draws the torso at the box's own width and length, so it was 1.0x). The body's movement and charge box is unchanged. Kept at 1.0: at 1.3 the bank-top camper's PULSE reached from farther and took 60 % of the bar (camp32 RED) while the pilot's time did not move (27.8 s); the lead decides between the 1.3x rule and the camp rule.
stag.openSeconds_why: The back stays open 3.25 s after a miss (NIGHT31: 2.5; at least the PULSE's 2.5 s cooldown + 0.75 s).
stag.crystalRegrowSeconds_why: A broken crystal regrows in 8 s (NIGHT31: 15).
stag.camp_why: The anti-camp (the lead 20:13): still 1.25 s (NIGHT31 2) brings the charge and the shards; a shard volley every 1.5 s (2.5) at a still, far or off-ice player, 14 a shard (9).
stag.stillSpeed_why: Slower than 2 m/s counts as still (NIGHT31 1: a camper walking back to its spot after a knock was never still).

wyrm.enabled_why: THE KILN WYRM takes this row's numbers (off: NIGHT31's rule).
wyrm.hpMult_why: THE KILN WYRM's pool x this (NIGHT31: 7800 x 1.1 x 0.7 = 6006, kept): the pool was never the problem, the 3 % gun share was. Sweep (WyrmPilot31, 20 seeds): A1's 0.357 gave p50 38.2 s with 0 staggers (the bonus never used), 0.55 gave 38.3 s, 0.78 gave 37.4 s (the kill waits for the worm to surface: times come in steps), 1.0 gives p50 50.8 s / p90 57.0 s.
wyrm.gunScale_why: Outside a stagger every hit lands 55 % x the part (the body's x0.5 makes 27.5 %, over 25 % after the boss's rounding of a KESTREL hit; the head x2 makes 110 %; NIGHT31: 3 %).
wyrm.open_why: While staggered every weapon lands 125 % x the part (x2.5 over the chip; NIGHT31: only the THUNDERCLAP and the PULSE, 100 %).
wyrm.staggerSeconds_why: The stagger lasts 4 s (NIGHT31: 2.5; at least the PULSE's cooldown + 0.75 s).
wyrm.aggroCooldown_why: A punchable aggro charge every 5 s (NIGHT31: 6).
wyrm.slugMinDamage_why: The slug fires as weapon 'shotgun' (one hit of the whole volley, 624 before the part share); a shotgun hit of at least 200 after the part share is the slug (a pellet is at most about 105 on the core), so design.n31.wyrm31.slugMult finally applies.
wyrm.maxHitFrac_why: One staggered hit takes at most 15 % of the pool: with the slug x2 working, a staggered slug on the head was 624 x 2 x 2 x 1.25 = 3120 (two thirds of the bar), so one stagger decided the fight and the kill time jumped by seeds.
wyrm.camp_why: The anti-camp (the lead 20:13): still 2 s (NIGHT31 3) brings the spit, a volley every 2 s (3), 16 a glob (10).

loom.enabled_why: THE LOOM takes this row's numbers (off: NIGHT31's rule).
loom.hpMult_why: THE LOOM's pool x this (NIGHT31: 2400; here 1680). Sweep (the lag bot, 20 seeds): 0.5 gave p50 47.5 s, 0.6 56.8 s (but corner THUNDERCLAP campers at 40 % took the whole bar), 0.8 with other guns 25 % 73.8 s, 0.7 with the hips moved gives p50 63.1 s / p90 66.8 s.
loom.otherScale_why: The KESTREL and the THUNDERCLAP land 25 % (NIGHT31: 1 %; the rule's floor: at 40 % a point-blank THUNDERCLAP from a deck corner killed the Loom in 10 s).
loom.nailLightScale_why: The NAILGUN and the PULSE away from a joint's reach land 50 % (NIGHT31: 12 %); a joint in reach or on the roped leg lands 100 % (x2).
loom.fullReach_why: Full damage on a joint within 7.5 m of the chest (NIGHT31: 6; the hips from a deck corner were 6.02 m).
loom.hipOut_why: m past the deck corner the hip hangs over the lava (NIGHT31: 6): with the hip 7 m from a corner camper a point-blank THUNDERCLAP at 25 % still took 63-72 % of the bar before the camper fell; at 8 m it is out of the 7.5 m reach from the deck and in the shotgun's falloff, and a player roped to that leg (under its knee) is 5 m from it.
loom.hipUp_why: m above the deck the hip hangs: 4.2 = 5 m over the lava (y -0.8), in sight from the deck and in reach from the rope (NIGHT31: 1.5).
loom.jointRadius_why: Each joint's hit sphere radius in m (NIGHT31: design.n30.span.loom.jointRadius 1, drawn by Boss30View as a 2 x r x 0.8 = 1.6 m cube, so the hit was 1.25x the drawing; BossMarks32's open shell drew 2.9 m, bigger than the hit). 1.3 m: a 2.6 m sphere; the drawing grows with it (Boss30View reads the same radius), so the 1.3x rule needs Boss30View's 0.8 at 0.75 (UnityTuning.Loom30JointScale: the lead's patch Tools/night/n32b-loomjoint.cjs).
loom.hangSeconds_why: Hanging on the Loom 4 s before the shake (NIGHT31: 3).
loom.camp_why: The anti-camp (the lead 20:13): grounded 2 s (NIGHT31 3) calls the flyer drop, a 0.8 s tell (1), 35 damage (25), 1.5 s before the next (2).

grapple32._why: Builder G (DESIGN32 G, D-1): the grapple has charges (2, each back after a recharge; a minimum gap between pulls; a non-boss kill gives one back); tap-pull and hold-swing both spend one. NIGHT31's pull cooldown was 0.4 s, so it could be chained forever (harness grapple32 --off32: the span TAP bot fired 38 hooks in 20 s, airborne 19.9 s). The rule is Game/SurvivalSim.Grapple32.cs (outside the Mover; Mover.cs untouched).
grapple32.charges_why: Hooks in hand (a tap-pull and a hold-swing each spend one when the hook fires; a press with no target spends nothing). D-1: 2 (M2: Apex Pathfinder / Titanfall / Doom Eternal's meathook are one or two uses on a clock; A1 suggested 2).
grapple32.rechargeSeconds_why: s for ONE spent charge to come back (one at a time; landing does not refill). D-1: 4, the middle of M2's 2 / 6 s and A1's 2 / 3 s with a landing refill. The contract (NIGHT32.md): a spam bot gets 2 pulls, then one per 4 s (plus kills).
grapple32.minGapSeconds_why: s: at least this long between two hooks fired, whatever the charges (D-1: 0.8; NIGHT31's only gate was the web's 0.4 s rope cooldown). A press inside it is cleared and spends nothing.
grapple32.cancelKeepMax_why: m/s: the speed kept when a jump (in the air), a dash or a second press lets go of a pull's attached rope (clamped before the Mover's release; the release's own x1.08 rising boost and jump-up still apply; a dash out of a pull is a plain dash, max(24, entry)). D-1: 20. A1: a cancel kept 44-47 m/s and skipped the 12 m/s arrival cap: the endless chain.
grapple32.range_why: m: the hook's reach for a run with the row on, written on the Mover's config.arcline.range (GrappleAim's nodes, rays and enemy pick read it); the web's 60 comes back with the row off. D-1 / DESIGN32 G: 40.
grapple32.killRefill_why: A kill of a non-boss enemy (the 'kill' event, kind not in bossKinds) gives one charge back (D-1), so fighting feeds the grapple.
grapple32.bossKinds_why: Kill kinds that give no charge back (the bosses: BossKit's 'boss', the Bulwark, the campaign bosses, THE CROWN, RIVAL).
grapple32.tapNodesOnly_why: D-3: a TAP pulls only to a node (a ring, a boss joint) or a big enemy (the ARCLINE's zip), never to a bare wall (A1: any wall in 60 m was a target); a tap on a wall lets go and gives the charge back. A HOLD still swings from a wall (it spends one).

balance32._why: Builder G (DESIGN32 G2): the combat balance pass outside the bosses (weapon damage per second parity, room enemy health and counts, damage taken, health drops), each change measured by a harness table. Builder G adds its numbers with their _why.

arenas32._why: Builder A (DESIGN32 A): boss 1's arena a true circle (64 wall segments; floor, wall and collider), and new or rebuilt arenas on levels 1-3 (smaller, vertical, a hazard edge, an enemy climb route, every room a loop). Builder A adds its numbers with their _why.
arenas32.levelSwap_why: Curriculum25.N32Levels: while this row is on, each level id here is swapped for its rebuilt file ({old id: new id}); builder A fills it (e.g. n30-foundry: n32-foundry).
arenas32.facetsPerPanel_why: Lantern30Arena (read only while this row is on): each of the ring's 16 logical panels (the fight's sections: sweep, vents, platforms) is drawn and collided as this many flat facets, so the wall is a 64-gon with 5.6 deg seams (the Mover's ride corner rule is 30 deg; harness ring32 measures the speed kept over a wall-ride lap against NIGHT31's 16 flat panels). The web never had the ring (a Unity-only arena), so it has no such number.

span32._why: Builder S (DESIGN32 S): level 4 rebuilt from scratch around the limited grapple (small rooms, ring routes that need a charge plan, wall rides between pulls). Builder S adds its numbers with their _why.
span32.levelSwap_why: Curriculum25.N32Levels: while this row is on, n30-span is swapped for builder S's rebuilt level 4 ({old id: new id}).

level5._why: Builder F (DESIGN32 F): level 5, the finale: every verb and all four weapons, remixed rooms, a gauntlet, then the boss arena (a true circle). LEVEL 5 THE SPIRE (Design/levels/n32-spire.json from Tools/night/gen-n32-spire.cjs): v1 threshold, v2 FOUNDRY FLOOR (the lava wall lane), v3 ICE GLIDE, v4 landing, v5 KILN VENTS (aimed pads), v6 RING SPAN (rings for the 2-charge grapple), v7 landing, v8 THE GAUNTLET, v9 THE CROWN (boss id crown, builder C's arena; with design.n32.boss5 off the room clears on entry). While on: the level is inserted after n30-span, the level select has 5 playable slots (UnityTuning.LevelSel32Level5Playable). The weapons come from design.n31.unlocks (row n 5: all four from the start; the level earns the TORCH at its end through Design/levels/unlocks.json). No sim number of its own: the level is data.
level5.id_why: Curriculum25.N32Levels: while this row is on, this level id is inserted right after `after` (level 4) in the campaign order; builder F names it.

boss5._why: Builder C (DESIGN32 C, D-6): THE CROWN, level 5's boss (a proposal: GG owns enemy design), built to the 60-second rules from the start: kill band 50-75 s for a moving pilot with all four weapons; an always-hittable core (x1.0) and three cyan weak plates (x2.5); three beats (sweeping beam + parryable orbs; a rotating drop ring to lava with grapple rings over the rim; charges that slam the wall and stun it with its plates open); standing still 2.5 s brings a marked mortar. Code: Core/Enemies/Crown32.cs, Crown32Arena.cs, Game/SurvivalSim.Crown32.cs. The web never had this boss, so every number here is Unity-only.
boss5.name: THE CROWN
boss5.room_why: Its own room far from every map (as THE LANTERN's at 2400 and the n27 rooms at 2800): the arena is a triangle soup in its own world layer 'crown32Room'; salt: the per-fight Mulberry32 stream (sweep direction, drop-ring direction) from the run seed.
boss5.arena_why: GG: 'the first boss fight arena ... needs to be a circle'; level 5's ring is a TRUE circle from the start: 64 wall facets (5.6 degrees each: under the Mover's cornerAngleDeg 30, so a wall ride goes all the way round), apothem 18 m (36 m across: fits F's 44 x 44 m room), walls 14 m with a closed roof; a solid inner disc of 6.5 m (never drops: the safe middle) and an outer ring of 8 sectors that drop lavaDepth m into lava in beat 2; three rim ledges 2.6 m high (the 'high spot' every camper tries) 4 facets wide and 2.2 m deep, at sectors ledgeSectors.
boss5.pool_why: HP from DESIGN32 B: target 60 s x the four-weapon kit's sustained DPS (about 120 at mixed range) x 0.6 hit rate x 0.75 uptime ~ 3240, then tuned on the crown32 sweep (p50 in 50-75 s): 3000 -> 11000 -> 16000 (the THUNDERCLAP-heavy kit), 19000 with the kit answers (charge x5 on a plate, every-nail detonate x1.5, parry 300; 16000 died at p50 42.7 s, 22000 at 73.2 s); then 10000 (GG 2026-10-10 20:10: 'bosses still too tanky!'; the lead: pilot band 25-40 s, p50 about 30, p90 <= 45 s, pistol + fist <= 90 s: bots aim near perfectly, a person takes much longer; 9500 probed: p50 28.5 s). Each beat is shortened by HP alone: beat2At / beat3At unchanged.
boss5.introHold_why: The bar's rise before it can be hurt (the BossKit intro is the floor); not a beat change.
boss5.beatSeconds_why: DESIGN32 C: at most 1.5 s unhittable at each beat change; 1.2 s lets the core move to its new height with a readable flash.
boss5.beat2At_why: Beat 2 starts when the bar is at or under this share (DESIGN32 C: 100-55 %, 55-20 %, 20-0 %).
boss5.retryBeatStart_why: A death in the room puts the bar back to the start of the current beat (THE BULWARK's phase-start rule), so dying and re-entering never wins (the degenerate 'trade lives' strategy); the fight's beat is kept.
boss5.core_why: A blocky core (a cube, coreHalf m half size) under a crown of cubes; the sim's hurtbox is hurtScale x the drawn size (DESIGN32 B: at least 1.3x); hoverY is the core centre's height over the floor per beat (beat 2 drops it low: easy to hit and to punch; beat 3 runs on the floor); hoverSpeed m/s to a new height; spinRate rad/s turns the plates round so the player must circle; in beat 2 the low core ORBITS the ring at orbitRadius m and orbitRate rad/s (moveSpeed m/s to its orbit point), so the player chases it across the dropping sectors (the first sweep: a still low core at the middle was killed from the safe disc in 5 s and the drop ring never mattered).
boss5.plates_why: Three cyan weak plates on three of the core's four faces (they face different ways), plateMult x2.5 (DESIGN32 B's window bonus); the half sizes are the drawn plate, the hurtbox is hurtScale bigger; in beat 3 they are shut except through the slam stun.
boss5.kit_why: The lead (19:07): the THUNDERCLAP on a plate did most of the damage; every weapon's special must be a real plate answer and no one weapon over about 45 % of the damage. A hit's answer is read from its weapon id and size (Crown32.WeaponClass): THUNDERCLAP hits on a plate x shotgunPlateMult (a spread gun on a small target; its slug, a THUNDERCLAP hit of slugMin or more, too: the first kit sweep had the slug at 51 % of the damage); a charged KESTREL shot (revolver at chargeMin or more: 100 charged vs 25 a tap) x chargePlateMult on a plate, x chargeCoreMult on the core; a NAILGUN detonate (a nail's blast, nailgun at detonateMin or more: 14 vs a 5 hp nail) x detonateMult wherever the nails sit; a gauntlet parry sends an orb back for parryDamage (NIGHT31's x2 of a 12 hp orb was 24). Every number tuned on the crown32 sweep's per-weapon share.
boss5.sweep_why: Beat 1: a waist-high beam (beamLow..beamHigh m over the floor: a slide (collider 1 m) passes under it, a jump (1.5 m apex) or the double jump over it) turns once round the ring from the core at rate rad/s (one lap in about 3.9 s), every everySeconds, after a tellSeconds tell (DESIGN32 C: every attack a 0.6 s+ tell); it starts on the side away from the player; a hit costs damageFrac of max health once per sweep with a knock.
boss5.orbs_why: Beats 1-2: slow led orbs at the player (everySeconds per beat, a tellSeconds glow first) the PULSE gauntlet's parry sends back (NIGHT31's boss parry: the weapon id parry31 lands in full on the core); speed m/s, damage hp, radius m, life s.
boss5.mortar_why: Anti-camp (DESIGN32 C): a player whose flat speed stays under stillSpeed m/s for stillSeconds (a wall ride never counts as still) has the spot marked; a mortar lands delaySeconds later within radius m: damageFrac of max health and a knock up. Every beat.
boss5.drop_why: Beat 2 (M3 'Drop Ring'): the outer sectors in pattern (offsets from a rotating start) glow tellSeconds, drop lavaDepth m into lava for downSeconds, rise, gapSeconds, and the pattern turns one sector on; the lava burns with design.n30.lava's numbers (damageFraction, knockUp, graceSeconds); the inner disc and the ledges never drop.
boss5.rings_why: Beat 2: count grapple rings appear over the rim (inset m in from the wall, height m up, between the sectors) so the limited grapple matters (pull out of a dropping sector); they go with beat 3.
boss5.charge_why: Beat 3 (THE STAG's charge): after firstSeconds, a tellSeconds tell (the red-orange line to the wall), a straight run at speed m/s that always meets the round wall: the SLAM stuns it stunSeconds with its plates open (x2.5; DESIGN32 B: at least the gauntlet's 2.5 s cooldown + 0.75 s), then recoverSeconds back to the middle; a hit costs damageFrac of max health with a knock.

grapplePips._why: View only (G): the grapple's charges on the HUD (two cyan pips beside the reticle, refilling). Unity-only view numbers in UnityTuning.*32.cs. Game/GrapplePips32.cs (UnityTuning.Grapple32.cs): one cyan diamond per charge right of and under the reticle; a spent one fills from the bottom as it comes back; a charge back flashes once; no text.

bossMarks._why: View only (B): every boss's damage spot glows cyan-white and its open window is unmistakable (the frames showed the Stag, Wyrm and Loom as dark boxes with no 'hit here'). Game/BossMarks32.cs, drawn from Boss31View.Render: a faint cyan-white outline on every hurtbox, the spot (Lantern core, Stag rear plate, Wyrm head, Loom joints) glowing, swelling 1.45x and pulsing while its window is open. Its render numbers are constants in BossMarks32.cs (view only).

hud32._why: View only (G): the HUD errors seen in the NIGHT31 frames: the round countdown during a boss fight, the cut-off LT label ('CHARGIN'), a lesson line left from another room. Game/UiHud32.cs: (1) the survival break line is blank while any boss fight is live (any mode); (2) the weapon slot's word box is the slot's pitch and overflows instead of truncating; (3) a boss's teaching line (lessonBegin id boss) goes when its fight is not the live one or after UnityTuning.Hud32BossLineMax.

n33._why: NIGHT33 (GG 2026-10-11, after playing NIGHT32: 'more elements' in every arena, better effects and lighting (lights 'placed and floating'), the arena design is poor, the HUD 'looks so AI generated', the zoom is 'a forced angle', enemies 'run into lava', ULTRAKILL-style trigger spawns, bosses 'still way too tanky', the grapple should pull you to the enemy and stop at it with 'a little damage', a stronger piercing pistol charge, campaign points that buy something; 'I expect major major changes'). Every row is off in the shared commit and turned on only when its contract passes. Off (--off33 / -skygrindOff33, and every older off switch): NIGHT32's game bit for bit. Unity-only numbers each carry a _why (the web never had these systems). Design: Design/levels/DESIGN33.md; defaults: DECIDE33.md; research: Research/2026-10-11-wave33/.

ai33._why: Builder E (DESIGN33 E): enemies never walk into lava on their own: a lava mask in the nav grid (NavField SetBlocked) filled at the run's start, the same mask in LevelValidate24, and an edge guard after the crowd's pushes, a husk's last straight run and the charger's dash (stunned at the edge). Knockback by the player can still throw them in. Builder E adds its numbers with their _why.
ai33.maskAbove_why: A nav node is lava (blocked for every walker) when its column's centre lies in a lava rect and it stands at most this many m over the surface (A4: kiln k2 has 84 nodes in its rect, 42 at lava height; the rest are the lane above). Unity-only: the web never had lava.
ai33.walkwayAbove_why: The crowd guard: a push that carries a walker's feet over a lava rect less than this many m over the surface is undone (it would fall in next step); higher up is a walkway (A4: exempt feet more than 1.5 m above the surface). Unity-only.
ai33.goalLine_why: Round 2 (the lead 11:06, the lava-edge stall): a flow-field goal seed (a node near the player where a walker counts as arrived and steers straight at him) is dropped when lava lies on the straight line to the player (NavGrid.HazardBetween), so walkers path round the lava instead of pressing against the far bank. Round 1 without it: about 1.2 walkers pinned at an edge on average in spire v6.

spawns33._why: Builder E (DESIGN33 E, D-7): ULTRAKILL-style trigger spawns: a room's `triggers33` (a rect, its wave, its own far-side spawn spots, an early flag) read in StepFight; a 0.6 s red-orange spawn tell before each enemy appears; a lava room's first wave waits for its trigger line. Builder E adds its numbers with their _why.
spawns33.tellSeconds_why: Each campaign enemy appears this long after its red-orange spawn tell (event enemySpawnTell33; DESIGN33 E: 0.6 s). Whole steps. Unity-only: the web's waves had no tell.
spawns33.lavaFirstWave_why: OFF since round 4 (the lead 12:09: R's walk bot soft-locked in i2, whose crossing needs five kills for the PULSE launch): only authored triggers33 hold a wave. When on: A lava room with no trigger for its first wave gets one: the line lineBeyond m past the lava's far edge along the room's spawn -> exit axis; the wave's spots are the room's nodes past that line (the room pulls the player across the lava first).
spawns33.waitSeconds_why: Any held wave comes anyway once the room has sat this long with nothing alive and nothing told (round 4: an idle watchdog in every path, not a timer from the entry; the harness asserts no such spell over 25 s). A room with a lesson never holds a wave.
spawns33.minSpawnDist_why: Round 4: the move never crosses lava from the campaign's pick, and with no far-enough node on that side the pick stands. A told spawn nearer the player than this (m) moves to the room's nearest node that is not (the campaign's own pick falls back to any node on its last try: n32 measured spawns 1.2 m from the player). Unity-only.
spawns33.tellStagger_why: OFF (round 4): when on, each placed enemy is held still for the tell (a tellSeconds stagger). With it on R's walk bot fell into deterministic retry loops (f5b seed 7: 166 lava deaths; s4 seed 3), so the tell is the column only, drawn as the enemy appears: NIGHT32's timing. The lead decides after a Player look.
spawns33.triggers33_why: Per room id (the n32 and n33 levels keep the ids): [{wave, rect [u0, v0, u1, v1], nodes [[u, v], ...], early}] in FRACTIONS of the room's floor rect (x0..x1, z0..z1), so a reshaped room keeps them in place. Wave `wave` waits for the player's feet in the rect and spawns on the nodes (nearest nav node; the campaign's minSpawnDist applies); early: it comes in on top of the living. Authored (round 3, the lead 11:47) for six lava rooms where the lava rule does not pull the player across (side gutters, a central block, or no encounter node past the lava); every room runs spawn (v about 0.9) -> exit (v about 0.1), so the far side is low v. An authored first-wave trigger also comes by the waitSeconds timer.

triggers33.f9_why: Foundry f9: the lava band v 0.28-0.68 crosses the room but all five encounter nodes sit on the spawn side (the lava rule had nowhere past the line to spawn): wave 0 waits until the player is over the lava's far edge, then comes in at the exit end.
triggers33.f10_why: Foundry f10: two side gutters by the spawn (v 0.59-0.91): the first wave waits until the player has walked past them, then fills the exit end.
triggers33.k2_why: Kiln k2: a lava strip along the left wall (u 0-0.15): the first wave waits for the room's far half and comes from the exit end, so the player runs the strip's length.
triggers33.i6b_why: Iceline i6b: lava pockets on both sides: the first wave waits until the player is between them, then comes at the far end.
triggers33.s7_why: Span s7: a lava block in the middle (v 0.33-0.67): the first wave waits past it at the exit end; the last wave is an ULTRAKILL ambush: early, at the exit line, from behind (the spawn end) on top of whoever still lives.
triggers33.v8_why: Spire v8: a U of lava (v 0.29-0.75): the first wave waits until the player is out of the U, then comes at the exit end.

bosses33._why: Builder E (DESIGN33 E, D-2): bosses 'still way too tanky' at 26-39 s pilot fights: the pilot band is now 15-22 s (harness p50 about 18 s; a person about 40 s), by per-boss hpMult overrides and the Crown pool; the anti-camp stays. Builder E adds its numbers with their _why.
bosses33.convention_why: Each boss's hpMult REPLACES design.n32.bosses32.<boss>.hpMult (the NIGHT31 pool x this, applied once per fight at full health; the code applies n33 / n32 on top of NIGHT32's cut); crown.pool replaces design.n32.boss5.pool (x the same ctx.scale.hp). Tuned on `bosses33` (Tools/SimHarness: the NIGHT32 pilots, p50 about 18 s; NIGHT32's pilots measured 29.0 / 27.8 / 28.6 / 30.0 s at the n32 numbers). Unity-only: the web never had these bosses.

lantern.hpMult_why: THE LANTERN (n32 2.4: pilot p50 29.0 s). Sweep (8 seeds, the rider): 1.45 gave p50 21.2 s, 1.3 20.8 s, 1.2 19.6 s (the beats and breaks set a floor near 19 s). The PLAYER decides (L-029): n33-r5 at 1.2 (pool 616) killed in 12.7 s, under the band: x1.4 -> 1.68 (pool about 862; harness 19.4 s).
lantern.camp_why: With the cut pool the campers reached the 66 % / 33 % breaks sooner and the camp strike paused through them (Lantern31.Camp32 ran only while hurtable): they lived 13-14 s and took 49-54 % of the bar (n32 pools: 9 s, 19 %). The strike now runs through the breaks; the other numbers override n32's (still 2 s, tell 0.8 s, 20 damage, every 1.5 s).

stag.hpMult_why: THE STAG (n32 0.52: pilot p50 27.8 s). Sweep (StagPilot31, not seeded): 0.45 gave 21.0 s, 0.40 18.8 s, 0.32 34.2 s (a pilot death lands on that pool: the curve is not monotone), 0.26 19.3 s. The PLAYER decides (L-029): n33-r5 at 0.40 (pool 720) took 25.3 s, over the band: 0.28 (pool 504; harness 19.6 s; 0.30-0.36 sit on the pilot-death bump, 22.6-34.2 s); its campers then took up to 47 %: stillArmor.stagScale 0.2.

wyrm.hpMult_why: THE KILN WYRM (n32 0.51: pilot p50 28.6 s; it dies only while surfaced, so kill times come in steps of about 10 s). Sweep (8 seeds): 0.29 gave p50 29.2 s, 0.27 and 0.25 18.8 s (p90 20.3), 0.22 19.7 s: 0.26 keeps a margin under the 0.28 step. The PLAYER decides (L-029): n33-r5 at 0.26 (pool 1562) took 22.4 s, the top edge: x0.9 -> 0.234 (pool about 1406; harness 20.5 s).
wyrm.camp_why: The centre camper took 87 % of the cut bar before falling at 11.7 s (n32 numbers): override n32's spit (still 1.5 s, a volley every 1.5 s, 25 a glob).

loom.hpMult_why: THE LOOM (n32 0.46: pilot p50 30.0 s). Sweep (8 seeds, LoomPilot32 on the full sim): 0.27 gave p50 16.8 s, 0.30 17.2 s, 0.33 19.3 s.

bosses33.stillArmor_why: STILL ARMOR (round 2; the lead 11:06: punish stillness, never more health): a player who stays within stillRadius m of one spot for stillSeconds lands only scale of each hit on the boss until he moves again (the pool is untouched; event bossStillArmor33 for the view's tell). Why: at the cut pools the lane-middle Stag camper, the Wyrm's centre camper and the Loom's corner camper dealt 8-10 % of the bar a second, about twice the moving pilot's 5.3 %, so no strike that spares the pilot could kill them before 40 %; harder shards (Stag 35 every 1 s) and drops (Loom 70 every 0.8 s) slowed the PILOT instead (Stag p50 18.8 -> 32.7 s, Loom 18.5 -> 21.3 s) and were taken out. Still = staying within stillRadius m of the spot where the stay began (a camper knocked away who walks back is still camping: a speed test like NIGHT32's missed the Stag's lane-middle camper).

stillArmor.stagScale_why: THE STAG lands only this share for a still player (round 3: at the Player-tuned pool 504 the bank-top camper took 40-47 % at 0.5; 0.3 still 40 %, 0.2 35 %; the moving pilot is not slowed: 19.6 s either way).

crown.pool_why: THE CROWN's pool (n32 boss5.pool 10000: Player pilot 39.3 s). Sweep (8 seeds, Crown32Pilot): 4600 gave p50 16.0 s, 5600 19.1 s (p90 22.0), 6200 21.7 s.

whip33._why: Builder W (DESIGN33 W, D-3): the whip: a tap latches the first enemy on the ray; light enemies come to you, heavier ones pull you and you stop 1.5 m short with a small hit and 2-3 steps of hitstop; rings and boss joints stay pull targets; a whip kill gives no charge back. No Mover.cs edit. Builder W adds its numbers with their _why.
whip33.stopGap_why: m: an enemy whip lets go when one more reel step would bring the gap (chest to the enemy's aim point, less its Radius and the player's capsule radius) under this, so you stop between stopGap and stopGap + one reel step (44 m/s / 120 Hz = 0.37 m) short of the hit volume, never inside (D-3, G1 S2: 1.5 m). The web's zip let go at 2.6 m chest-to-aim-point with 47 m/s kept, through the body (A4 c).
whip33.stopMargin_why: m added to stopGap in the stop test (one more reel step must stay outside stopGap + this), for what moves after the decision: the hop lifts the chest and a pinned or walking enemy's aim point shifts. MEASURED (harness whip33 D, margin 0): the least gap over 6 spam pulls was 1.49 m, under D-3's 1.5; 0.15 keeps every measured gap above 1.5.
whip33.stopKeep_why: m/s: the flat speed toward the enemy kept at the stop (not the pull's 44 m/s). 0 = a dead stop: MEASURED (harness whip33 A, 2 m/s): the drift through the hop's airtime carried the player from the 1.6 m stop to 1.0 m of a pinned charger in 2.3 s, under D-3's 1.5 m; with 0 the gap holds.
whip33.hopSpeed_why: m/s: the arrival's small hop (vy raised to at least this after the stop; D-3 'a small hop'). NIGHT31's node pull pops 5; 4 is a step under it so a whip is not a jump.
whip33.damage_why: The arrival's hit through Loadout.Damage (weapon whip33): one KESTREL shot's weapons.revolver.damage (25), under a husk's 40 hp, so a whip alone never kills a fresh husk (A4: the kill-refill chain); a whip kill gives no charge back either way.
whip33.hitstopSteps_why: Whole 120 Hz steps of hitstop at the arrival's hit (D-3: 2-3; 3 = 25 ms).

pierce33._why: Builder W (DESIGN33 W, D-4): the charged KESTREL shot pierces everything in a line (the LONGWAVE's pierce) at 8-10x damage, with a beam under a new event name, hitstop and a camera kick; cooldown 4 s. Builder W adds its numbers with their _why.
pierce33.pierce_why: Bodies one charged KESTREL shot goes through before a wall stops it: the LONGWAVE's weapons.rail.pierce (24), so in practice everything in the line (n31.charge.revolver.pierce was 3; G1 S3: no 3-body cap). The tracer then ends at the wall, not the last body.
pierce33.damageMult_why: x a normal KESTREL shot per body (25 x 9 = 225, headshot x2 on top), no falloff along the line (G1 S3); D-4 asks 8-10, 9 is the middle (n31.charge.revolver.damageMult was 4). The cooldown stays n31.charge.revolver.cooldownSeconds (4 s, D-4), so the crosshair arc needs no change.
pierce33.hitstopSteps_why: Whole 120 Hz steps of hitstop when the shot hit a body (G1 S3: 2-3 frames at the first hit; 3 = 25 ms); the sim's Hitstop keeps the longest request, so a kill's feel.hitstopTime still wins when longer.

devices33._why: Builder R (DESIGN33 R): arena devices that move the player or threaten it (updraft fan, hazard vent with a tell, moving platform), each deterministic, each with a tell and a refuge within 6 m, at most 3 device types per room. Builder R adds its numbers with their _why.
devices33._numbers_why: Unity-only numbers (the web has no device beyond the jump pad: K1-arena-kit.md 6b's proposals, untested in the Player). Core/Devices33.cs reads them; the level rows (campaign.rooms[i].devices33, Tools/night/gen-n33-*.cjs) give each device its place, size, column height and phase.

fan.lift_why: m/s: the updraft's vertical speed cap; from the ground the fan launches at it (Mover.Launch, the pad's path). With the jump's gravity (2 x 1.5 / 0.36^2 = 23.1 m/s^2) the player coasts lift^2 / 2g = 2.6 m above the column's top (K1: 10 m/s)
fan.accel_why: m/s^2 added to the vertical speed while the feet are in the column and below lift (gross; the Mover's gravity still pulls: net about +27 m/s^2)

vent.idleSeconds_why: s the grate rests (K1: idle 3 s)
vent.warnSeconds_why: s of the TELL before a burst (the grate glows red-orange, event ventTell; K1: 0.8 s)
vent.damageFraction_why: share of max health a burst takes (lava takes 0.25: a vent has a tell, so it hurts less), once per burst
vent.knockUp_why: m/s up on a burst hit (lava's knockUp 9: the same path, Mover.Launch)
vent.burstHeight_why: m over the grate the burst reaches (feet above it are safe: a jump clears it)

platform.speed_why: m/s along the two-point path (K1: 3 m/s)
platform.dwellSeconds_why: s the platform waits at each end (K1: 1.5 s)
platform.rideMargin_why: m past the platform's edge the feet still count as riding (the capsule's overhang)
platform.rideHeight_why: m the feet may sit above or below the top and still ride (grounded feet sit on it within the Mover's skin)

shop33._why: Builder P (DESIGN33 P, D-6; Core/Shop33.cs, Game/SurvivalSim.Shop33.cs, Game/SurvivalGame.Shop33.cs): campaign points carry across levels (the WALLET, Profile.bank33) and are spent in a SHOP between levels (opened from ContinueCampaign after RESULTS) on eight upgrades; a rack of four slots holds what is EQUIPPED (2 weapon mods, 1 movement perk, 1 wildcard: G1's four-slot rack, Research/2026-10-11-wave33/G1-feel-ai-economy.md 6); owning more than a slot holds is a choice made in the shop. Prices are tierMult x typicalEarn rounded to priceRound. The owned and equipped upgrades (Shop33 encoding: bit i owned, bit 8 + i equipped, i = the item's index here, so items are APPEND ONLY) are on the run's tape (format 16). The WALLET is a separate campaign currency (the lead, 11:04): a run's own points stay NIGHT32's (points.start, in-level buys spend them), the tape's bank33 stays 0; at layerClear a level's earned points are banked BEST-OF per level (only what beats that level's best earn so far: a replay never earns twice; Profile.banked33); automation (any -skygrind argument but the -skygrindOffNN switches, or SurvivalGame.Shop33NoSave) keeps the wallet and the upgrades in memory and never writes them. The web has none of this (it has no campaign), so every number here is Unity-only. Off: NIGHT32's campaign (nothing carried).
shop33.typicalEarnWhy: MEASURED (shop33 earn --seeds 7, 2026-10-11, the design config as committed at b10e06e6): walk29's pilot through each n32 level's playable rooms (boss rooms excluded), Economy.earned per run, p50 per level: n32-foundry 2683 (6 of 7 cleared), n32-iceline 3869, n32-kiln 3751, n32-span 5274, n32-spire 5845; the p50 of the level p50s is 3869, the campaign's sum of p50s 21422. 1x is the LOWEST level p50 (foundry, rounded down to priceRound), so a tier-one upgrade is affordable after any level including the first (G1: 'tier one per level, tier two per two levels'); the eight together cost 17x = 45050, about twice a campaign's bot earn, so the rack is a choice.

items.name: HAIR TRIGGER
items._why: x design.n31.charge.revolver.fullSeconds (0.5 s -> 0.35 s to a full charge); tier 0: the KESTREL is level 1's gun.

items.name: BORE SLUG
items._why: + bodies the charged THUNDERCLAP slug goes on through after its first (NIGHT31's slug hits one body: Loadout.slugPierce33, each body the slug's full damage, a wall stops it).

items._why: x weapons.specials.nailgun.detonateDamage (14 -> 17.5 a nail; Projectiles.detonateMult33), the LT DETONATE and the charged KESTREL's nail combo.

items.name: QUICK FEET
items._why: The dash has no cooldown of its own: it costs design.stamina.boost.cost (0.5 bar) and the bar refills at refill.rate after refill.delay / emptyDelay, so one dash comes back in 0.4 + 0.5 / 0.5 = 1.4 s. x this: the delays x 0.8 and the rate / 0.8 (1.12 s, -20 %).
