The shake is ULTRAKILL's CameraShake: amounts in its units, the bigger replaces (never adds), linear decay shakeDecay per real second, the camera moving min(shake, 1) of its full turn (a shake above 1 only lasts longer).
juice38.entranceShake_why: A boss entrance (every boss's bossRise, and boss38Entrance for an explicit call): ULTRAKILL's boss stomps are 2-3 (Minotaur 1.5-3, Minos 2-3, Geryon 3); 2.5 holds the full turn for 0.5 s and fades out by 0.83 s at shakeDecay 3.
juice38.entranceHitstop_why: s: the world freezes this long on the entrance (through SurvivalGame.Hitstop: the impact layer's Sim tier, inside its budget: 0.2 s a second, max 0.5 s); ULTRAKILL's parry TrueStop is 0.25 s, a boss entrance is a beat, not a stop.
juice38.entranceFlicker_why: s: the full-screen CRT flicker on an entrance (PLAN.md section 4: Crt29's strength spiked ~0.3 s): two brightness pulses (<= 3 flashes a second, the game's FlashGate), deeper scanlines, a tear, a colour split.
juice38.entranceGap_why: s: a second entrance inside this is the same entrance (a boss's resume start after its walk-in, a bossRise and a boss38Entrance on one beat): no second shake / flicker / hit-stop.
juice38.moveShake_why: A big boss move (the worm's dig and erupt, the Stag's crash, the Loom's fall, the Crown's shatter, the Wick's dive): ULTRAKILL's Minotaur slam / explosion-in-range 1.5 (0.5 s of decay at 3 / s).
juice38.moveFlicker_why: s: the flicker on a big move (one pulse in 0.2 s: shorter than the entrance's).
juice38.moves_why: The big moves by their sim events (event:stage when only one stage is the move: wick37Dive's tell / dive / stall; the rest any stage). The worm's dig and erupt come from its bossTell (wyrmTells) at the tell's seconds.
juice38.wyrmTells_why: THE KILN WYRM's bossTell names for its dig (crack: where it dives into the floor) and its erupt (dive: where it comes out of the wall); the shake lands when the tell resolves (its `seconds` of world time later; the Wyrm is not edited).
juice38.shakeDecay_why: Per real second, linear (ULTRAKILL CameraController.cs: 1.0 lasts 0.33 s, 3.0 lasts 1 s).
juice38.hurtShakePer_why: A hit taken shakes damage / this (ULTRAKILL NewMovement.cs: damage / 20 on a 100 HP player; ours is health.max 100 too), between hurtShakeMin and hurtShakeMax.
juice38.hurtShakeMin_why: Every hit shakes at least this (ULTRAKILL's integer division drops hits under 20; GG asked for a hit to be felt: PLAN.md 'a small shake').
juice38.hurtShakeMax_why: A hit never shakes more than this (a small shake: a boss move is 1.5).
juice38.hurtStaticMin_why: The static burst's level on a hit (ULTRAKILL's hurt screen: alpha 0.5, and the i-frames last that many seconds: the overlay IS the timer); it decays at staticDecay per s, so it shows for level / staticDecay s.
juice38.hurtStaticMax_why: The level at hurtHeavyAt damage and above (ULTRAKILL: 0.8 for 50+ damage); between, by the damage's share.
juice38.hurtHeavyAt_why: Damage at which the static is hurtStaticMax (ULTRAKILL's 50 on a 100 HP player).
juice38.staticDecay_why: Per real second, linear (ULTRAKILL's hurt screen alpha falls 1 per second).

p39._why: Builder P1 (NIGHT39.md P1; GG: 'if I'm holding it down it should intelligently prioritize the charge shot instead of firing the fast shot first'): the KESTREL's tap fires on a quick release, a held press charges with no tap first (tap36's fire-on-press with the row off; the THUNDERCLAP keeps tap36). Builder P1 adds its numbers with their _why (in this row only).
p39.tapS_why: The KESTREL's tap / hold split (whole steps: 18 at 120 Hz): a press released inside this fires the tap ON THE RELEASE; held past it, NO tap fires and the hold is a charge (charge35Start, the HUD's CHARGING; FULL at design.n31.charge.revolver.fullSeconds 0.5 s from the press, as before). In research/feel-web.md section 3's range: Unity's Input System tap 0.2 s, casual players need up to ~0.2 s to choose hold over tap, an average finger is off the button in ~0.1 s; 0.15 s sits above a deliberate click (50-100 ms, design.n35.charge35.tapS_why) and under tap36's holdStartS 0.18 s, so a tap's added latency (the press's own length) is at most 0.15 s and the charge reads 0.35 s of filling.
p39.partialFires_why: A hold released past tapS but before FULL fires the tap on the release (true: the trigger always answers, NIGHT35 charge35's rule) or drains with no shot (false: ULTRAKILL's Piercer winds down without firing, feel-web.md section 3). true: a slow pad trigger that just passes tapS still shoots; the tap after a partial gets no aim correction past correctFadeS.
p39.correctFullS_why: A release tap fired up to this long after its press leaves from the PRESS's eye along the PRESS's aim, in full (INVERSUS, Ryan Juckett, gamedeveloper.com 'Reducing perceived attack delay in INVERSUS': full correction 0-0.11 s; feel-web.md section 3): the shot goes where the crosshair was when the finger went down, so the release's delay never moves the hit.
p39.correctFadeS_why: The correction fades linearly from correctFullS to none at this age (INVERSUS: none by 0.19 s); tapS 0.15 s is inside it, so every quick tap is corrected at least 50 %.
p39.intervalMult_why: x the KESTREL's normal fire interval while p39 is on (GG: the pistol 'should feel heavier, slower, and more impactful'): the web's 0.4 s (48 steps) becomes 58 steps (0.483 s), taps and the held auto-fire alike; the charged shot and its 2.5 s cooldown unchanged. Tap DPS -17 %: the boss bands (B1) are measured with p39 on. 1.2 is a guess, logged; the heavier look (Pistol39View) carries the rest.
p39.hitS_why: A KESTREL tap's hit on a body freezes the frame this long (sim.Hitstop, the web's freeze: the longest request wins, so a kill's own freeze still rules). crunch36's body hit is 15-20 ms (design.n36.crunch36.bodyHitS); ULTRAKILL's revolver beam 0.05 s and punch 0.1 s (REVIEW.md root cause 3). Pistol39View requests it on the hit event (loop pacing: the sim and the tape never see it).
p39.chargedHitS_why: The charged KESTREL shot's (the cannon's) hit freezes this long, once per shot however many bodies it pierces: ULTRAKILL's heavy tier (punch 0.1 s; fighting games' heavy 16 frames ~0.27 s at 60 fps is too long for a gun that pierces three).

ride39.speedBuff_why: The ride's speed floor is wallRide.minSpeed (8) x (1 + 0.15) = 9.2 m/s (wallride35: 0.3, 10.4 m/s). GG 2026-10-13: 'you gain speed too quickly'. NIGHT39.md R1's lever (~0.15); Lucio's own buff (30 %, lucio.md) is not the target any more: the feel is GG's. Measured: n39ride chain (the first wall's ride speed 10.4 -> 9.2 m/s).
ride39.exitBoost_why: Metres per second added at each jump-off (wallride35: 2). Half the gain per wall (NIGHT39.md R1's lever ~1). Blizzard published no magnitude (lucio.md); ours, measured in n39ride chain.
ride39.chainCap_why: The chain's top speed (wallride35: 20). With capJumpOff the cap holds the whole jump-off speed, so a chain climbs to 16 m/s and stays there (before: 10.4 -> 15.2 -> 19.1 -> 20.7 -> 22.2 -> 23.6 m/s on six walls, n39ride chain). 16 is NIGHT39.md R1's lever, under the slide jump's 24 so a slide-hop stays the fastest takeoff.
ride39.capJumpOff_why: Measured (n39ride chain, NIGHT38's numbers): wallride35's chainCap never held a chain, because a jump-off pushes outSpeed 8 m/s straight out from the wall and the next wall's ride start keeps the whole horizontal speed (the web's SPEC 1.3: 'no loss from the approach angle'), so every wall adds about hypot(along, 8) - along on top of the exit boost (24.9 m/s off the sixth wall with a cap of 20). With this on, the jump-off's whole horizontal speed is held to max(chainCap, the ride's own speed): a ride already faster than the cap (a slide-hop entry) keeps its speed, a chain never gains past the cap (Ride35.Boost39, Mover.cs's wallride35 jump-off).
ride39.upLow_why: The jump-off's up speed looking down (wallride35: 4.12, the wiki's Lucio). GG 2026-10-13: 'the jump height should be increased slightly'. About +12 %; measured rise in n39ride chain's jump rows. The ground jump (PortExport jumpSpeed 10) is a web number and not changed (NIGHT39.md R1).
ride39.upHigh_why: The jump-off's up speed looking up (wallride35: 9.12). The same ask, about +10 %; level look (pitch 0): (4.6 + 10) / 2 = 7.3 m/s (wallride35: 6.62). Measured rise: n39ride chain's jump rows.
ride39.noRideLook_why: VIEW ONLY (no sim number; independent of `enabled`): NoRide39View draws every campaign box tagged noride (the boxes the Mover refuses, NIGHT38's noride) as a dark plate with vertical fins (UnityTuning.NoRide39.cs), and hides Doors38View's NIGHT38 ribs. GG 2026-10-13: 'a new wall material with a clear visual texture that indicates you cannot wall ride on it'. Off until the lead has looked at frames (NIGHT39.md method 2).

boss39._why: Builder B1 (NIGHT39.md B1; DECIDE39 D-1; GG: 'all bosses need more balanced health bars so each fight lasts around one to two minutes, maybe three if you're slow'): per-boss overrides (health, stagger meter, window, budget, the worm's pool mult) while on (design.n37.* and the worm's rows unchanged). Builder B1 adds its numbers with their _why.
boss39.band_why: Bot band 30-60 s (every seed killed, p50 30-60 s, p90 <= 70 s; Tools/SimHarness `boss39`): a person takes about twice the bot's time (CORE.md w31 / w32: the 15-22 s bot band was '~40 s person'; NIGHT32: tune the bot band to about half GG's target), so 30-60 s bot = GG's 'one to two minutes' (NIGHT39.md B1). Before / after per boss: Research/2026-10-14-wave39/B1.md. Each boss's keys override only that boss, only while the row is on; design.n37.* and the worm's rows are unchanged, so --off39 gives NIGHT38's fights.

wick._why: THE WICK (level 1): before, total p50 34.3 s (from the cap 15.4 s). Its legs are places (the climb), so the pool is the lever that lengthens the fight at the cap; one more right move per window (stagger 3 -> 4) makes each window a cycle more. Measured: total p50 44.7 s, p90 44.7 s, from the cap 25.8 s, 10/10 killed.
wick.hpMult_why: The fight's pool x2 (Wick37.StartFight's pool x the run's scale). hpMult 2 alone: total p50 42.9 s; with stagger 4: 44.7 s.
wick.stagger_why: The CYAN window's meter per leg (design.n37.wick37.kit.stagger [3, 3, 3]): one more crack / parry / pierce per window (D-1: the brain's lever first). Alone it changed nothing (34.3 s): the window count is not the Wick's bottleneck.

stag._why: THE STAG (level 2): before p50 20.9 s, p90 24.8 s. One window per leg ended each leg (a launch is 320 of a 300-per-leg pool), so a bigger pool makes each leg 2-3 stagger cycles, and the meter grows per leg (Minos Prime's stamina pattern, Boss37.cs). Measured: p50 37.9 s, p90 45.7 s, 10/10 killed.
stag.hpMult_why: The pool 900 -> 4050: legs of 1350 HP, so a leg takes 2-4 launches / window punches instead of one. Probed: x2 22.3 s, x3.5 + stagger 6 32.7 s, x4 + stagger 6 + window 2 s 35.8 s, x5 37.0 s (diminishing).
stag.stagger_why: The meter per leg (design.n37.stag37.kit.stagger [4, 4, 4]): 3 / 4 / 4 hind-leg catches (catch.stagger 2) or chunk parries per window instead of 2.
stag.windowSeconds_why: The CYAN window 2.5 -> 2 s: a window is a burst, not a stand-and-shoot; the length comes from more windows.

wyrm._why: THE KILN WYRM (level 3; GG: 'the worm boss fight needs more health because it dies too quickly'): before p50 20.5 s on a pool of 1405 (design.n24.wyrm.hp.pool 7800 x 1.1 x design.n29 0.7 x design.n33 0.234). Its AI unchanged (GG); its phases are fractions of the pool (66 % / 33 %), so they move with it. Measured on level 3 itself (round 2: `boss39 kiln`, n38-kiln's k5 THE RING in K4's wyrm39-arena.json, NIGHT31's punch-and-slug pilot WyrmPilot31): before 11.8 s; after p50 43.0 s, p90 43.0 s, pool 5620, 10/10 killed (with P1's p39 on too: p50 50.4 s, p90 62.5 s). On the old `boss32 wyrm` rig (survival map, the old arena): p50 32.4 s, p90 43.8 s.
wyrm.hpMult_why: Each fight's pool x4 after NIGHT29 / 32 / 33's cuts (1405 -> 5620, still under NIGHT25's 8580). Round 1 picked x2.75 on the old rig (40.3 s); in the new arena x2.75 is 26.7 s. Probed on k5: x3.5 35.3 s, x4 43.0 s, x4.5 45.8 s, x5 66.6 s.

loom._why: THE LOOM (level 4): before p50 21.6 s, p90 21.8 s. Its legs are places and each leg ends when its one CYAN window closes, so its pool never gates the fight (hpMult x2: 21.7 s; nailsToTear 5: 21.9 s): only a longer road to each window does. Legs 2 and 3 ask for a parried spool on top of the two torn knees (the parry, GG's w35 'an understanding of parry mechanics'). Measured over 20 seeds: p50 38.8 s, p90 45.9 s, 20/20 killed.
loom.stagger_why: The meter per leg (design.n37.loom37.kit.stagger [6, 6, 6]): two torn knees (tearStagger 3 each) open leg 1's window; legs 2 and 3 also need one parried spool (parryStagger 1.5). Spools are YELLOW in every leg (weight 1.2), so a person who misses one gets another. 7.5 in leg 1 too: 3/10 killed (the pilot dies to lashes waiting): leg 1 stays the teaching leg.
loom.restSeconds_why: The breather between bursts 1.5 -> 2.5 s (Boss37 REST): the waits for a spool line up with the pilot's tears; 2.5 s measured 20/20 killed. 2 s measured 4/10 (the pilot died to lashes): the fight is sensitive here, so re-check after any loom change.

crown._why: THE CROWN (level 5): before p50 21.93 s, p90 23.02 s. Its health is its gems (a pass through the ring breaks passGems whole gems; the legs change at legGemsLeft), so neither the pool (x2: 21.9 s) nor the meter (stagger 6: 19.0 s) lengthens it: more gems = more passes, the fight's moving verb. The TORCH pass keeps its 2 gems (torchGems untouched: a verb's reward kept, PRINCIPLES 1). Measured: p50 36.5 s, p90 41.9 s, 10/10 killed.
crown.gems_why: design.n37.crown37.crown.gems 8 -> 20 (the pool is gems x gemHp 100, as Crown37.StartFight sets it; the view draws c.p.gems sockets). Probed: 12 27.7 s, 16 30.5 s, 20 36.5 s.
crown.legGemsLeft_why: Leg 2 at 13 gems left, leg 3 at 6 (design.n37.crown37 [5, 2] of 8): 7 / 7 / 6 gems per leg, leg 3 still ends on the finisher through the opening.

stag31._why: Level 6's old Stag (Stag31, plan id glacier on n35-finale): before 19.6 s (`boss32 stag`, NIGHT31's StagPilot31, the same time every seed). Pool only (its AI is NIGHT31's). Measured: 44.4 s, 10/10 killed; on n35-finale's own room x6 (round 2: `boss39 finale`, the game's config): before 19.4 s, after 37.5 s (with P1's p39 on too: 43.0 s), 10/10 killed.
stag31.hpMult_why: Each fight's pool x3 after NIGHT32 / 33's cuts. Probed: x2 27.8 s, x2.5 37.4 s, x2.75 37.4 s, x3 44.4 s, x3.25 51.3 s.

slow39._why: Builder F1 (NIGHT39.md F1; GG 2026-10-13: 'when you're wall riding and zooming in ... it needs to be extremely slow every time'; 'if you grapple onto an enemy the game should slow down with the same effect'; the gauntlet's parry 'emphasized more and slowed down'). Loop pacing (SurvivalGame.SlowAim27.cs -> Slow39 in SurvivalSim.N39.Slow.cs): the sim still steps at 120 Hz, the tape and the fingerprint never see it, Time.timeScale untouched, aim reads the real frame delta (Max Payne's rule: research/feel-web.md section 1). No N39Blocks bit; off (the row, --off39 / -skygrindOff39): slowAim27's NIGHT38 behaviour (design.n27.slowAim27, scale 0.75). Gated by SLOW-MO (REDUCED MOTION turns it off) as slowAim27. No meter and no drain (Severed Steel's meter does not drain while wall running). Harness: n39slow.
slow39.enabled_why: Off until the lead has looked at the Player frames (NIGHT39.md method 2); n39slow forces it on.
slow39.scale_why: World time share at full slow while riding a wall AND zoomed (and while latched on an enemy). No shipped game's time scale was found (research/feel-web.md section 1: not found for Ghostrunner, Max Payne, Mirror's Edge, Severed Steel), so a Unity-only design number in the card's 0.25-0.35 range: 0.3 = a 3.3x slow-down ('extremely slow', against design.n27.slowAim27.scale 0.75, which GG felt as 'removed'). Tune on Player frames.
slow39.easeInS_why: Real seconds for the slow's depth to go 0 -> 1 (linear depth, smoothstep share: ease in and out, no snap). slowAim27's 0.13 s, a little longer for the deeper drop. Not found in any source (research/feel-web.md: 'ramp-in / ramp-out times ... not found').
slow39.easeOutS_why: Real seconds back to real time (smoothstep). Longer than the way in so letting go of the zoom or leaving the wall reads as a release, not a jolt; short enough that a chain's air time between walls is mostly at speed.
slow39.latch_why: The whip latch (VERBS 20): the same slow while the hook is bitten into an enemy (the rope Attached on an enemy zip: SurvivalSim.Slow39Latched). A yank (a light enemy pulled to you, no rope) is not a latch.
slow39.parry_why: A player parry ('parry' or 'parry36', owner player) opens a slow window AFTER the parry's freeze (design.ultra.parryHitstop 0.25 s, ULTRAKILL's figure, unchanged): the emphasis is the slow after the freeze, not a longer freeze (NIGHT39.md F1).
slow39.parryScale_why: World time share in the parry's window: deeper than the ride's 0.3 so the returned projectile's flight reads (Parry31View's streak runs on world time). Ours (ULTRAKILL documents no slow after its freeze: research/feel-web.md section 2).
slow39.parryHoldS_why: Real seconds the parry window holds parryScale after the freeze: with the 0.25 s freeze about 0.55 s at under a quarter speed before the ease. Ours (no source gives a post-freeze slow); about the fighting games' heavy hitstop (16 frames, 267 ms: research/feel-web.md section 2) again, so it reads as one longer beat without stalling the fight.
slow39.parryOutS_why: Real seconds the parry window eases back to real time (smoothstep).

n40._why: NIGHT40, the build night (GG 2026-10-13 ~22:00, verbatim in Research/2026-10-14-wave40/GG-REQUEST.md; NIGHT40.md; DECIDE40.md). Every row is off in the shared commit and turned on only when its check passes and its frames were looked at. Sim rows (start40, kiln40, cut40, charge40, ride40, iceline40, brawl40, loom40, crown40, foes40) are behind N40Blocks; arc40, pump40, rods40 and models40 are view rows (no bit). Off (--off40 / -skygrindOff40, and every older off switch): NIGHT39's game bit for bit. Level rows swap levelFrom for levelTo (Curriculum25.N40Levels); their weapons are data: startSet, awards [{room, weapon}], loom40.dropWeapons (SurvivalSim.N40.cs).

start40._why: Builder S1 (NIGHT40.md S1; GG: 'the game needs a short delay or a required movement trigger before the first wave of enemies appears'): the first wave of a level (and after a respawn) waits for movement or a timer, then a tell before enemies can attack. S1 adds its numbers with their _why.
start40.enabled_why: Off until the lead has looked at its Player frames once and iterated once (NIGHT40.md method 2).
start40.moveMetres_why: S1: the hold ends when the player's feet are this far (3D) from where they stood when the wave was held (the level's spawn, or the respawn point). A hypothesis (NIGHT40.md S1; enemies-web.md section 5: Doom Eternal locks an arena when the player crosses in; no published grace number was found): about two strides of a sprint, so any deliberate move starts the fight.
start40.holdSeconds_why: S1: the hold ends this many seconds after it began even if the player stands still (never a soft-lock). A hypothesis (NIGHT40.md S1): time to read the room's first line and look around.
start40.noAttackSeconds_why: S1: the held wave's enemies cannot start an attack for this long after their spawn tell ends (design.n33.spawns33.tellSeconds when spawns33 is on); they move. A husk-family body (husk, tank, spitter, swarmer) gets it as its attack cooldown; any other kind is stunned for it. A hypothesis (NIGHT40.md S1).
start40.afterRespawn_why: S1: a death's retry holds the room's first wave the same way (GG: the first wave comes too fast; a retry starts the room over).

kiln40._why: Builder S1 (NIGHT40.md S1; GG: the boost 'needs clearer text and better explanation'; DECIDE40 D-2, GG 2026-10-13 ~23:00: 'yes the pistol and gauntlet' = level 3 starts with the shotgun, the pistol and gauntlet unlocked later): level 3 as n40-kiln (from n38-kiln; n38-kiln untouched).
kiln40.enabled_why: Off until the lead has looked at its Player frames once and iterated once (NIGHT40.md method 2).
kiln40.startSet_why: GG's answer (DECIDE40 D-2): the THUNDERCLAP alone at the start; S1 adds `awards` for the revolver and the gauntlet in the zones it picks.
kiln40.awards_why: S1 (DECIDE40 D-2: 'the pistol and gauntlet' unlocked later in the level): the first half (3.1 THE CHARGE, 3.1b THE FLUE, 3.2 POUR HALL) is the THUNDERCLAP's alone; the KESTREL comes on entering 3.2b THE STACK (before 3.3's spitters on the west gantry, a ranged job), the PULSE gauntlet on entering 3.3 CASTING FLOOR (the room whose verb is 'launch into the pour': the blast throws them in). Weapon ids, never display names.

chain.text: BOOST 2/5 · IN THE AIR, LOOK STRAIGHT DOWN
BOOST 3/5 · PRESS {fire}: THE BLAST LIFTS YOU
BOOST 4/5 · AT THE TOP, PRESS {fire} AGAIN
BOOST 5/5 · PRESS {jump} IN THE AIR: THE LAST METRES
THE BOOST: JUMP, LOOK DOWN, FIRE, FIRE, JUMP
HOLD {fire} ON THE GROUND: CHARGE A SLUG

kiln40.chain_why: S1 (NIGHT40.md S1, PRINCIPLES 2: ULTRAKILL's HudMessage, one step at a time, each shown when the last is done): the THUNDERCLAP CLIMB (K4's level: jump, shoot down, shoot again, double jump; envelopes38 'jump+double+boost x2' 13.36 m) as five numbered lines of at most 52 characters resolved (teach35.maxChars; BOOST n/5: the player sees it is a sequence), a one-time summary card (GG: 'more thorough'), then one on the charged slug (W1's charge40 rule: on the ground a hold charges). Round 3 (the lead's n40-r2 frames: 'JUMP SPACE.' read badly): one form for every line, all capitals, the bound button inside a verb phrase ('PRESS {jump} TO JUMP'). Words, not numbers: {jump} / {fire} resolve to the bound buttons (UiTeach35). done: jump | lookDown | boost | boostAgain | airJump | seen (SurvivalSim.N40.Kiln.cs).
kiln40.lookDownDeg_why: S1: 'LOOK STRAIGHT DOWN' is done at a look pitch this far below level (a hypothesis: past 60 deg the blast's push is mostly up; the boost below accepts 45).
kiln40.boostPitchDeg_why: S1: a THUNDERCLAP shot in the air counts as a boost when the look pitch is at least this far below level (a hypothesis: Sandbox19 pushes along -aim, so at 45 deg the shot still lifts the player by 0.71 x jumpSpeed).
kiln40.lineFallbackSeconds_why: S1 (NIGHT40.md S1: 'each line held until done (a 20 s fallback)'): a step not done in this time moves the chain on, so the text never sticks.
kiln40.minLineSeconds_why: S1: a chain line stands at least this long even when its step is already done (a fast climb does the shot, the double and the second shot inside a second; each line still reads). A hypothesis: about two reading fixations of a six-word line.
kiln40.seenSeconds_why: S1: the slug's line has nothing to do; it stands this long (teach35's showS is 5 s; one more for a longer line).

cut40._why: Builder S1 (NIGHT40.md S1; GG: 'The sixth level should be deleted entirely, along with any mention of levels beyond it'; DECIDE40 D-4): level 6 out of the campaign order; its files stay until GG's yes (--off40 still loads them).
cut40.enabled_why: Off until the lead has looked at its Player frames once and iterated once (NIGHT40.md method 2).
cut40.cut_why: S1: level 6 under either id (n35-finale today; n38-finale while design.n38.finale38 swaps it in), so the cut holds whichever row is on. The files stay in the tree until GG's yes (D-4); --off40 still loads them. The level select's six slots (the sixth LOCKED, unnamed) and 5 playable are UnityTuning.Cut40.cs (view numbers).

charge40._why: Builder W1 (NIGHT40.md W1; GG: 'charge shots for both weapons should take longer to load'; 'The shotgun also needs a charge shot'; DECIDE40 D-6): longer charges; the THUNDERCLAP's hold charges with no shot first on the ground. Overrides design.n31.charge / n35.charge35 / n39.p39 while on (those rows unchanged). W1 adds its numbers with their _why.
charge40.enabled_why: Off until the lead has looked at its Player frames once and iterated once (NIGHT40.md method 2).
charge40.revolverFullS_why: The KESTREL's FULL charge, seconds from the press (overrides design.n31.charge.revolver.fullSeconds 0.5 while on; whole steps: 108 at 120 Hz). GG 2026-10-13: 'charge shots for both weapons should take longer to load'. research/feel-web.md section 3: ULTRAKILL's Piercer 0.5 s (today's number), Apex's charge rifle 0.85 s, Destiny 2's fusion rifles 0.53-0.97 s (Precision 0.80 s), Splatoon's Splat Charger 1.0 s: 0.9 s sits at the fusion rifles' slow end, a hypothesis. p39's tapS 0.15 s is unchanged, so the charge reads 0.75 s of filling (was 0.35 s). A shop33 KESTREL charge multiplier still scales it (FullSteps: this x the shop's ratio).
charge40.shotgunFullS_why: The THUNDERCLAP's FULL charge (the slug), seconds from the press (overrides design.n31.charge.shotgun.fullSeconds 0.7 while on; 144 steps). research/feel-web.md section 3: Splatoon's Splat Charger 1.0 s, the E-liter 4K 1.53 s, Destiny's High Impact fusion 0.97 s: 1.2 s is between the Splat Charger and the E-liter, kept longer than the KESTREL's 0.9 s as the slug is a whole volley x3 on one line (n31 kept the same order: 0.5 / 0.7). A hypothesis.
charge40.shotgunTapS_why: On the GROUND only (D-6): the THUNDERCLAP takes p39's hold rule (Charge35.StepP39). A press released inside this fires ONE volley on the release, aimed from the press (the correction below); held past it, NO volley fires and the hold charges the slug. Copied from design.n39.p39.tapS (0.15 s, 18 steps; its _why: above a deliberate 50-100 ms click, under tap36's holdStartS 0.18 s), so both guns split a tap from a hold at the same moment. In the AIR a press fires at once (tap36 as today) so the boost keeps its timing.
charge40.partialFires_why: A ground hold released past shotgunTapS but before FULL fires the volley on the release (true: the trigger always answers, as design.n39.p39.partialFires) or drains (false: the Piercer's wind-down, feel-web.md section 3).
charge40.correctFullS_why: A ground release volley fired up to this long after its press leaves from the PRESS's eye along the PRESS's aim (INVERSUS: full correction 0-0.11 s; research/feel-web.md section 3), as design.n39.p39.correctFullS for the KESTREL.
charge40.correctFadeS_why: The correction fades linearly to none at this age (INVERSUS: none by 0.19 s), as design.n39.p39.correctFadeS; shotgunTapS 0.15 s is inside it.

ride40._why: Builder R2 (NIGHT40.md R2; GG 2026-10-13: 'Infinite wall-riding should also be implemented so players don't slowly slide down after a few seconds; the wall-ride must feel crisp, smooth, and reliable'; 'Wall-riding currently triggers too easily when climbing random platforms or stairs'; DECIDE40 D-9): EVERY ride holds (ride38's hold rule for a tap ride as for a hold ride: no sink, no 1.2 s timer, the look pitch past +-deadzoneDeg drifts it up / down, never past the wall's top); a ride ends only by the player (jump, crouch, the stick away), the wall's end or a landing; a 60 s guard against a stuck state. These numbers override design.n38.ride38's while the row is on (Core/Ride40.cs Hold; the n38 row is untouched). Core/Ride40.cs; Mover.cs branches marked NIGHT40 ride40, inside the NIGHT35 wallride35 branches only. Off: NIGHT39's ride bit for bit. Changes VERBS rows 9 / 11 on purpose. The harness: n40ride measure / walk.
ride40.enabled_why: Off until the lead has looked at its Player frames once and iterated once (NIGHT40.md method 2).
ride40.holdSink_why: m/s: a ride inside the pitch dead zone sinks at this speed. 0 = the height is kept exactly (GG: 'so players don't slowly slide down'). Same value as design.n38.ride38.holdSink, now for every ride (a tap ride sank 1.5 m/s after wallgrip36's 0.35 s grip and ended at 1.2 s).
ride40.guard_why: Seconds: a ride ends on its own only after this long (the event's reason 'safety'), a guard against a stuck state, never a meter: the MIT Godot controller's infinite_wallrun_time ends only on wall loss, floor contact or releasing forward (Research/2026-10-14-wave40/research/feel-web.md section 2). Same value as design.n38.ride38.guard.
ride40.deadzoneDeg_why: Degrees of look pitch (+ up) within which a ride holds its height, so aiming at enemies near the horizon does not move it. design.n38.ride38's value (NIGHT38 PLAN.md section 1).
ride40.fullDeg_why: Degrees of look pitch at which the drift reaches driftMax (linear from deadzoneDeg, clamped past it). design.n38.ride38's value (= design.n35.wallride35.pitchHighDeg, so one look reads both).
ride40.driftMax_why: m/s: the most a ride rises or sinks from the look pitch. design.n38.ride38's value (2.5 m/s climbs a 5 m wall in 2 s, about a quarter of the ride's 9.2 m/s floor along the wall with ride39).
ride40.topProbe_why: m past the capsule radius: a rise is cut when a ray toward the ridden wall from the capsule's upper contact sample (the feet + 1.45 m) moved up by this step's rise finds no wall this close (never past the wall's top). design.n38.ride38's value; an engine reach, not a feel number.
ride40.minClearance_why: THE ATTACH ASKS FOR INTENT (round 2; a hypothesis): no ride starts while the ground below the feet is closer than 1.0 m (a ray down from the feet). A jump at a ride wall from the floor still rides: it attaches once the jump has carried the feet 1.0 m up (jump.height 1.5). Source: the CSE125 'Titanfall Movement System' enter rule, ground clearance >= 50 Quake units (about 1.3 m at 1 u = 1 inch; 1.0 is NIGHT40.md R2's lower start so a floor jump still rides), and the common Unity tutorial's AboveGround() ray (Research/2026-10-14-wave40/research/feel-web.md section 1). Measured before (n40ride walk, levels 1-5, 3 seeds): 432 of 606 ride starts had ground within 1.0 m.
ride40.minSpeed_why: m/s of horizontal speed (before the wall clipped it) for a ride to start: slowly climbing onto a platform never rides. TMS's enter rule: >= 200 u/s (about 5 m/s at 1 u = 1 inch); 4 = the web's wallRide.entrySpeed for a timed ride (feel-web.md section 1). A hypothesis.
ride40.inputDot_why: The stick must point toward the wall: dot(move direction, -wall normal) >= 0.1 (about 6 deg into it; a stick held along a wall at any angle into it counts, a neutral stick or one along or away from the wall does not). TMS's intent rule dot(wishDir, -wallNormal) >= 0.1 (feel-web.md section 1). A hypothesis.
ride40.minWallHeight_why: m: the wall's face must still be there 2.0 m above the feet (a ray toward the wall from the body's axis at that height): stair risers, platform faces and rails are shorter, so they never ride. No source has a minimum wall height (feel-web.md: 'not found'); ours, NIGHT40.md R2's hypothesis. Measured before: 122 of 606 ride starts on a face under 2.0 m above the feet.
ride40.attachReach_why: m past the capsule radius: wallride35's near-miss draw (jump held beside a wall pulls onto it), KEPT at wallride35's 0.5. NIGHT40.md R2's hypothesis was 0.25 (GG w29: 'almost like you snap on to it'); measured (n40ride n38f foundry --probe reach=..., 3 seeds): THE GANTRY's chain clears 3/3 at 0.5 and 0/3 at 0.4, 0.35 and 0.25 (its 8 m apart walls are caught by the draw after each jump-off). The draw now asks for the same intent as a contact (the stick toward the wall, 1.0 m of clearance, a 2.0 m face, 4 m/s), which is what stops the snap onto risers and platform faces.
ride40.lockout_why: Seconds: after a ride ends in the air, its wall (or one facing within wallride35's reRideDeg) starts no ride for 0.2 s: no re-snap after a jump-off or a drop. TMS's 0.2 s 'exiting wall' flag; the MIT Godot controller's time_bef_can_wallrun_again 0.2 s (feel-web.md section 1).

iceline40._why: Builder L2 (NIGHT40.md L2; GG: level 2's rooms 'need a complete overhaul to better support the new gauntlet mechanic'; 'players should not have access to the pistol at the start of level two'): level 2 as n40-iceline (from n37-iceline; n37-iceline untouched).
iceline40.enabled_why: Off until the lead has looked at its Player frames once and iterated once (NIGHT40.md method 2).
iceline40.startSet_why: GG: no pistol at level 2's start; L2 adds `awards` with the revolver in the armoury zone.
iceline40.awards_why: GG ask 14 ('unlock them later in the level when entering certain zones'): the KESTREL is given on entering n40-iceline's 2.6 THE ARMOURY (room g6, after the gauntlet's five lessons g1-g5; Design/levels/n40/iceline.beats.md). Given once, as the unlock table's room award (SurvivalSim.N40 N40RoomAwardsStep).
iceline40.budgetCost_why: The wave budget's cost of the three kinds n40-iceline places (LevelValidate29.Budget knows husk 1, swarmer 0.5, spitter 2, heavy / tank 6 from design.n27.budget; it has no cost for these): a level-authoring number, no gameplay effect. WARDEN 4 (200 hp behind a shield: between a spitter and a heavy), DRONE 2 (30 hp, ranged: a spitter's), CHARGER 4 (150 hp, a heavy's charge but no tank's hp). Unity-only; the web has no wave budget.

brawl40._why: Builder B2 (NIGHT40.md B2; GG: 'The second boss fight should be completely redesigned into a brawler-style encounter'): the brawler on n40-iceline's last room. B2 adds its numbers with their _why.
brawl40.enabled_why: Off until the lead has looked at its Player frames once and iterated once (NIGHT40.md method 2).
brawl40.name: THE ICEBREAKER
brawl40.name_why: The working name (DECIDE40 D-3: GG may rename it). The boss bar and the name card read it.
brawl40.arena_why: The arena's boxes (Tools/night/gen-n40-brawl-arena.cjs): 36 x 36 m of ice, 8 m ride walls on the rim, four pillars to break line, the entry gap on +z. Built as world layer brawl40Arena at the boss room row's brawl40.centre (n40-iceline's x9 THE BRAWL), as THE STAG's canal was built at its row's centre.
brawl40.salt_why: Mixed into the run's seed for the fight's own Mulberry32 (rule 6: per-run randomness).
brawl40.pool_why: Hit points. Tuned for the bot band 30-60 s (boss_rules 7, DECIDE39 D-1): the PULSE's heavy swing lands 192 per 2.5 s (design.n27.pulse27 damageMult 6 x weapons.gauntlet.damage 32) and the KESTREL 25 per shot, both in full only up close. Measured (`n40brawl band`, the skilled mixed pilot, 10 seeds, round 1: the haymaker only): 2400 -> p50 19.3 s; 6000 -> p50 44.6 s, p90 46.3 s, 10/10 killed, damage gauntlet 69 % / KESTREL 28 % / punch 3 %. Research/2026-10-14-wave40/B2.md.
brawl40.revealSeconds_why: The walk-in: it stands and turns to face you, no damage, no attacks (walkin36's reveal; THE STAG used 1.5 s).
brawl40.phase2At_why: Phase 2 at half its bar (boss_rules 6: ULTRAKILL splits health about evenly, Minos Prime 65 + 65, Gabriel 50 + 50; research/boss-web.md section 1).
brawl40.phaseSeconds_why: The phase change: no damage, no attacks, the kit's beat (a banner, a flash, a push away). boss_rules 6: a 1-2 s transition.

body.height_why: A hunched giant, twice the player's 1.8 m: big fists, a small head (enemies-web.md section 4: squares for tanks). The view draws its model to these.
body.radius_why: The torso's hit sphere and the body's footprint (the clamp, the pillars, the range rule measures from this surface).
body.fistRadius_why: Each fist's hit sphere (a shot at the glowing fist lands too).
body.margin_why: Metres the body keeps from the rim walls beyond its radius (boss_rules 4: every position clamped to the arena rect minus a margin).

move.walkSpeed_why: Its walk at the player in phase 1, metres per second: under the player's ground speed (the run's maxSpeed), so a player can always open distance; a brawler that comes to you (the husk walks 6).
move.walkSpeed2_why: Phase 2's walk: faster (boss_rules 6: phase 2 changes the attack set or the arena; V2's Brutal: 'movement and attacks 50 % faster', we take ~27 %).
move.turnRateDeg_why: Degrees per second it turns toward the player while walking (x1.5 in a wind-up's tracking share): a circle-strafe at speed gets behind it.
move.stopDist_why: Metres off its body's surface where it stops walking (it does not push into the player).

range.close_why: Metres from its body's surface within which a gun lands x1 (NIGHT40.md B2: 'x1 at <= 4 m'; the Marauder's open band ~3-4.5 m, research/boss-web.md section 5).
range.far_why: Metres at and beyond which a gun lands farMult (NIGHT40.md B2: '~x0.2 beyond 12 m'); linear between close and far.
range.farMult_why: A gun's share from far away (NIGHT40.md B2 '~x0.2'). The pistol from range alone must take >= 3x a mixed fight (the card's check, `n40brawl range`).

stagger.meter_why: The STAGGER meter's full value per phase (Minos Prime's stamina pattern, 6 then 12; ours 6 then 8). Only the gauntlet and the punch drain it.
stagger.gauntlet_why: Meter points per PULSE swing that lands: two swings (or one swing on the stuck fist) open the window in phase 1.
stagger.punch_why: Meter points per F punch (the gun in hand): the weaker melee.
stagger.stuckMult_why: While its fist is stuck after the haymaker: every hit x1.5 and melee stagger x1.5 (the punish window, Minos Prime's stuck fist).
stagger.windowSeconds_why: The window when the meter empties (it reels): every hit x windowMult (design.n37.boss37.windowSeconds 2.5).
stagger.windowMult_why: Every hit's multiplier in the window (after the range rule: a gun from far is still weak).

rest.seconds_why: Seconds between attacks in phase 1 (it walks at you meanwhile): under design.n37.boss37.restSeconds 1.5, a brawler keeps the pressure on.

haymaker.windup_why: The heavy wind-up (boss_rules 1: heavy >= 0.9 s): the fist rises and glows red-orange; a RED tell36.
haymaker.windup2_why: Phase 2's wind-up: still at the heavy floor 0.9 s.
haymaker.trackShare_why: It turns with you for the first 70 % of the wind-up, then commits (THE STAG's charge locks at 70 %): a late dash beats it.
haymaker.startDist_why: Metres off its body within which it starts a haymaker (else it keeps walking): a step and a lunge reach you.
haymaker.active_why: The swing's length: the lunge and the hit test.
haymaker.lunge_why: Metres it lunges along its committed facing during the swing.
haymaker.reach_why: Metres past its body's surface the fist reaches (from the lunge's end).
haymaker.coneDeg_why: Half-angle of the swing's cone: a dash sideways out of it (or a jump over its head) is the answer (boss_rules 2).
haymaker.damage_why: Health the player loses to a haymaker (a heavy: THE STAG's charge did 25-35).
haymaker.knock_why: Metres per second of horizontal knockback along its swing.
haymaker.knockUp_why: Metres per second up with the knockback.
haymaker.stuckSeconds_why: Seconds its fist stays stuck in the ice after the swing, hit or miss: the punish window (Minos Prime's stuck fist 'about a second'; boss_rules 2 ~1 s).
haymaker.recover_why: Seconds it takes to pull the fist free before it walks again.

camp.seconds_why: Seconds grounded within camp.radius before its camp answer (the slam on your spot, round 2; design.n37.boss37.campSeconds 3).
camp.radius_why: Metres: staying within 4 m of one spot counts as camping (design.n37.boss37.campRadius).

slam._why: Both fists into the ice: a shockwave ring runs out along the floor (NIGHT40.md B2: 'a shockwave ring: jump or ride over it'). Its camp answer (boss_rules 3: standing still is punished by an attack you can see) and a mid-range pick.
slam.windup_why: The wind-up: both fists over its head, a RED tell36 and a ground ring decal (boss_rules 1: medium 0.65-0.9 s).
slam.windup2_why: Phase 2's wind-up (still inside the medium band).
slam.recover_why: Seconds it stays bent over after the slam (a short punish: about one swing).
slam.ringSpeed_why: Metres per second the ring runs out: it crosses the 18 m arena half in 1.5 s, so a jump timed on sight clears it (the player's jump is in the air ~0.6 s).
slam.ringRadius_why: Metres where the ring dies: the arena's half (18) plus the walls: it reaches every spot of the floor.
slam.ringWidth_why: Metres of slack on each side of the ring's front for the hit test.
slam.ringHeight_why: Metres above the floor the ring reaches: feet higher than this (a jump, a wall ride) pass over it.
slam.damage_why: Health a ring hit takes (a medium: under the haymaker's 30).
slam.knockUp_why: Metres per second up: the ring pops you off the ice.
slam.midChance_why: At mid range (between haymaker.startDist and block.startDist) the chance it slams instead of walking on (never twice running).
slam.chain2_why: Phase 2: the chance a haymaker up close is chained straight into a slam (NIGHT40.md B2: 'phase 2: faster chains').

block._why: A block of ice torn from the floor and thrown when you stay far (NIGHT40.md B2: 'a thrown ice block when the player stays far (YELLOW: parry it back for a stagger)'; ULTRAKILL: yellow = parryable).
block.windup_why: The wind-up: the block raised in its left fist, a YELLOW tell36 (boss_rules 1: medium).
block.recover_why: Seconds after the throw before it walks again.
block.startDist_why: Metres off its body past which it throws (it walks at you meanwhile): the range a gun lands at x0.5 or less.
block.speed_why: Metres per second the block flies (the flight time is distance / speed, at least 0.35 s): readable, slower than the spitter's glob's parry window allows (16 m/s glob, design.n36 parry).
block.gravity_why: Metres per second squared on the block (a lob that still arrives at the aim point).
block.radius_why: The block's hit radius against the player's capsule and the parry's reach measure.
block.parryReach_why: Metres from the eye a punch (or a gauntlet swing) reaches the block (THE STAG's chunk: design.n37.stag37.chunk.parryReach).
block.parryConeDeg_why: Half-angle of the punch's cone for the block.
block.returnSpeed_why: Metres per second the parried block flies home.
block.parryDamage_why: Damage the returned block lands on it (in full: a parry hit), about one swing's worth less: the punch-back is the far answer, the gauntlet the close one.
block.stagger_why: Meter points the returned block drains (NIGHT40.md B2: 'parry it back for a stagger'): with one swing it opens the window in phase 1.
block.bufferSeconds_why: A punch this early still parries the block when it arrives in reach (design.n36 parry36's 0.12 s buffer).

rush._why: A shoulder charge along a locked line when the player is far (NIGHT40.md B2: 'a rush when the player is past ~15 m'); a wall or pillar stops it dazed (the CHARGER's rule, Charger.cs: stunned on a wall).
rush.windup_why: The wind-up: it lowers its head and paws, a RED tell36 and a ground line along its path (boss_rules 1: light 0.45-0.65 s); it turns with you for the first 60 %, then the line locks.
rush.startDist_why: Metres off its body past which it may rush (NIGHT40.md B2 '~15 m').
rush.speed_why: Metres per second of the charge: under the CHARGER's 22 (Charger.cs) on a small arena; a dash sideways clears its 1.2 m half-width easily.
rush.maxSeconds_why: The longest charge (it crosses the arena's diagonal) before it stops on its own.
rush.hitRadius_why: Metres past its body's radius the charge hits the player's capsule.
rush.knock_why: Metres per second of knockback along the charge.
rush.stuckSeconds_why: Seconds it is dazed after running into a wall or a pillar: the punish (as the haymaker's stuck fist; every hit x stagger.stuckMult).
rush.recover_why: Seconds after a charge (or a daze) before it walks again.
rush.chance_why: Past rush.startDist: the chance it rushes rather than throws (it never does the same far attack twice running).

floes._why: Phase 2's arena change (NIGHT40.md B2: 'Phase 2 at 50 %: faster chains, the ice cracking into floes'; boss_rules 6: phase 2 changes the arena): the floor as a grid of floes; one cracks where the player is heading (RED), then is open water that bites a grounded player. No geometry changes (the room's floor stays under it), so nothing falls: the arena changes what is safe to stand on.
floes.grid_why: Floes per side: 6 x 6 floes of 6 m on the 36 m arena (a floe is two strides across: one dash clears it).
floes.every_why: Seconds between cracks in phase 2 (with floes.open 4 s at most two floes are water at once).
floes.tell_why: The RED crack before a floe opens (boss_rules 1: an area attack shows a ground decal; heavy >= 0.9 s since it denies ground).
floes.open_why: Seconds a floe stays open water before it freezes over.
floes.dps_why: Health a second on open water (grounded): a nudge to move, never a trap (the haymaker is 30).
floes.tick_why: Seconds per bite (the damage lands in 0.5 s bites: 6 health each).
floes.lead_why: The floe that cracks is the one under where the player will be 0.6 s from now at his velocity (the anti-run line), else the one he stands on.

line._why: The boss line (B5's BossLine40; boss_rules 5: the damage rule taught on entry with the bound buttons, every hit answers). Resolved by the lesson widget: {fire} {punch} {dash} {jump}.
line.entry: GET IN CLOSE: {fire} THE GAUNTLET HITS FULL
line.entry_why: On entry (and once more after the first death): what hurts it, in one line. Short: the lesson box takes ~52 characters with the button names (n40-r3: the longer line was cut off).
line.far: TOO FAR: SHOTS BARELY SCRATCH IT
line.far_why: Every 4th gun hit landing at x0.5 or less (8+ m away), at most 3 times a fight: a hit that does little says why.
line.stuck: ITS FIST IS STUCK: HIT IT NOW
line.stuck_why: The first two times it is stuck (the punish window named).
line.block_why: The first two block wind-ups (the parry named; the gauntlet's swing parries it too).
line.seconds_why: Seconds a line stays up (the stuck and block lines half as long).

loom40._why: Builder B4 (NIGHT40.md B4; GG: 'The STITCHER weapon should be removed from the fourth level entirely'; THE LOOM 'often runs out of the map'; no-ride zones, more in phase 2; DECIDE40 D-7, D-12): level 4 as n40-span (from n38-span; n38-span untouched), the tear by the grapple, the STITCHER out of the campaign.
loom40.enabled_why: Off until the lead has looked at its Player frames once and iterated once (NIGHT40.md method 2).
loom40.dropWeapons_why: D-7: the STITCHER leaves every campaign start set and award while loom40 is on (survival keeps it); tied to loom40 so THE LOOM never needs nails nobody has.
loom40.marginM_why: m: THE LOOM's stations and body centre stay inside THE CANYON's (o3) floor plan minus this (boss_rules 4). Its feet reach 9.8 m along the canyon from the centre (kneeSpreadZ 7 x 1.4) and its knees 9 m across (kneeSpanX), so 10 keeps the whole machine inside. MEASURED before (n40loom stay, loom40 off): a camper in o2 dragged the body 43.7 m out of o3.
loom40.glideMax_why: m/s: the top speed of THE LOOM's glide between stations and onto a camper (stationSpeed's 36-40 m/s crossed a 36 m station step in one second: a jump cut, GG 'often runs out of the map'). 18 m/s is about the player's dash speed: a move the eye follows. Ours.
loom40.glideAccel_why: m/s2: the glide eases up at this and brakes onto its goal (v <= sqrt(2 a d)): 0.75 s to full speed, a 36 m station step in ~2.75 s. Ours.
loom40.homeS_why: s after the last anti-hide before the leg's station goes back to its own place (NIGHT39 never put it back; the MMO leash: return home when the chase ends). Longer than the hide rule's 3 s (design.n37.boss37.hideSeconds), so a player still hiding keeps it over them.
loom40.legHoldMaxS_why: s: a leg change is held open (no attacks) until the body arrives at its new station, at most this past the change's own 1 s (design.n37.loom37.kit.legChangeSeconds): the glide is now ~2.75 s, and the leg change is the phase's transition (boss_rules 6: 1-2 s announced). The old 36 m/s glide existed to fit the 1 s change (stationSpeed_why).
loom40.floorY_why: m: THE CANYON's void floor (n38-span / n40-span o3: the floor boxes' bottom, design.n37.loom37.fallY_why 'the void floor at -24'): THE LOOM's death fall stops with its feet on it (footDropY above it). MEASURED before: the fall went 27.6 m under it.
loom40.lineS_why: s each boss line stands (Core/BossLine40, B5's: boss_rules 5 'the damage rule is taught on entry'): teach35's showS (design.n35.teach35.showS 5).
loom40.lineRule: HOOK A LIT KNEE {grapple}. THEN {grapple} PULL AWAY.
loom40.lineRule_why: THE LOOM's damage rule on entry (the lead's line, NIGHT40 round 2): the grapple hooks a lit knee (it latches), a pull to another thread tears it (Core/Enemies/Loom37.N40.cs Latch40).
loom40.lineLatch: HOOKED. NOW {grapple} PULL AWAY TO A THREAD.
loom40.lineLatch_why: shown on the first two latches of a fight: the second half of the rule, at the moment it applies.
loom40.lineOpen: OPEN: SHOOT THE CORE. EVERY GUN COUNTS.
loom40.lineOpen_why: shown on the first CYAN window: every weapon lands in full there (Boss37 Scale: Open -> 1).
loom40.noRideWarnS_why: s the canyon's next no-ride walls blink before they refuse a ride (D-12: 'switched at the leg change behind a 1 s warning flash').
loom40.practiceBackS_why: s after o2's practice knee tears before it is back (a rehearsal: try again at once). Ours.
loom40.spoolTurnDeg_why: deg/s a live spool turns toward the player's chest, its speed kept (boss_rules 2: its answer is the parry, a dash past it still works). MEASURED round 3 (n40loom stay --on): with straight spools a strafing pilot was never close enough to parry, and legs 2-3 need one parry (design.n39.boss39 loom stagger 7.5): the leg waited 19 s on lashes until the pilot died.
loom40.tearHeal_why: health a torn knee gives back (Doom Eternal's blood punch: the aggressive move refills). MEASURED round 3: the deaths were falls (-20 each, design.n37.loom37.fallCostHp) plus a lash (-30); the tear is the fight's right move.

crown40._why: Builder B5 (NIGHT40.md B5; GG: 'players have no idea what to do, and even I don't know how to damage it'): level 5 as n40-spire (from n38-spire; n38-spire untouched), THE CROWN taught. B5 adds its numbers with their _why.
crown40.enabled_why: Off until the lead has looked at its Player frames once and iterated once (NIGHT40.md method 2).

ring._why: B5 round 2 (Research/2026-10-14-wave40/B5.md D3 / D4 / D7 / D8; boss_rules 4): where THE CROWN's ring may be (Core/Enemies/Crown37.N40.cs). The web has no CROWN.
ring.hoverDistance_why: m (flat) from the player (NIGHT37: 5). At 5 m the ring (3 m) and its blades (1.6 m) spanned ~85 deg of the view and filled the screen (frames f0700, f1000); at 8 m ~60 deg: the whole ring and the space through it read at once. A jump-dash reaches 21 m (Harness crown37 jumps), so 8 m stays in one pass. A hypothesis, judged on the Player's frames.
ring.coreMargin_why: m kept between the ring's rim and the spire's core (the core's half width 4 m, the ring's radius 3 m): the ring never cuts into the core's wall (D3: 9.9 % of fight steps did, frame f0500).
ring.roomMargin_why: m kept between the ring's rim and the boss room's walls (boss_rules 4: every position clamped to the arena rect minus a margin).
ring.repositionSpeed_why: m/s of the anti-hide's flight onto the player (NIGHT37 teleported, Crown37.cs:407): 2.7x its 11 m/s hover, so it closes 20 m in under a second and is seen doing it (boss_rules 1: tell every move).

crown40.fallDamage_why: hp a fall costs in the descent (NIGHT37 crown.fallDamage 20). Falls are part of the descent: the skilled pilot fell 4.7 times a fight and died once in 9 of 10 fights with no attack hit taken; the casual pilot fell ~10 times and died twice (n40crown defects, round 1). The leg's checkpoint is still the cost (the climb and the time); 5 keeps a sting.

line._why: B5 (boss_rules 5: 'the damage rule is taught on entry, one line with the bound buttons'; GG 2026-10-13: 'players have no idea what to do, and even I don't know how to damage it'). The entry line THE CROWN shows when its fight begins (Core/BossLine40.cs through the lesson widget: {dash} and {jump} become the bound buttons), shown again after the first fall or death (maxShows 2 per fight). The web has no boss lines.
line.entry: FLY THROUGH THE RING: {dash} DASH + {jump} JUMP
line.entryPad: FLY THROUGH THE RING: {dash} DASH + {jump} JUMP
line.seconds_why: Long enough to read the line twice and look at the ring (the widget's 18 px line; the Lantern's lineSeconds was 3 for a 4-word line, this one is 7 words with two buttons). A hypothesis: no published number for a boss line's time was found (research/boss-web.md section 6).
line.maxShows_why: Once on entry, once more after the first fall or death (the moment a person who missed it needs it); never more (Teach30's budget was 2 per fight).
line.ringPrompt_why: n40-spire's v10 THE RING lesson (empty since NIGHT37), written into the level by Tools/night/gen-n40-spire.cjs: the fight's pass rehearsed with the same two buttons. Six words: a room lesson's limit (levelgen's lesson rule, Design/levels/CURRICULUM.md); the boss line above has no such limit.

foes40._why: Builder E3 (NIGHT40.md E3; GG: 'a few more enemy types, including ones that fire projectiles you can deflect'; DECIDE40 D-11): the ported DRONE, WARDEN and CHARGER in the campaign, retuned (their survival numbers unchanged). E3 adds its numbers with their _why.
foes40.enabled_why: Off until the lead has looked at its Player frames once and iterated once (NIGHT40.md method 2).

drone.chargeS_why: The DRONE's glow before its orb (s; the web's drone.chargeTime 0.4 s). NIGHT36's tells36 already makes it 1.0 s (design.n36.tells36.droneChargeS); foes40 holds 1.0 s even with tells36 off: ULTRAKILL's Stray throws 1-2 s after it spots you (https://ultrakill.wiki.gg/wiki/Stray); the low end, because the drone's orb is the slowest shot the player meets.
drone.orbSpeed_why: m/s of the DRONE's orb in the campaign. The card asked '~14 m/s, slower'; the port's orb is already 12 m/s (config orb.speed, read 2026-10-14), slower than the spitter's glob (16 m/s), so it is kept at 12: at 12 m/s the orb crosses the punch's reflect reach (orb.reflectRange 2 m) in 0.17 s, longer than parry36's 0.12 s buffer. ULTRAKILL's Drone shot is 27.86 u/s on Harmless vs V1's 16.5 u/s walk (https://ultrakill.wiki.gg/wiki/Drone): ~1.7x walk; ours is ~1.3x the player's ~9 m/s run.
drone.approachSpeed_why: m/s the DRONE flies to its slot (the brain caps it at ai.kinds.drone.speed 7 m/s x the drone's paceMult, set to approachSpeed / 7 at its spawn in Drone.cs; its climb and hover keep drone.speed). 0.6x the husk's 6 m/s: ULTRAKILL's Stray (the parry teacher) moves at 10 u/s, 0.61x V1's walk (https://ultrakill.wiki.gg/wiki/Stray). A slow drone stays where the player can read its glow and punch its orb back.
drone.reflectKillsShooter_why: A parried orb that reaches the DRONE that fired it kills it (its damage raised to the drone's hit points). parry36 already homes a parried orb on its shooter (Parry36.cs) and bursts 40 in 3 m; with parry36 off the web's return (orb.damage 10 x reflectDamageMult 2 = 20) leaves a 30 hp drone alive. The card: 'a reflected orb kills or staggers it'; the drone has no stagger (drone.js), so it kills. Doom: The Dark Ages: a parried projectile homes back to whoever fired it (https://www.shacknews.com/article/144239/how-to-parry-doom-the-dark-ages).

warden.meleeShield_why: Only a melee knock (the punch, the PULSE gauntlet's swing) opens the WARDEN's shield (its 1 s stun, warden.shieldStun, kept). The port opened it for ANY knock from the front, so the THUNDERCLAP's knock broke it too: n40foes ttk (2026-10-14) measured the shotgun killing a warden in 3.9 s, the gauntlet in 5.0 s, the revolver 17.3 s: the gauntlet was not its answer. The card: 'the WARDEN is the gauntlet's: its punch-stun stays the answer, a flank the other' (Halo's Jackal: a front shield you open, then the kill, https://www.halopedia.org/Kig-Yar/Gameplay).
warden.frontSoft_why: x a front hit the shield already softens (design.n26.weaponIdentity.vulnerability.warden.soft 0.2, so x0.1 in all; the gauntlet and the punch still land whole). With meleeShield alone n40foes ttk measured the shotgun at 5.5 s against the gauntlet's 5.0 s (the THUNDERCLAP's volley is ~200 raw, so 0.2 of it still kills); the card asks the counter to be >= 1.5x faster.

charger.frontMult_why: x the damage of every hit on the CHARGER while it is not stunned, and of a stunned hit from its front (its armour; stunned from behind x charger.weakMult 3 as before: the stunned back is the one open spot). n40foes ttk (2026-10-14) measured the KESTREL killing a 150 hp charger from the front in 2.4 s, faster than any back attack: the card's 'jump or ride its charge, then its stunned back (x3)' paid nothing. Doom Eternal's Pinky: hit its tail after dodging its charge (https://www.thumbsticks.com/how-to-exploit-demon-weaknesses-doom-eternal/). 0.3 is a guess tuned by the matrix.
charger.stunS_why: s stunned after a charge into a wall (charger.stunTime 1.5): long enough to run round it and fire one THUNDERCLAP shot into its back (the shot's interval is ~1.5 s, CODE-MAP; boss_rules 2: a punish window of ~1 s after an attack, plus the walk round).

parry42._why: Builder W1 (G4, GG: 'the parry attack timing from the flying enimies is relaly tight and you miss depsite felling like you hit it'; DECIDE42 D-3: orbs only): the DRONE orb's parry forgives (a larger reach, a mercy window after contact, a longer early buffer; ULTRAKILL 1.03b, hitfeel-web.md). W1 adds its numbers with their _why.
parry42.enabled_why: Off until its check passes and the lead has looked at its before / after Player frames and iterated once (NIGHT42.md method 2; closing_reminder).
parry42.reachMult_why: DECIDE42 D-3: the orb's reach 1.5x orb.reflectRange (2 m -> 3 m), measured as a volume: the orb's surface to the body's axis (eye down to the capsule's lower sphere), not the eye's point (ULTRAKILL 1.03b: 'changed from a raytrace into a hitbox', hitfeel-web.md section 4).
parry42.mercyS_why: ULTRAKILL 1.03b: '3 mercy frames between a projectile hitting the player and the damage happening' (50 ms at 60 fps); doubled to 0.1 s (12 steps) because GG misses 'despite feeling like you hit it': a press in the same rendered frame as the touch at 30-60 fps plus input latency still parries. The orb waits at the contact point meanwhile.
parry42.orbBufferS_why: DECIDE42 D-3: parry36's early buffer (0.12 s) doubled for orbs only: a punch or a gauntlet swing that sent nothing back still parries an orb that comes into reach within 0.24 s (an orb at 12 m/s covers 2.9 m: about the new reach).
