W1 adds its numbers with their _why.
charge42.enabled_why: ON at the NIGHT42 freeze: n42-r3 weapons42 vs -skygrindOff42: shots while fire is held through the KESTREL's cooldown 7 -> 1, charge42Rearm 0 -> 1, a second charged shot False -> True; looked at W42-held-rearm (CHARGING under the KESTREL, the arc starting); iterated: the reel's hold (n42-r2 showed 3 re-arms, no second shot).
charge42.cannonTurnS_why: G8 (GG: 'complete animation before you can preform necxt attack'): after a charged shot (KESTREL or THUNDERCLAP) the gun's next shot waits this long, the reticle's cannon turn (spin + snap; reticle42 draws it in this time). 0.46 s is inside the KESTREL's tap interval (0.483 s, design.n39.p39 x1.2), so a tap right after the cannon loses at most nothing of its rhythm; NIGHT41's turn was 1.82 s and a tap fired through it (CODE-FACTS G10 / G8).

impact42._why: Builder F1 (G9 + G15, GG: 'hits and kills need to feel more satifying'; 'a greater or mor epowerful effect when hitting it or any other enemy iwth gaughtlent'): hitstop per weapon on a hit, a bigger freeze on a kill, the gauntlet's the strongest, THE ICEBREAKER's the biggest (hitfeel-web.md's numbers). F1 adds its numbers with their _why.
impact42.enabled_why: ON at the NIGHT42 freeze: hits42 n42-r3 GREEN: THUNDERCLAP 58 -> 85 ms, gauntlet on a husk 83 -> 143 ms, on a tank 123 -> 183 ms (KESTREL kept: its 50 ms is the headshot freeze); n42hit: THE ICEBREAKER frozen 6.5 -> 8.9 % of the fight, kill times unchanged; looked at H42 off / on ghusk.
impact42.gauntletHitS_why: G15 ('a greater or mor epowerful effect when hitting it or any other enemy iwth gaughtlent'): a gauntlet hit on any body freezes 0.16 s, above heavy41's 0.14 s big-kind freeze and crunch36's 0.1 s punch (ULTRAKILL's punch). hitfeel-web.md number 4: 0.05-0.08 s on a strong or melee hit, 0.10-0.15 s on a finisher; the PULSE swing is the game's finisher-weight blow (one swing per 1.8-2.5 s), so it sits just above that band and under ULTRAKILL's major hitstop 0.25 s (number 1), which stays the parry's.
impact42.gauntletBigS_why: A gauntlet hit on a big kind (design.n41.heavy41.kinds: the TANK, the WARDEN, the CHARGER) freezes 0.2 s: the weight GG asked the gauntlet to have against large enemies (w40). hitfeel-web.md section 1: fighting games stop 6-10 frames (0.10-0.17 s) on a heavy attack and 12-18 frames (0.20-0.30 s) on a boss super; this is the bottom of the super band.
impact42.gauntletBossS_why: A gauntlet hit on a boss body (THE ICEBREAKER and every Loadout.IsBoss34 body) freezes 0.24 s, the biggest hit in the game (NIGHT42.md F1: 'THE ICEBREAKER's hit the biggest'), just under ULTRAKILL's major hitstop 0.25 s (hitfeel-web.md number 1) and the perfect parry's 0.3 s, so a parry still reads as the top moment.
impact42.gauntletKillS_why: A gauntlet kill freezes at least 0.22 s (a boss hit's 0.24 still wins): longer than a plain gauntlet hit, the finisher (hitfeel-web.md number 4: 0.10-0.15 s on a finisher, raised for the gauntlet's slow cycle; number 10: DOOM keeps its finishers to hundreds of ms).
impact42.gauntletCooldownS_why: The shortest real time between two gauntlet freezes: the web's gauntlet cycle 0.42 s (PortExport/config.json weapons.gauntlet), so a faster swing rule (a mod, a shorter pulse27) can never chain freezes into a stall.
impact42.gauntletPerMinute_why: The gauntlet's freezes take at most this share of any rolling minute (4.8 s), their own budget beside design.impact.budget.perMinute 0.06 (the shared one: kills, headshots, punches); over it a freeze is cut to what is left. A boss fight landing every 1.8 s swing on the boss would ask 33 x 0.24 = 7.9 s a minute; the share holds it to 8 % of real time (SimHarness n42hit measures it).
impact42.heavyHitS_why: A heavy gun hit (a rocket's direct hit, a rail hit, a THUNDERCLAP shot landing design.impact.freeze.heavyPellets pellets in one body) freezes 0.06 s (was 0.03): hitfeel-web.md number 4's strong-hit band 0.05-0.08 s.
impact42.killS_why: A gun kill freezes 0.085 s (was 0.058): GG's G9 'hits and kills need to feel more satifying'; hitfeel-web.md number 4: a finisher 0.10-0.15 s; the body kill is the most common moment, so it sits under that band, 10 sim steps, and two still fit design.impact.budget.perSecond 0.2.
impact42.headshotKillS_why: A headshot kill freezes 0.12 s (was 0.096): the finisher band 0.10-0.15 s (hitfeel-web.md number 4).
impact42.punchKillS_why: A punch kill freezes 0.13 s (was 0.108): a melee finisher, the band's middle (hitfeel-web.md number 4); the gauntlet's kill is gauntletKillS.
impact42.killCapS_why: A step with N kills freezes killS + design.impact.freeze.killPerExtra x (N - 1), at most 0.18 s (was 0.155): a THUNDERCLAP blast through 5 husks freezes 0.18 s; under design.impact.budget.perSecond 0.2, so it is never cut alone.

bodyHitByWeapon._why: A gun's non-kill body hit freezes by weapon (the weapon id of the hit event), inside crunch36's body budget (bodyHitCooldownS, bodyBudgetPerSecond); a weapon not listed keeps design.n36.crunch36.bodyHitS. Each value's reason is its _why key.
bodyHitByWeapon.revolver_why: The KESTREL's body hit freezes 0.024 s (crunch36: 0.018): hitfeel-web.md number 3, Nuclear Throne's 10-20 ms on an ordinary bullet hit, a step above for the slow, heavy pistol (one shot per 0.4 s): about 3 sim steps.
bodyHitByWeapon.shotgun_why: A THUNDERCLAP volley's body hit (under heavyPellets pellets) freezes 0.036 s: between the ordinary bullet (number 3) and the strong-hit band 0.05-0.08 s (number 4); a full volley in one body is heavyHitS.
bodyHitByWeapon.nailgun_why: A STITCHER nail's body hit freezes 0.012 s: the bottom of Nuclear Throne's 10-20 ms (number 3), because it fires about 10 nails a second (crunch36's bodyHitCooldownS 0.15 and bodyBudgetPerSecond 0.1 still cap the stream).

brawl42._why: Builder B1 (G14, GG: 'level 2 boss might needs more attacks and needs to be more difficult'; DECIDE42 D-5): THE ICEBREAKER gains two new attacks with fair tells (RED tell36, red-orange, >= 0.9 s), each with its own answer: the SWEEP (a low spinning arm up close: JUMP it; the haymaker's answer is a dash, so up close the player must read which) and the LEAP (from mid range it jumps onto the spot you stood on: DASH out of the locked circle; it lands stuck, the punish). Phase 2 harder: shorter rests, a haymaker chains into a sweep, the leap's landing sends the slam's ring. Never more HP (GG w31-32): pool, stagger and the damage rule are NIGHT40's. Sweep / Sekiro's read-the-answer grammar (sweep = jump, thrust = deflect, research/boss-web.md section 1 'Others'); the leap after Minos Prime's 'Judgement!' dropkick (a tell, a committed landing). Numbers measured with `n42brawl` (Tools/SimHarness/Harness.N42.Brawl.cs); Research/2026-10-14-wave42/B1.md.
brawl42.enabled_why: ON at the NIGHT42 freeze: brawl42 reel GREEN on n42-r1 / r2 / r3 (sweep 0.90 s, leap 1.10 s tells, all answered); brawl40casual with it 53.9 -> 81.6 s, 10/10 in the harness; skilled p50 48.6 -> 55.9 s (46.2 with gauntlet42), never more HP; looked at B42-sweep-tell and B42-leap-lock (r1: amber, thin); iterated (3ea7665d): a red-orange filled disc (r3: reads as danger).
brawl42.rest2_why: Phase 2's rest between attacks (NIGHT40's design.n40.brawl40.rest.seconds2 0.8): faster chains, every wind-up still >= 0.9 s (DECIDE42 D-5 'phase 2 faster').

sweep._why: THE SWEEP: up close it drops, cocks its right arm low and back (RED tell36 at the fist, a red-orange ring on the ice at its reach), then spins once with the arm at shin height. Answer: JUMP as the arm comes (feet above sweep.height when it passes you), or dash out of its reach. Then it is dizzy (sweep.recover): the punish.
sweep.windup_why: The wind-up (boss_rules 1: heavy >= 0.9 s; DECIDE42 D-5 'red-orange >= 0.9 s').
sweep.windup2_why: Phase 2's wind-up: kept at the 0.9 s floor (phase 2 is harder by its rests and chains, never by a shorter tell).
sweep.active_why: Seconds the arm takes for one full turn. It starts on the far side from you, so it reaches you after half of it (0.2 s after the tell ends): a jump pressed from ~0.3 s before the tell ends to ~0.1 s after it clears (the jump holds the feet above 0.5 m for ~0.5 s: config jump.height 1.5, apexTime 0.36).
sweep.recover_why: Seconds it stays dizzy after the spin (no attack, it turns slowly): about one gauntlet swing to punish.
sweep.reach_why: Metres past its body's surface the arm reaches (the haymaker's lunge + reach is 5.1): the skilled pilot circles at 2.5 m, the casual at 3.5 m, both inside it.
sweep.startDist_why: Metres off its body within which it may pick the sweep instead of the haymaker.
sweep.height_why: Metres above the floor the arm reaches (the slam ring's 0.5): feet higher pass over it.
sweep.armDeg_why: Degrees of slack on each side of the arm's line for the hit test (the arm is a thick box, not a line).
sweep.damage_why: Health a sweep takes (a medium: under the haymaker's 30, over the slam's 20).
sweep.knock_why: Metres per second outward (away from its body) on a hit.
sweep.knockUp_why: Metres per second up on a hit (it trips you).
sweep.chance_why: Within sweep.startDist: the chance it sweeps instead of the haymaker (never two sweeps running): up close the player must read which one is coming (a high cocked fist: dash; a low arm and a ring: jump).
sweep.chain2_why: Phase 2: the chance a haymaker up close is chained into a sweep after its stuck fist (when the slam chain did not fire): the punish window ends in a tell you must jump.
sweep.spins2_why: Phase 2: the sweep spins this many times (each turn sweep.active long, each pass can hit once): the arm passes you at 0.2 s and 0.6 s after the tell, one jump stays over 0.5 m ~0.5 s, so the second pass wants a second jump (the double jump, config jump.doubleJumps 1) or a dash out of reach. Phase 2 harder by a new answer, not a shorter tell (round 2: with gauntlet42's 1.8 s swing the skilled band fell to p50 43.7 s).

leap._why: THE LEAP: from mid range it crouches (RED tell36 at its head) and a red-orange landing circle tracks you on the ice; at leap.trackShare of the wind-up the circle LOCKS (it brightens), then it jumps and lands on it: a hit inside the circle, then its fists are stuck in the ice (the punish, every hit x stagger.stuckMult). Answer: DASH (or run) out of the locked circle. Phase 2: the landing also sends the slam's ring (jump it). The answer to keeping your distance (NIGHT40's block / rush are far answers; the leap closes the gap).
leap.windup_why: The wind-up: 1.1 s, the circle tracking for the first 0.66 s then locked for 0.44 s + the air time (~1 s from the lock to the landing; boss_rules 1 heavy >= 0.9 s).
leap.trackShare_why: The circle follows you for the first 60 % of the wind-up, then locks (the haymaker locks at 70 %, the rush at 60 %).
leap.air_why: Seconds in the air from the jump to the landing.
leap.apex_why: Metres up at the top of the arc (above the 3.6 m body: it reads as a jump).
leap.startDist_why: Metres off its body past which it may leap (between the haymaker's 5 and the block's 9).
leap.chance_why: Past leap.startDist: the chance it leaps rather than its NIGHT40 pick (never two leaps running).
leap.radius_why: Metres round the landing spot it hits (the body's 1.2 + 2 m of shock): one dash (24 m/s x 0.25 s = 6 m) clears it from anywhere inside.
leap.hitHeight_why: Metres above the floor the landing reaches: a hop does not answer it, leaving the circle does.
leap.damage_why: Health a landing takes (a heavy, under the haymaker's 30).
leap.knock_why: Metres per second outward from the landing spot on a hit.
leap.knockUp_why: Metres per second up on a hit.
leap.stuckSeconds_why: Seconds its fists stay in the ice after the landing, hit or miss: the punish (the haymaker's stuck fist is 1.2).
leap.recover_why: Seconds to pull free before it walks again.
leap.ring2_why: Phase 2 (1 = on): the landing sends the slam's shockwave ring (design.n40.brawl40.slam's ring numbers): dash out of the circle, then jump the ring.

arena42._why: Builder K1 (G12, GG: 'way better arena deisgn for the gameplay. more elements that are not just decoration'): arena elements that change play (a hazard enemies are knocked into, breakable cover, a launch pad, ...), each with a sim rule, a view and a level-data form (arenas-web.md, ARENA-KIT.md). K1 adds its numbers with their _why.
arena42.enabled_why: Off until its check passes and the lead has looked at its before / after Player frames and iterated once (NIGHT42.md method 2; closing_reminder).

grinder._why: THE GRINDER (level JSON `grinders42`: [{rect: [x0, z0, x1, z1], y, room}], Core/Arena42.cs): a pit floor of blades. Any enemy whose feet touch it is ground at once, the player's kill (the traps' path, weapon trap), event arena42Ground; went in knocked or in the air -> style GROUND. ULTRAKILL pays for using the arena as a weapon (https://ultrakill.wiki.gg/wiki/Style: an enemy into a pit, Fall 80). Walkers never walk in (nav mask + edge guard). The web has no grinder.
grinder.touchMargin_why: The feet count as touching at or below the grinder floor y + this (Lava30's touchMargin, design.n30.lava: a body standing on the floor always reads as in it).
grinder.playerDamageFraction_why: The player who falls in loses this share of max health per touch (lava: 0.25; the grinder sits in a pit you climb out of, so a touch costs a little less).
grinder.knockUp_why: The player is knocked up this many m/s on a touch (lava's knockUp 9: the same hop out, Mover.Launch).
grinder.graceSeconds_why: No second hurt for this long after a touch (lava's graceSeconds).
grinder.groundStyle_why: The style bonus GROUND for a body that went in knocked or in the air: ULTRAKILL's Fall / Minced / Shredded are 80 each (https://ultrakill.wiki.gg/wiki/Style, arenas-web.md).
grinder.maskAbove_why: A nav node whose column is in a grinder rect and stands at most this many m over its floor is closed to walkers (a walkway higher up stays open; ai33's lava mask works the same).
grinder.guardMargin_why: The edge guard's band round the rect, m: a walker the player did not knock that enters it is put back (a husk's radius is 0.4, so it never hangs over the rim).
grinder.guardAbove_why: The edge guard acts up to this many m over the grinder floor (a 4 m pit's rim and a step over it); a walkway higher up is not guarded.

cover._why: BREAKABLE COVER (level JSON `cover42`: [{min: [x, y, z], max: [x, y, z], hits, room}], Core/Arena42.cs): a solid box in the world (the sim layer arena42Cover). Each player shot that ends on it takes a hit; at 0 it shatters (event arena42CoverBreak): the shards hit every enemy within burstRadius and push them away; shards that hit a body pay SHATTER. ULTRAKILL 0-1 / 4-2 glass floors and walkways that break (arenas-web.md). The web has no breakable cover.
cover.hits_why: Shots a box takes when its level row gives no `hits` (about 1.5 s of KESTREL fire: a fight's cover, gone if you camp behind it shooting).
cover.burstRadius_why: The shatter hits every enemy whose aim point is within this many m of the box centre (a crowd at the cover, not the room).
cover.burstDamage_why: The shards' damage per body: more than a husk's 40 hp (PortExport husk.hp), so a shatter kills the husks at it and hurts the heavy kinds.
cover.burstPush_why: The shards push a surviving body away from the box at this many m/s (Enemy.Knockback): toward a grinder when the level puts one behind the cover.
cover.burstPushSeconds_why: The push lasts this long (whole steps): about 2.7 m.
cover.shatterStyle_why: The style bonus SHATTER when the shards hit at least one body (under GROUND's 80: the arena as a weapon, the smaller trick).

reticle42._why: Builder W1 (G8, GG: 'animation for redical for all weapons needs to spin faster and complete animation'): every weapon's reticle turn faster (view numbers in UnityTuning.*42.cs); the attack gate is charge42's.
reticle42.enabled_why: Off until its check passes and the lead has looked at its before / after Player frames and iterated once (NIGHT42.md method 2; closing_reminder).

meter42._why: Builder U1 (G7, GG: 'the meter or how the pulse or charge attack works field award and ... needs to be polished and more accurate'): the arc40 meter shows the true charge / cooldown each frame (no eased under-read, the PULSE swing cooldown shown).
meter42.enabled_why: ON at the NIGHT42 freeze: ui42 n42-r2 / r3: 754 frames, meter42 0 mismatches vs arc40 44 (worst 0.173), false FULL 0 vs 301, the PULSE swing shown (74 frames); iterated: the reel's inputs (n42-r1 RED: no press reached the gun).

style42._why: Builder U1 (G13, GG: 'styule meter ... needs to feel aweosme to combo and UI needs to be animated'): the style meter redesigned: rank letters that punch in, shake and decay (DECIDE42 D-6), combo count; motion on every change.
style42.enabled_why: ON at the NIGHT42 freeze: ui42 n42-r2 / r3: 2 rank ups, combo 6, 6 awards; looked at U42-s-up2 (x6, B BOLD, +40 CLOSE CALL) and the brawl42 frame (x2, D DULL, +20 QUICKDRAW); iterated (86342b9c): the award line inside the right edge, the letter's ghost off after the punch.

health42._why: Builder U1 (G13, GG: '... heathbar need to look better'): the health bar redesigned: a damage chunk that drains, a heal glow, motion on every change.
health42.enabled_why: ON at the NIGHT42 freeze: ui42 n42-r2 / r3: the damage chunk 3 ticks at +0.03 / +0.3 s, 0 at +1.0 s; heal glow 3 ticks; looked at U42-h-chunk (73, three red-orange ticks); iterated with style42's slice (the shared Health33 split).

kills42._why: Builder F1 (G9 / G15): the kill's view (a burst, a crunchier break, KillFeel42) and the gauntlet's shockwave ring; view only.
kills42.enabled_why: ON at the NIGHT42 freeze: hits42 n42-r2 / r3: rings 4, kicks 2, flinches scaled 3; looked at H42-on-ghusk-050 (r2: the double ring covered ~70 % of the screen); iterated (eaf62434): rings 0.22 -> 0.075 band, half as bright, capped at 9 deg (r3: a cyan burst on the husk, the view clear).

n43._why: NIGHT43, the cohesion night (GG 2026-10-16 after playing n42-r4 up to level 3; thirty asks verbatim in Research/2026-10-16-wave43/GG-REQUEST.md as G1-G30; NIGHT43.md; DECIDE43.md; CODE-FACTS-A.md / CODE-FACTS-B.md; docs/DESIGN-RULES.md). Every row is off in the shared commit and turned on only when its check passes and its before / after frames were looked at. Sim rows (chimney43, ride43, boost43, foundry43, gauntlet43, parry43, fusion43, rooms43, iceline43, kiln43, burrow43, wick43) are behind N43Blocks; the view rows (hud43, counter43, teach43, screens43, bossbar43, feel43, models43, look43) are N43View rows (no bit). Off (--off43 / -skygrindOff43, and every older off switch): NIGHT42's game bit for bit. The level rows swap levelFrom for levelTo (Curriculum25.N43Levels); an n43 level is its levelFrom to every older system (SurvivalSim.N43BaseId through N42BaseId).

chimney43._why: Builder M1 (G13 + G2, GG: 'after a certain number of jumps or transitions, the player simply cannot consistently make the movement work. Fix this at the movement-system level'): the wall-jump count (wallJump.maxPerAirtime 3, refilled only by a landing; CODE-FACTS-A A2) refills on a NEW wall (Titanfall / ULTRAKILL research), so a climb between facing walls never silently turns a press into the double jump. M1 adds its numbers with their _why.
chimney43.enabled_why: ON at the NIGHT43 freeze: M1 harness: a 4.5 m chimney by presses 5.58 -> 13.53 m top; one SameWall rule (re-ride refusals on THE STACK pilot 11 -> 0); the chain lever (box FLUE taps 0 -> 16/40); B1's WICK bands 10/10 with it; the move43 reel's pilot never reached a wall in the Player (n43-r2 / r3): judged on the harness and the round-4 verbs check.
chimney43.newWallDot_why: A wall jump off a wall whose horizontal normal is less than this dot with the last wall jump's (about 26 deg apart or more) is a NEW wall: the count (wallJump.maxPerAirtime 3) refills first (DECIDE43 D-1; research/movement-web.md A5-A6: Dave's tutorial refills on a normal change, cr-parkour's same-wall test is dot >= 0.9). A chimney's facing walls (dot -1) and THE STACK's spiral panels (90 deg apart, dot 0) are always new.
chimney43.newWallDist_why: Metres along the ground from where the last wall jump left: a parallel wall (or the same plane) farther than this is a new wall too (DECIDE43 D-1). Horizontal only, so climbing one face straight up never refills (the same wall still spends: no endless climb on one face).
chimney43.chainWindow_why: Round 2, the chain (GG's G2: 'the walls should be slightly closer together so that even though the player is moving quickly, the rapid bounce from wall to wall naturally carries them upward'): a pressed wall jump off a NEW wall within this many seconds of leaving the last one (a wall jump, a jump-off, a ride's end) is a chain jump (chainUp / chainOut). A chimney's crossing at speed takes ~0.45 s.
chimney43.chainUp_why: Round 2: a chain jump's up speed (m/s; the plain wall jump's 1.0 x v0 = 8.33, wallfling42): it arrives at the facing wall still rising, so each bounce gains height (n43move flue, L1's tap pilot, 4.5 m: 2/40 -> 16/40 to the deck).
chimney43.chainOut_why: Round 2: a chain jump's speed out from the wall (m/s; wallfling42's 5): a shorter flight across the gap (less height lost on the way).
chimney43.rideRefills_why: A ride that starts on a new wall (the same test) refills the count too (NIGHT43.md M1 chimney43), so a ride, a press and the next wall never run out.

ride43._why: Builder M1 (G3, GG: 'clunky and buggy, sometimes snaps too aggressively, sometimes causes the player to fall off awkwardly, and can conflict with other inputs such as pressing B'): the ride's attach / hold / detach made forgiving and readable: a softer attach (wallgrip36's 1.5 m/s rise clamp), a longer lostGrace, a wider attach probe, no slam from B in the first moments after a ride (CODE-FACTS-A A3: B after a ride = a slam to (0,-48,0)), a buffered jump-off. M1 adds its numbers with their _why.
ride43.enabled_why: ON at the NIGHT43 freeze: M1 harness: B 0.1 s after a ride a drop keeping 15.97 m/s (was a slam to (0,-48,0)); near misses 0/12 -> 8/12 held; a dash into a wall attaches (seen in the move43 reel n43-r2: dash attaches 1); sub-rule (e) off after B1's casual WICK regression (3/10 -> 10/10); judged with the round-4 verbs check.
ride43.tapDraw_why: (a) wallride35's near-miss draw (attachPull 4 m/s into a wall beside the motion) also when jump is not held (a tap ride, with ride40's intent: the stick into the wall). Was hold-only (CODE-FACTS-A A1).
ride43.attachReach_why: (a) the swept attach probe: rays ahead-diagonal of the motion reach this many metres past the capsule plus this step's move (at 16 m/s one 120 Hz step is 0.13 m: research/movement-web.md B9 'a swept probe, 0.35-0.6 m for ATTACH while keeping 0.12 for STAY'). The stay probe (wallRide.probeDistance 0.12) is unchanged.
ride43.keepRise_why: (b) the snap: wallgrip36 clamps a rising attach to 1.5 m/s at once (a jump at ~8 m/s up stops dead: the 'snaps too aggressively' of G3). With ride43 the attach keeps this share of the rise (never under the clamp), then the rising entry brakes by gravity as before (8.3 m/s -> 4.2, about 0.37 m more rise).
ride43.lostGrace_why: (c) seconds a ride survives a probe that finds no wall (wallride35's lostGrace 0.05): a facet's edge or a seam between panels no longer drops you (research/movement-web.md B10: cr-parkour lostGraceMs 120).
ride43.slamGrace_why: (d) seconds after leaving a wall (any ride end, a wall jump, a jump-off) during which B (slide) in the air is a DROP that keeps the horizontal speed (a rise cut to 0), not a slam: a slam sets (0, -48, 0) and kills every m/s (CODE-FACTS-A A3; DECIDE43 D-2).
ride43.slamLookDeg_why: (d) looking down more than this many degrees below level, B inside the grace is the slam after all (an aimed slam stays possible; DECIDE43 D-2).
ride43.holdNoStick_why: (e) OFF since round 2 (measured): waiving ride40's intent (the stick into the wall) while jump is held caught players holding jump on walls they were passing: B1's `n43wick casual --blocks wick43,ride43` killed THE WICK 3/10 with it (the casual bot held jump past the hot shaft wall and the ledges' faces: 222 deaths), 10/10 without it (every other ride43 sub-rule on). ride43.lockPlane_why: (f) ride40's 0.2 s lockout (walls facing within 30 deg of the ended ride's) only for the SAME wall: a parallel wall whose plane is more than this many metres from where the ride ended is not locked (THE FLUE's stepped panels).
ride43.dashAttach_why: (g) a dash in the air that meets a ridable wall it heads into attaches at once, along the wall at the dash's exit speed (DOOM Eternal's climb walls: dashing into one grabs it; research/movement-web.md B7). The locks, the re-ride rule, noride, ride40's clearance and wall height still apply.
ride43.dashIntoDot_why: (g) the dash must head into the wall at least this much (dot of the dash direction with -normal): a dash grazing a wall it runs along does not attach.
ride43.bufferDeg_why: (i) flow34's wall buffer holds a jump press for a wall ahead within the jump buffer (0.1 s) only for an approach steeper than 30 deg (wallRide.awayDot 0.5): a press 0.05 s before reaching a wall at the usual ride approach (10-30 deg) was the double jump (n43move jumpseq, before). With ride43 an approach from this many degrees off the wall line holds it too, so the press becomes the wall jump / the hold ride on contact.
ride43.holdReach_why: Round 2 (a'): with jump held, the sideways near-miss draw reaches this many metres past the capsule (ride40 cut wallride35's to 0.5 m): a player holding jump in a 4-4.5 m lane is drawn onto a wall (n43move flue, L1's held pilot: 4.5 m 16/40 -> 27/40 with the chain, 4.0 m 0/40 -> 31/40; L1 found 3.5-4.0 m lanes never started a ride). Jump held is the intent (e).
ride43.sameWallDeg_why: Round 2 (the lead's card, G13 at the root), the ONE 'same wall' every NIGHT43 rule uses (Move43.SameWall): facing within this many degrees (wallride35's reRideDeg 30) ... (the next four keys). Used by the re-ride rule, ride40's 0.2 s lockout, the ride lock, the wall-jump lock (ride43) and chimney43's new wall (a wall jump off a wall that is not the same wall refills the count; chimney43's newWallDot / newWallDist are no longer read).
ride43.sameWallPlane_why: ... and its plane within this many metres of where the player left it (a parallel wall behind is another wall: was lockPlane, (f)) ...
ride43.sameWallAlong_why: ... and along the ground within this many metres (wallride35's reRideDistance 3) ...
ride43.sameWallRise_why: ... and less than this many metres higher than where the player left it: a wall face 1.5 m or more above is a NEW wall (THE STACK's panel a turn up stands 11.2 m straight above; the lead's card: the re-ride rule refused it within 3 m horizontal until a landing) ...
ride43.sameWallDrop_why: ... and less than this many metres lower: falling back down the wall you just left (a missed leap) catches you again instead of a fall to the floor (n43move stack trace: a missed panel fell past the one it left with re-ride refusing it).
ride43.pressPushes_why: (h) a jump PRESS on a ride with the wall-jump count empty is the jump-off (wallride35's push, no spend), never the double jump straight up with no push (CODE-FACTS-A A2 'cap empty: EndRide + 7.5 up, no push off'). The lead's note: GG's pad shows the bottom face button as B = JUMP, so 'pressing B' in G3 may be this.

boost43._why: Builder M1 (G26, GG: 'When I press jump and shoot downward at approximately the same time, I do not receive nearly enough height'): the THUNDERCLAP boost combines jump + shot inside a window (a ground press just before the jump fires in the air; a shot just after leaving the ground boosts in full), the jump cut never halves a boost (CODE-FACTS-B G26: releaseMult 0.5 halves it today), boost42's lift by pitch. M1 adds its numbers with their _why.
boost43.enabled_why: ON at the NIGHT43 freeze: M1 harness: jump + shot within +-0.15 s 1.48-5.08 m -> 6.33-7.98 m; no jump-cut halving; K1's kiln steps landing 36 -> 82 % (step 1) and 13 -> 54 % (step 2); level 3 gates 7/7 with K1's headroom (G1 +10 -> +56 %).
boost43.window_why: (a) the combine window, seconds: a ground THUNDERCLAP hold still inside its tap split when you take off fires on the takeoff step in the air; a ground volley aimed below level up to this long before the takeoff boosts on the takeoff (research/movement-web.md C13: TF2 treats a shot just before the jump as airborne; NIGHT43.md M1 boost43 a). charge40's shotgunTapS is 0.15 too.
boost43.lift_why: (c) m/s up a boost gives at fullDeg below level or steeper (boost42's shape: a fall cut to -fallFloor first, then + lift; scaled by sin(pitch) / sin(fullDeg) above fullDeg). 11 vs 12 measured in Research/2026-10-16-wave43/M1.md (n43move boost).
boost43.fullDeg_why: (c) degrees below level from which the boost is full (boost42's 40).
boost43.doubleKeeps_why: Round 2: a double jump never lowers a rise (the Mover's vy = max(vy, the double's 7.5 m/s)): a jump press just after a boost set vy to 7.5 and erased the boost (the move43 reel on n43-r2: jump + shot pressed on one frame, the press repeated on the frame's second sim step became the double jump: the rise 1.36 m both halves).
boost43.fallFloor_why: (c) a fall is cut to this many m/s down before the lift (boost42's 3): a late shot still climbs.

parry43._why: Builder W1 (G18, GG: 'the player currently has to wait until an incoming projectile is extremely close'; CODE-FACTS-B G18: a ~0.11 s window from the eye point): the orb parry intercepts farther: parry42's surface-to-body reach and mercy, plus a swing that reaches along the orb's path and a buffered press. W1 adds its numbers with their _why.
parry43.enabled_why: ON at the NIGHT43 freeze: W1: presses in the last 200 ms 11/24 -> 24/24, the earliest parry 1.94 -> 5.61 m; n43-r3 weapons43 Player: an orb PARRIED pressed at 3.62 m (the off pass: missed); globs the same rules (9/24 -> 24/24).
parry43.reachMult_why: parry42's volume (DECIDE42 D-3), kept as test 1 of three: the orb's surface within 1.5x orb.reflectRange (3 m) of the body's axis (the eye down to the capsule's lower sphere). parry43 reads its own copy so parry42 can stay off (D-10 open).
parry43.mercyS_why: parry42's mercy (ULTRAKILL 1.03b's 3 mercy frames, doubled): a touching orb waits 0.1 s (12 steps) at the contact point before its damage; a press in that time still parries.
parry43.catchRadius_why: THE CATCH VOLUME's radius (m), test 2: ULTRAKILL catches projectiles in a 3 m sphere 3 m ahead (combat-web.md A1, Punch.cs); sized to the gauntlet's 2.4 m reach (NIGHT43.md W1: radius ~1.5 m centred ~2 m ahead). The orb's surface (orb.radius 0.35) inside it is caught: up to 2 + 1.5 + 0.35 = 3.85 m along the aim.
parry43.catchAhead_why: The catch sphere's centre, m ahead of the eye along the aim (NIGHT43.md W1: ~2 m). Its near edge reaches back to 0.5 m ahead of the eye, so nothing between the sphere and the body volume is missed.
parry43.windowS_why: THE TIME WINDOW, test 3 (combat-web.md A3: 'express the window as time (distance / closing speed), not metres, so fast and slow orbs feel the same'; the genre band for a deliberate parry is 150-200 ms of time to impact, NIGHT43.md W1 asks >= 0.2 s at 12 m/s): an orb that, flying on as it flies, touches the player within 0.25 s (30 steps; 3 m at 12 m/s) is caught from any side. 0.25 s sits just above the band because the press also has to cross input and frame latency.
parry43.bufferS_why: The early buffer (NIGHT43.md W1: 'a 0.15 s early buffer on the gauntlet swing too'; ULTRAKILL buffers a punch 6 physics frames, ~0.12 s, combat-web.md A2): a punch or a gauntlet swing that sent nothing back keeps catching for 0.15 s (18 steps) through parry42's orb buffer (Core/Parry42.cs), so a press made just before the orb reaches the volume still parries when it does.

fusion43._why: Builder W1 (G19, GG: 'If the player performs a high-speed dash impact or gauntlet attack, create a powerful special feedback response'): a gauntlet hit or punch landed at high speed (a dash, a ride jump-off, a slide) is a FUSION: more damage, a knockback, a stagger, the event fusion43 (N43Events.Fusion) for F1's view. W1 adds its numbers with their _why.
fusion43.enabled_why: ON at the NIGHT43 freeze: W1: dash-in hits 0 -> 100 % FUSION (x2, knock, stun), the held swing 30/35 -> 35/35; n43-r3 weapons43 Player: FUSION YES at 22.8 m/s, 955 damage; E1's g6 lane 12/12.
fusion43.speedMin_why: A melee hit is a FUSION when the player's horizontal speed at the hit is at least 14 m/s (NIGHT43.md W1: '>= ~14 m/s'): above the ride's 9-13 m/s and a sprint, under the dash's 24 m/s, so only a launched / boosted body or a dash reaches it.
fusion43.dashAfterS_why: ...or the hit lands during a dash or within 0.25 s (30 steps) after it ended (NIGHT43.md W1): the dash lasts 0.25 s (config dash.duration), so a press up to one dash-length late still fuses (the 'dash INTO it' lesson, iceline43).
fusion43.rideJumpS_why: ...or within 0.35 s (42 steps) of a jump off a wall ride (NIGHT43.md W1: 'a ride jump-off'): about the wall jump's rise, so a jump off the wall into an enemy below fuses.
fusion43.damageMult_why: A FUSION hit's damage x2 (NIGHT43.md W1: 'x2 damage'): the PULSE swing's 192 becomes 384 (before momentum: Combat.Damage's own melee momentum still rides on top), a husk-class body dies to one; the punch's 10 becomes 20.
fusion43.bossDamageMult_why: On a boss body (Loadout.IsBoss34) the FUSION multiplies by 1.5 only: GG's boss band (DECIDE39 D-1: one to two minutes for a person, bot 40-70 s) is measured by `n43weap band --fusion` (THE ICEBREAKER's skilled pilot dashes in).
fusion43.knockSpeed_why: The FUSION knock, m/s away from the player (the gauntlet's 7 m/s doubled, weapons.gauntlet.knockback): the body is thrown, not pushed. A boss body ignores knocks (its own Knockback is empty).
fusion43.knockTime_why: Seconds of that knock (the gauntlet's 0.2 s x1.5): ~4 m of travel at 14 m/s with the slide's decay, out of melee reach.
fusion43.staggerS_why: The FUSION stagger (NIGHT43.md W1: 'a 0.6 s stagger'): Enemy.Stun, the longer stagger wins; its attack in progress is cancelled. Boss bodies keep their own stagger rules (their Stun is empty).
fusion43.hitstopS_why: The FUSION freeze (NIGHT43.md W1: 'a hitstop tier above the gauntlet's (0.22 s)'): over impact42's gauntlet hit 0.16 s, big 0.20 s and its kill 0.22 s (equal to the kill: the fusion wins the step as its own tier); combat-web.md B10: an empowered dash impact 18-30 steps (0.15-0.25 s). ImpactRules' Fusion43 tier, out of the shared gap.
fusion43.bossHitstopS_why: On a boss body (NIGHT43.md W1: 'boss 0.28 s'): over impact42's boss gauntlet hit 0.24 s and ULTRAKILL's parry TrueStop 0.25 s, under the perfect parry's 0.3 s.
fusion43.perMinute_why: The FUSION freezes share the gauntlet's rolling-minute budget (impact42's gauntletPerMinute 0.08 = 4.8 s a minute; ImpactRules counts gauntlet + fusion freezes together): over it a FUSION freeze is cut to what is left (never a stall).
fusion43.reachBonus_why: While a FUSION is ready (the conditions above) the gauntlet's swing and the punch reach this many metres farther when nothing is in their normal reach (NIGHT43.md W1: 'a dash INTO an enemy ... the swing's reach +1 m while dashing'): at 24 m/s the dash covers 0.2 m a step, so the extra metre is ~5 steps of forgiveness on the press.
fusion43.cooldownS_why: At most one FUSION in 0.5 s (60 steps): one dash (0.25 s + the 0.25 s after) gives one, so a punch chain inside it is not three bursts and three freezes.
fusion43.holdS_why: THE HELD SWING (the lead's round 2, G19's 'a dash press 5 m+ away still misses'): a gauntlet swing that finds no body while a FUSION is ready waits up to 0.2 s (24 steps) and lands the moment a body comes into the FUSION reach (2.4 + 1 m). At 24 m/s the dash closes 4.8 m in 0.2 s, so a press at the dash's start lands on a body up to ~7-8 m ahead (`n43weap fusion`'s grid). The swing's cooldown runs from the press.

rooms43._why: Builder E1 (G5, G22, G4): a room's door counts only its own enemies (CODE-FACTS-A B9: EnemiesAlive is the whole level), a body out of its room or in a dry pit is ended, a verb lesson never blocks a clear forever, a stuck enemy on screen is moved, a wave can wait for a lesson (wave.afterLesson), 'heavy' is a real kind or a tank. E1 adds its numbers with their _why.
rooms43.enabled_why: ON at the NIGHT43 freeze: E1: doors open after every kill path 17/64 -> 64/64 (68/68 on the n43 levels), the longest still enemy 6.3 -> 2.7 s, waves wait for the player to step in (enemy-seconds in view 118 -> 58.6), fallReturn43 with by; rooms43 reels n43-r2 / r3: the counter 3 -> 1 and the door opening seen.
rooms43.endS_why: G5 (NIGHT43.md E1: 'an enemy out of its room's bounds, under its floor or in a dry pit for > 2 s ends'): a room's own body that stays outside its room's box or under its floor this long is ended (alive false, no kill event, no points), so a husk knocked into THE GANTRY's or PIERCE's dry 4 m pit, or one that fell through geometry, never holds the door (CODE-FACTS-A B9.3: only lava and the -30 m kill plane killed them). 2 s lets a body that is only passing a pit's lip or hopping a gap come back first (the husk's hop is ~0.6 s).
rooms43.pitDropM_why: Under its room's floor = the feet more than 1.5 m below the lowest of the room's spawn and nodes (the places a body of this room is meant to stand). Levels 1-3's dry pits are 4 m deep (CODE-FACTS-A B5), a step or a ramp's foot is under 1 m, so 1.5 m is a pit and never a floor detail.
rooms43.outMarginM_why: Out of its room = the feet more than 2 m outside the room's rect and its nodes' box (x / z). 2 m is a door's depth beyond the rect's line (the doors are 4 m wide, a body stepping into the doorway is still in), and a drone's orbit stays inside its room.
rooms43.heavyKind_why: G22 (NIGHT43.md E1: "'heavy' maps to a real heavier kind (name it)"): levels 3 and 5 list 'heavy' (kb3 x2, v2, v6) and Husks.Make made a plain 40 HP husk of it (CODE-FACTS-B Enemies). The TANK (design.n29.tank: a husk body with 600 hp, the gauntlet x10, drawn 1.4x and darker) is the game's heavy and the validator already prices 'heavy' and 'tank' the same (LevelValidate29: costHeavy).
rooms43.maxTopUps_why: G5: with rooms43 on a room re-spawns its last wave for an enemy-needing lesson at most twice (design.n25.lesson.maxTopUps: 12, ~3 minutes of re-spawns holding the door: CODE-FACTS-A B9.4), then the enemy lessons are passed over (lessonTopUpCap) and the door opens on the room's own count. Two top-ups give a player who killed the husks before the lesson two more tries.
rooms43.lessonCapS_why: G5 (CODE-FACTS-B: 'a lesson that needs a verb (not an enemy) can block the clear forever'): once a fight room's enemies are all dead, a lesson still not done is marked done after 8 s (the event lessonCap43) and the door opens: the line has shown its verb for its 5 s (teach35's showS) plus a breath, and the room never holds a player who cannot or will not do it.
rooms43.afterLessonMaxS_why: G4 / afterLesson43: a wave that waits for a lesson comes in anyway 20 s after the room's entry (or retry), so a player who does not perform the taught verb is never left in an empty locked room (PIERCE: 'HOLD {jump} ON A WALL', then the enemies arrive). 20 s is four times teach35's 5 s line.
rooms43.onScreenRelocateS_why: G22 ('fail to move'; NIGHT43.md E1: 'the watchdog relocates a stuck enemy ON screen too ... after ~2 s'): the web's watchdog (ai/watchdog.js) hops, side-steps and re-paths at 0.5 / 1 / 1.5 s and relocates only OFF screen after ai.watchdog.relocateAt (CODE-FACTS-B: HuskBrain.cs:1141), so an enemy stuck in view stood there for the fight. With rooms43 on, in a campaign run, an enemy stuck 2 s in view (the ladder's three rungs tried) gets a tell and a short step.
rooms43.onScreenTellS_why: The on-screen relocation's tell (event navTell43 with the enemy's id: the view's flash / shimmer) before the step: ULTRAKILL-style readability, a body never pops without a warning. 0.35 s is the spawn tell's order of time (spawn33) cut to a blink, short enough that the stuck spell ends at ~2.4 s.
rooms43.onScreenStepMinM_why: The step's target: the nearest free nav node at least 1.5 m from the stuck enemy (a capsule's diameter plus a margin, so it leaves the corner it was stuck in) that still reaches the player (NavField.Relocate's field test, a full circle round the enemy).
rooms43.stillNudgeS_why: G22 (NIGHT43.md E1: 'no enemy stands still > 3 s while the player is in reach'): an enemy not in an attack that has moved under stillMoveM in 2 s near the player takes a new wait spot (its strafe flips and its ring angle jumps half a strafe cycle; a swarmer's flank side flips). Measured by `n43rooms still` (every enemy on screen, alive 20 s): the ring waiters (swarmers 4.8 s, a husk 4.3 s) and a dazed charger (6.3 s) stood longest. 2 s keeps the longest still spell under 3 s with a think's slack.
rooms43.stillMoveM_why: Still = the feet moved less than 0.5 m (x / z) since the spell began: a body holding its ring spot (the strafe's own drift is under that within a think or two) or pressed into a wall.
rooms43.stillRangeM_why: The nudge only near the player: within 16 m (the ring's 10 m wait radius plus a spitter's hold), where a still body reads as 'failing to move' (GG G22).
rooms43.unstickS_why: G22: the sim's own check on a room's body (SurvivalSim.N43.Rooms.cs), for what the brain's watchdog cannot see (it counts only while the enemy wants to move and makes no progress): `n43rooms still` found swarmers hung just off the ground at their spawn nodes (grounded false, y 0.1, 'direct' mode, the watchdog's stuck 0) and a charger standing 4.5 m from the player, still 4.8-6.3 s. A body still (under stillMoveM) for 2.4 s within stillRangeM, not in an attack, gets the tell and the step, so no spell reaches 3 s (2.4 + the 0.35 s tell = 2.75 s).
rooms43.standInHoldS_why: Nothing lost (PRINCIPLES 1): in NIGHT42 a room's stand-ins (a lesson's example targets: the KESTREL room's, PIERCE's) counted as alive, so they held the room's first wave until shot (the KESTREL room's order: the stand-ins, then the husks) and also its door. With rooms43 they still hold the next wave, for at most 20 s after the entry (a player who cannot land the shot still gets the fight), and never the door (the lesson gates it, and lessonCapS caps the lesson).
rooms43.commitM_why: G4 / T-4 round 2 ('teach, confirm, then spawn'; CODE-FACTS-A B7: in every arena36 room spawns33's trigger lines are bypassed, Level36.cs:161, so a room's waves started at its entry): a room's FIRST wave waits until the player's feet are 3 m from the room's spawn (the doorway side), i.e. the player has stepped into the room; enemies never stand in view of a player still in the doorway.
rooms43.commitMaxS_why: ...or 3 s in the room (the lead's round-2 card): a player who stands in the doorway still gets the fight after a breath (the arena36 switch-on bubble and spawn33's tells still play).

STEP 3 · AT THE TOP, PRESS {fire} AGAIN

kiln43.chain_why: K1 (G26; kiln40's chain shape, PRINCIPLES 2: one step shown when the last is done): the THUNDERCLAP's boost taught on THE STEPS: step 1 split into its three verbs (jump, look down, fire: kiln40's lines), step 2 asks the shot WITH the jump, step 3 the second shot at the top (two shots; one boost and the boost + the double fall short; a double pressed against the face is a wall kick-off backwards, so the double is taught in the open shaft of 3.1b), then the summary, 3.1b THE FLUE (THE CLIMB: shot, double, shot, 12 m) and the slug (kiln40's last line); then, on entering 3.2c THE ASH BED (`at`: a line waits for its room), the BURROWER's two lines (its room has no Campaign24 lesson: a lesson there could hold the door after the fight, G5). Each 'top' line is done when the feet stand on that step (room `room`, the level row's tops43[`top`], written by gen-n43-kiln.cjs), so the words follow the geometry. At most 52 characters resolved (teach35.maxChars); {jump} / {fire} resolve to the bound buttons.
kiln43.lookDownDeg_why: kiln40's lookDownDeg (S1, NIGHT40): 'LOOK STRAIGHT DOWN' is done this far below level.
kiln43.topSlackM_why: K1: a 'top' line is done with the feet within this many metres under the step's top (the grounded capsule stands on it; a hypothesis: the Mover's ground snap is well under 0.3 m).
kiln43.lineFallbackSeconds_why: kiln40's lineFallbackSeconds: a step not done in this time moves the chain on, so the text never sticks.
kiln43.minLineSeconds_why: kiln40's minLineSeconds: a line stands at least this long even when its step is already done.
kiln43.seenSeconds_why: kiln40's seenSeconds: a line with nothing to do stands this long.

burrow43.hp_why: Hit points: 'enough to take a few shotgun blasts' (G28 card): the THUNDERCLAP's volley is 8 x 8 = 64 (83 with shotgunTune's x1.3), so ~3 volleys out of the window, 2 with a counter (x2) in it; the gauntlet's swing (192) nearly kills one, a countered swing kills it. Port-only: the web has no burrower.
burrow43.radius_why: Its body's radius out of the ground (m): a fat worm column, wider than a husk (0.4) so a surfaced one is an easy target in the 0.5 s window.
burrow43.height_why: Its body's height out of the ground (m): it rears up above a standing player's eye (1.6 m) so the emergence fills the view.
burrow43.huntSpeed_why: Its head's speed under the floor (m/s): above the husk's 6 (it is the room's pressure on a player who stands still) and below the walk speed 8, so a player who keeps moving outruns it and a tell only lands on one who stops or slows.
burrow43.digSeconds_why: The spawn's dig-in (s): it is seen screwing itself into the floor (visible and hittable) before it vanishes, so the player knows a burrower is in the room (encounters-arenas-web.md: introduce, never already hidden).
burrow43.tellSeconds_why: The tell (s) between the ring under the player and the emergence (G28 card: 0.8 s; research: 0.7-0.9 s): a jump, a dash out of the ring or a step onto a plate in time.
burrow43.windowSeconds_why: The counter window (s) from the emergence (G28 card: ~0.5 s; research: a 0.4-0.6 s exposed apex): every hit in it deals x counterMult, the first staggers it.
burrow43.surfacedSeconds_why: How long it stands out of the ground after the emergence before it dives (s): the window plus 0.6 s of plain damage, so a late shot still lands.
burrow43.diveSeconds_why: Its sink back into the floor (s), still hittable (a parting shot).
burrow43.restSeconds_why: Buried and still after a dive (s) before it hunts again: the room breathes between attacks (one burrower attacks at most every ~3.3 s with the tell and the surface time).
burrow43.triggerRange_why: Its head within this of a grounded player's feet (m, horizontal) starts the tell (it locks the spot under the player then).
burrow43.emergeRadius_why: The emergence hurts a grounded player within this of the locked spot (m): larger than its body (0.55) so standing at the ring's edge is still a hit, small enough that one dash (or two steps at walk speed in the 0.8 s tell) clears it.
burrow43.damage_why: Damage to the player on an emergence: the charger's 25 (the heavy hit that is telegraphed and dodgeable).
burrow43.launchUp_why: The emergence throws a hit player up (m/s): about a jump and a half (jump 8.33): 'emerge aggressively' (G28), and the player lands away from it.
burrow43.launchOut_why: ... and out from the spot (m/s, horizontal), away from its body.
burrow43.floorTolerance_why: The player's feet within this of its floor's height (m) while grounded count as its ground (it hunts and strikes there); airborne or on anything raised more than this (a metal plate, a deck, a step) the player is safe (G28 card: 'airborne or on metal plates you are safe'). K1: a plate 0.4 m or higher is safe ground.
burrow43.counterMult_why: Damage x this on every hit inside the counter window (G28 card: x2).
burrow43.counterStaggerSeconds_why: A counter (the first hit in the window) leaves it out this much longer (s), staggered (N43Events.BurrowCounter): the special reaction (G28: 'a timing window with a special reaction').
burrow43.buryDepth_why: Buried, its body is this far under its floor (m): beyond every punch, blast and sphere test, so nothing touches it until it surfaces (the trail the view draws is on the floor).
burrow43.maxCount_why: The burrowers' pool (bodies at once): level 3's two burrower rooms place 1-3 (DESIGN-RULES: never more than one worm tell on screen before level 4 is the level's call, K1).

slug43._why: Builder W1 round 2 (G20, GG: 'Charged attacks, especially charged shotgun attacks, should produce more dramatic particles, explosions, enemy reactions'): the charged slug hits like a cannon in the sim: a knockback and a stagger on what it does not kill, a small blast at the impact point. W1 adds its numbers with their _why.
slug43.enabled_why: ON at the NIGHT43 freeze: W1: a husk 6 m ahead thrown 0.95 -> 6.30 m, stun 0.79 s, the 2 m blast kills 3 instead of 1; F1's blast view (feel43 n43-r3: on vs off differ 0.034-0.038 in the centre).
slug43.knockSpeed_why: Every body the charged slug strikes and does not kill is thrown along the shot at 18 m/s (the charged knock today: 2 x the gauntlet's 7 = 14 m/s for 0.2 s, husks only, design.n31.charge.shotgun.knockMult): a cannon, not a push (combat-web.md B13: 'enemies launched'). Any kind: a boss body's Knockback is empty, so bosses stay put.
slug43.knockTime_why: Seconds of that throw (and of the blast's push): ~5 m of travel at 18 m/s with the knock's decay, out of the fight for a beat.
slug43.staggerS_why: The struck body's stun (Enemy.Stun, the longer wins): it cannot answer while it flies and lands (a parry stuns punch.staggerTime 1 s; the slug a little less, it also threw it).
slug43.blastRadius_why: The impact BLAST's radius at the slug's end (the last body struck, or the wall), m to a body's hit sphere (the lead's card: ~2 m): the bodies packed behind or beside the target are caught.
slug43.blastDamage_why: The blast's base damage at its centre: a quarter of the slug's base 192 (8 pellets x 8 x damageMult 3). Combat.Damage's shotgun multipliers ride on it as on the slug (measured `n43weap slug`: the slug lands 624 on A, the blast 86-102 on the husks beside / behind), so the bodies packed around the target die with it (husk.hp 40) and a tank is hurt: the charged slug into a crowd is a small explosion.
slug43.blastEdge_why: The falloff: the blast deals blastDamage x 1 at the centre down to x 0.4 at blastRadius (linear).
slug43.blastKnock_why: The blast pushes each body it hits outward from the impact at 10 m/s for knockTime: the crowd scatters.
slug43.blastStaggerS_why: The blast's stun on what it hits and does not kill (half the struck body's).

torch43._why: Builder W1 round 2 (G20, GG: 'The flamethrower currently feels weak'; combat-web.md: DOOM Eternal's flame belch works because burning enemies change state): an enemy the TORCH hits ignites for a few seconds (a burn tick, a state the views can show), the TORCH's reach ramps in over ~0.2 s. W1 adds its numbers with their _why.
torch43.enabled_why: ON at the NIGHT43 freeze: W1: burning 3 s at 12 dps (after release 22 -> 55 damage), reach ramp 0.2 s; A1's burning look; F1's flame stream (feel43 n43-r3: torch on vs off 0.056 / 0.089).
torch43.burnS_why: A body the TORCH hits burns 3 s after the last flame tick on it (the lead's card: ~3 s; DOOM Eternal's Flame Belch: burning is a state, combat-web.md C11).
torch43.burnDps_why: The burn's damage per second (the TORCH itself: 6.5 per 0.1 s tick = 65 dps, weapons.torch): a body that leaves the cone keeps losing 36 HP over the 3 s, so a sweep across a crowd keeps killing after it.
torch43.burnTickS_why: Seconds between burn ticks (4 a second, 3 each): each tick is a Combat.Damage with weapon 'burn' and shock true (no freeze, no momentum; ImpactRules ignores a wave's share).
torch43.igniteStaggerS_why: A body catching fire flinches 0.3 s (Enemy.Stun; once a burn, a refresh does not): the target changes state when it ignites (combat-web.md C11).
torch43.rampS_why: The flame's reach grows over the first 0.2 s of a spray (combat-web.md C12 (d): 'the first 0.2 s of fire grows reach ... from 50 % to 100 %, so holding it feels like building power'); a pause of more than 1.5 flame ticks starts it again.
torch43.rampFrom_why: The reach at a spray's first tick: 0.6 x (4.2 m of the 7 m); 0.8 x at the second tick (0.1 s), the full 7 m from the third (0.2 s). Not combat-web's 0.5: at 0.5 the first tick (3.5 m) missed a husk 4 m away and its kill took 0.208 s instead of 0.175 s (`n43weap torch`); 0.6 keeps the close fight's first tick.

wick43._why: Builder B1 (G13-G16, G10; GG 2026-10-16: 'the player needs clear feedback explaining whether the boss is taking damage, whether it is vulnerable, what phase it is in'; 'meaningful phases, evolving attacks, and readable transitions'; 'even more cinematic ... if it does not interrupt the game's momentum'; DECIDE43 D-7). THE WICK readable: the boss bar's state for the whole fight (SurvivalSim.N43.Wick.cs N43BossStateFill: valid from the reveal to the dying, hp, the leg's lock, OPEN, the stagger meter, the leg of 3, a hint), the reveal (the look eased toward the rising WICK while the player keeps control; the letterbox is the view's), each leg change a beat (Core/Enemies/Wick37.N43.cs: the recoil, the slag drop, bossLeg43, a gift crack) and one attack variation per later leg (not more HP). Notes and measurements: Research/2026-10-16-wave43/B1.md; harness: n43wick (Tools/SimHarness/Harness.N43.Wick.cs).
wick43.enabled_why: ON at the NIGHT43 freeze: B1: THE WICK's bar valid every live step, leg beats, the reveal (yaw 34.4 -> 0 deg, letterbox), the door without the red / blue split, the shaft speed loss 5.6 -> 0.7 m/s; bands skilled p90 57.4 s, casual 10/10; the bar state for every boss; wick43 reel n43-r2 GREEN.

hints._why: The bar's hint (Boss43State.hint, U1's bossbar43 draws it): what hurts THE WICK now, in the HUD's words, {glyph} tokens for the bound buttons. One line per state, picked in this order: reveal, legChange, stall, window, crack, locked, ember, cap, idle (SurvivalSim.N43.Wick.cs Wick43Hint). The card's two lines are crack and idle (NIGHT43.md B1 G14).
hints.reveal: HOLD {jump}: RIDE. LET GO: LEAP UP
hints.reveal_why: The walk-in's reveal (no damage yet): the climb's verb first (BOSSES.md rule 2: movement is the only way). MEASURED (n43wick climb --off): the HELD ride's jump-off climbs THE STACK (10/10 hands, skilled and casual), a PRESSED wall jump never does (0/10, max feet 3.0 m: it peaks ~1.5 m, the panels rise 2.8 m, 90 degrees round), so the bar names the hold.
hints.legChange_why: The brain's LEGCHANGE second (no attacks, no damage): says the gift crack is coming (legs.giftCrack).
hints.stall_why: Leg 3, the dive's stall at the wall: the launch (design.n37.wick37.boss.dive: a punch while dashing knocks it into the shaft).
hints.window_why: The CYAN window (the stagger meter emptied): full damage from anything (Wick37.Filter: brain.Open).
hints.crack_why: A plate is cracked: a charged KESTREL shot from a ride through the gap lands in full (Wick37.Filter's pierce).
hints.locked: LOCKED: CLIMB TO THE NEXT LEDGE
hints.locked_why: The HP sits on the leg's lock (design.n37.wick37.boss.legLock 0.6 / 0.3): no hit moves the bar until the player stands on the next ledge (the legs are places). CODE-FACTS-B: 'The HP locks read as not taking damage'.
hints.ember_why: EMBER's yellow tell or a glob in the air: the parry returns it into the cage and cracks the plate it hits (the fight's central verb, GG: 'preserve and build upon that').
hints.cap_why: Leg 3 on the cap between attacks: the dive, then its stall is the opening.
hints.idle: CRACK A PLATE: RETURN AN EMBER
hints.idle_why: Anything else: the way in (NIGHT43.md B1 G14's first line).

bosses._why: Round 2 (the lead: DESIGN-RULES B-1, every boss): wick43 also fills the boss bar's state (N43BossState) for THE ICEBREAKER, THE KILN WYRM, THE LOOM and THE CROWN (SurvivalSim.N43.Bosses.cs): HP, the phase / leg, OPEN, the stagger meter and these hints, and emits bossOpen43 / bossLeg43 for them. bosses.window_why: Any boss's CYAN window (THE ICEBREAKER's, THE LOOM's, THE CROWN's): full damage from anything.
bosses.brawlStuck_why: THE ICEBREAKER's fists in the ice after a haymaker / a rush / a leap: every hit x design.n40.brawl40 stuckMult.
bosses.brawlBlock_why: Its BLOCK's tell or a block in the air: the parry returns it and drains the stagger meter (the way to its window).
bosses.brawlHaymaker_why: The haymaker's tell: dash out of its lunge (n40-iceline's rehearsal line '{dash} ASIDE, THEN {fire} ITS BACK'); it sticks.
bosses.brawlSweep_why: NIGHT42's sweep tell (low arm, a ring on the ice): jump it.
bosses.brawlLeap_why: NIGHT42's leap tell (a circle tracking you): leave it before it locks; it lands stuck.
bosses.brawlIdle: PARRY THE BLOCK. PUNISH STUCK FISTS
bosses.wyrmStagger_why: THE KILN WYRM staggered by a head punch (design.n31.wyrm31): the THUNDERCLAP's slug lands in full.
bosses.wyrmCore: ITS CORE IS OPEN: SHOOT IT
bosses.wyrmCore_why: The core open (Wyrm.CoreOpen): its core multiplier.
bosses.wyrmCharge_why: A charge / dive coming (Wyrm.Charging30): the head punch staggers it (design.n30.wyrm30).
bosses.wyrmIdle: PUNCH THE HEAD TO STAGGER IT
bosses.wyrmIdle_why: Anything else: guns land design.n31.wyrm31 gunScale until it is staggered.

reveal._why: G15 / DECIDE43 D-7 (you keep control; letterbox + the camera eased toward the WICK for ~2.5 s the first time, ~1 s on a retry); research/bosses-web.md C.11 ('one in-engine camera move of <= 2 s that ends on the player's own view (or no camera takeover)') and B.8 (first meeting <= 6-8 s, every retry <= 1.5 s). The look ease is the sim's (it is the player's real aim: what you see is where you shoot); the letterbox and the shaft's lights are the view's (Wick43RevealView, UnityTuning.Wick43.cs).
reveal.firstSeconds_why: DECIDE43 D-7: ~2.5 s the first time (THE WICK rises over design.n37.wick37.boss.revealSeconds 2 s: the ease frames the whole rise and lets go as the fight starts).
reveal.retrySeconds_why: DECIDE43 D-7: ~1 s on a retry (bosses-web B.8: every retry <= 1.5 s).
reveal.lookRate_why: Per second at the curve's full weight: the share of the look's angle left to the WICK closed each second (4 x 1/120 = 3.3 % a step: ~85 % of a 90 degree turn closed in the first second at full weight, no snap).
reveal.yieldDeg_why: Degrees in one step (120 deg/s): a turn of the player's own bigger than this ends the ease for this reveal at once (D-7: the player keeps control; a mouse flick or a stick push wins).
reveal.pitchMaxDeg_why: The eased look never pitches past 35 degrees up or down (THE WICK rises from 3 m under the floor to 2 m over the player's head: a framing, not a stare at the floor).

air._why: G10 / G13 ('the player essentially runs into what feels like a brick wall'; CODE-FACTS-A B8 names the shaft's 12.4 m/s clamp a candidate): THE STACK's thick air (design.n37.wick37.air.maxSpeed: every leap of the climb flies the same arc) with wick43 on is never applied on a floor (the run in from the tunnel, a ledge, the floor keep their speed) and in the air bleeds the speed over 12.4 m/s at easeRate instead of cutting it in one step (SurvivalSim.N43.Wick.cs Wick43AirClamp).
air.easeRate_why: Metres per second per second the airborne speed over the clamp bleeds (20 -> 12.4 m/s in 0.25 s: still well before the next panel ~66 degrees round; NIGHT42: in one step).

legs._why: G16 (research/bosses-web.md B.7: 'every transition: the layer breaks on the bar, ~1 s of boss invulnerability with a roar / pose, the arena change happens in view, then a free hit opportunity'; 'phase 2 adds one attack ... not the boss's HP'). The leg change is NIGHT37's (the player stands on the next ledge / the cap); these add the beat and one variation per later leg, built on the same language (Core/Enemies/Wick37.N43.cs).
legs.volleyGap_why: Leg 2: EMBER's second volley this many seconds after the first (3 more yellow globs, aimed again): two parries in a rhythm, inside the attack's own 0.3 s active + 0.5 s recover (no new tell, no longer attack).
legs.leg2Volleys_why: Leg 2's volleys per EMBER (leg 1: design.n37's one).
legs.flareLeg3_why: Leg 3: the FLARE comes back on the cap (design.n37.wick37.attacks.flare.legs [1, 2]): the red half-wipe the player learned on the walls, now on the catwalk.
legs.capFlareHalfDeg_why: Leg 3's flare burns +-55 degrees round the player's angle (the walls' 90 would be half the 4 m catwalk: 34 m of running in a 1.4 s tell). 110 degrees at the catwalk's 11 m middle is 21 m of arc; out of it is ~11 m round (1.1 s at 10.5 m/s) or a dash across the hole.
legs.capFlareWeight_why: Leg 3's flare's pick weight (design.n37's 1.0 on the walls; the DIVE 1.5, EMBER 1.4). MEASURED (n43wick band, 10 seeds, wick43 + chimney43 + ride43 + air.easeRate 30): weight 1.0: p50 54.0 / p90 69.7 s (the cap flare took the DIVE's turns: the stall is leg 3's only opening); 0.4: p50 54.0 / p90 63.6; 0.2: p50 49.3 / p90 63.6 (one seed); no cap flare: p50 50.5 / p90 52.8. The pity (+0.25 a turn) still brings it every few attacks.
legs.capFlareEvery_why: Round 2 (the lead: the band SHORT at p90 63.6 s): after a cap flare's tell the flare leaves leg 3's pick until this many DIVE tells have come (Wick37.N43.cs SetFlareLeg3): the dive's stall, leg 3's only opening, comes at least twice between flares. Measured in Research/2026-10-16-wave43/B1.md (round 2).
legs.slagDrop_why: Metres the slag falls at each leg change (clamped at its start): the arena changes in view and the climb behind you cools (the next leg starts with room under it).
legs.recoilSeconds_why: The recoil's length (the view's cage shudder reads Wick37.recoil43): about half of the brain's 1.5 s LEGCHANGE.
legs.recoilUp_why: Metres the cage is kicked up at the beat (its follow, 6 m/s, brings it back in ~0.4 s): it reads as being hurt.
legs.recoilBack_why: Metres it is kicked away from the player at the beat (decays 5 % a step back toward the axis).
legs.giftCrack_why: When the LEGCHANGE ends, the plate facing the player cracks for design.n37.wick37.boss.crackSeconds (4 s): a free ride-shot to restart momentum (bosses-web B.7's gift window).

Rooms whose waves use the room's shared nodes are not judged (the spawner already keeps every body minSpawnDist 12 m from the player). 12 m = design.n24.campaign.minSpawnDist.
numbers.growthMax_why: The lead's round-2 fix, the general half (NIGHT46): a wave more than 2 x the size of the wave before it is the room's next beat and is never released early: it waits for the full clear. n46flow --trace on n45-iceline (overlap46 on, entryM in): g7's 8 deaths in 10 walks came with wave 2's 7 bodies released on top of wave 1's last of 3 (swarmers + the spitters on the gantries), not with wave 3. A 1-body wave before it never overlaps anyway (shareLeft).

stack.stepArcDeg_why: deg each step spans (6.1 m of arc): room to land and run.

Measured with wyrmTell48 + wyrmDive48 (when 2, windowShare 0.25), 40 seeds: +8 s 138.3 / 179.0 / 85.7 s median / p90 / min (p90 on the band's edge): 0 tonight (windowShare 0.15 holds the min with p90 174.9)

Round 3, when 2, 40 seeds, with wyrmTell48 on too (G31's min): 0.25 131.0 / 157.6 / 44.4; 0.2 130.4 / 158.4 / 59.3; 0.15 135.2 / 174.9 / 64.0 (IN, 2.09 dives a minute); all three B rows at 0.15 132.5 / 174.9 / 64.0 (2.17); wyrmDive48 alone at 0.15 116.6 / 164.2 / 68.5 (2.35): 0.15

loomReach48._why: Sim row (NightRows.On): THE LOOM's hit test. The drawn hull (view, loomHull48) runs 13.6 m long and its outer 3.8 m of each end lie outside the 3 m hit sphere (design.n37.loom37 bodyHalfW 3), so a shot at a visible point passes through (L's n48loom reach, DECIDE48 D-34). The row adds hit capsules along the hull's long axis, from the middle to each point; numbers come from the measurement, not from taste. Off: NIGHT47's sphere (--off48 keeps it).

numbers.radiusM_why: m: each capsule's radius = the drawn spindle's half HEIGHT over its straight middle (UnityTuning.L48.cs: Loom37BodyH 3 x Hull48HeightMul 0.8 / 2; its half width across the near faces is 1.165 m), so a shot at the drawn body's flank or belly lands; the 3 m sphere still covers the middle.
numbers.innerM_why: m along the axis from the centre where each capsule starts: the middle (the two capsules meet there: one segment point to point).
numbers.outerM_why: m along the axis from the centre where each capsule's segment ends: lengthM / 2 - radiusM, so its round end reaches the drawn point at 6.8 m and no further.
numbers.lengthM_why: m point to point of the drawn hull (Loom37BodyL 8 x Hull48LenMul 1.7): the check outerM + radiusM = lengthM / 2 (n48loom reach asserts it); not read by the sim.
numbers.yawFollow_why: share of the angle the long axis turns from world x toward the shooter's broadside: the view's own rule (UnityTuning.L48.cs Hull48YawFollow, which must stay equal), so the capsules lie where the hull is drawn.
numbers.yawMaxDeg_why: deg the long axis turns at most (the view's Hull48YawMaxDeg, which must stay equal).

numbers.minCentrePx_why: px at 1080p: the element's nearest drawn pixel (its dark under-stroke included) must be at least this far from the screen centre: outside the reticle's centre box, whose ticks end 18 px out (NIGHT49.md G1 acceptance and section 1 'Two boxes'; UnityTuning.Hud38BarY's comment). The a149 reel checks the mesh's geometry and the changed pixels against it at 1920x1080 and 1280x720.
numbers.minHeightPx_why: px at 1080p: the element's band (the arc's thickness, a pip's height) must be at least this tall (NIGHT49.md G1 acceptance: '>= 4 px at 1080p'); thinner reads as a hairline at 720p (2.7 px). The a149 reel checks it.

numbers.hueDeg_why: The level's one dominant environment hue (deg; order = LightPlan33.Themes: foundry, iceline, kiln, span, spire). Each is >= 20 deg (Look49AccentMinHueGapDeg) from every role token in UnityTuning.Look49.cs (usable 186, danger 12, parry 44, RIVAL 312, boundary 250): gaps 27.6 / 30.4 / 22.4 / 21.8 / 61.6. Round 2: kiln 72 -> 66 (the lead read n49-r1's kiln as olive mud: 66 is the warmest hue the rule allows), span 280 -> 272 (n49-r1's span floor went pink, near RIVAL: now 39.6 deg from RIVAL). rideKill53._why: EXT53 builder N (row N; GG w35, 2026-10-12, docs/memory/OWNER.md: "The rooms still don't incentivize wall-riding or creative use of the weapons"): RIDE KILL. A player's kill landed while riding a wall (Mover state WallRide), or within numbers.graceS after the ride (the step the ride ended counts as a riding step), pays the rider back numbers.charges boosts (a dash charge: charges x design.stamina.boost.cost of the bar with the bar on, charges x dash.pipCost pips without; capped at the max), on top of the kill's own refill (design.stamina.rewards / n19), and emits `rideKill53` (payload RideKill53Event: the HUD's RIDE KILL callout, GG's sounds). The verb pair is Titanfall 2's wall-run gunplay; the payout is ULTRAKILL / DOOM Eternal's resource-for-aggression rule that design.stamina.rewards already follows. Core/RideKill53.cs (the rule), SurvivalSim.N53.RideKill.cs (the sim), UiRideKill53.cs (the callout). The web has none of these numbers (no reward for a wall ride).

It covers the jump-off shot (VERBS row 11, the jump-off boost) and a shot fired on the wall that lands just after (a KESTREL charge, a short rocket); ride43's lost-wall grace and the flow34 coyote / buffer windows are 0.1-0.15 s, a rocket flies 30 m/s (12 m in 0.4 s), so 0.4 s keeps it a ride verb, not a 'rode recently' buff.

One keeps a ride chain going (ride, kill, boost to the next wall) without refilling the whole bar on one shot (the parry's design.stamina.rewards.parry 1 is the whole bar); a multi-kill on the wall pays each kill, capped at the bar's max.

numbers.muzzleTailS_why: s: when the muzzle flash's window ends (fx.flashTime / guns52's 40 ms) its light falls over this k^2 tail from fx.flashSecondFrame's share instead of a cut (fix 1): the on/off square wave at the fire rate becomes a pulse with a soft back edge.
numbers.slotHysteresis_why: share of distance (fix 2): a borrowed fixture slot keeps its fixture unless the re-pick's best is under 0.65 of the current one's distance from the camera (the re-pick's best at nearly the same distance swapped every 0.25 s at a walk).
numbers.slotFadeS_why: s: a slot's move is a cross-fade over this (fix 2): its twin fades out where it stood while the slot fades in at its new fixture (smoothstep); NIGHT47's 0.18 s out + 0.18 s in went through black.
numbers.flickerHz_why: the danger fixtures' (braziers') perlin time scale (fix 2; Vfx33, UnityTuning.Look33FlickerHz 11 off): under the strobe line (strobeHz 3), a fire's slow breath instead of an 11 Hz shimmer.

numbers.swellHz_why: Hz: what a strobing pulse becomes (fixes 4 and 10): a swell slower than the strobe line, still visibly alive.

numbers._why: Builder G (GG 2026-10-20, NIGHT54.md: each boss its own palette and lighting identity that shifts during the fight, JoJo's colour turns; the guns by colour theory). A second URP Volume (BossGrade54.cs, priority common.priority over Look's post volume) blends in over common.fadeInS when a boss bar is live (BossRead41) and out over common.fadeOutS; each boss has a grade per phase (p1..p3: colour filter, split toning shadows / highlights in URP's soft-light space where 0.5 grey is neutral, saturation / contrast / EV as deltas on PostFx's live values) and a lighting layer (fog lerp, ambient and key-light multipliers) written after the other writers (it re-reads their colours each frame). No hue rotation anywhere: the player's cyan (colors.usable #19d3e6, hue 187) and the danger red-orange (colors.enemy #ff4a1c, hue 12) keep their hues in every palette (rule 8); EV deltas are never above 0 (the lead 14:45: do not raise brightness). The web has none of these numbers (it has no boss grade).

common.priority_why: the boss Volume's priority over Look's post volume (0): URP lerps each overridden parameter toward it by its weight
common.fadeInS_why: s: the grade blends in after the fight's first frame (the start turn rides on it)
common.fadeOutS_why: s: the grade leaves after the boss dies or its bar hides (slower than in: the aftermath settles back to NIGHT53's look)
common.turnS_why: s: THE TURN (a phase change, the fight's start, a stagger window opening): one smooth envelope (GG's 0.3-0.8 s ask), the duotone flipped and the next phase's wash at its peak, then the new phase settles
common.turnPeak_why: the envelope's peak as a share of turnS (a fast attack, a slower release: a cut, not a pulse)
common.turnGapS_why: s: the least time between two turns (a later event inside it is dropped). One turn is one light-dark pair, so at most 1 a second: under the 3 flashes a second photosensitivity limit (WCAG 2.3.1)
common.intensity_why: every phase colour's distance from neutral (the white filter, the 0.5-grey split toning) and its saturation / contrast deltas x this (the lead's n54-r2 a254: at 1 the graded frame moved 3-4 deg of hue and 0.01 of value against the ungraded one, once the stack refresh was missing too; the lead's aim: >= 25 deg or >= 0.08 value in P1)
common.evGain_why: each phase's EV delta x this (all <= 0: darker only; THE WICK's P1 -0.35 -> -0.49 EV: the dark arena, the hot boss)
common.turnSat_why: saturation points added at a turn's peak (the wash reads as colour, not as a flash of light; the lead: much stronger at the turn)
common.turnContrast_why: contrast points added at a turn's peak
common.turnEv_why: EV at a turn's peak: a turn darkens (never brightens: no white flash; the lead 14:45: the lighting is too bright already)
common.washMix_why: the colour filter's share of the next phase's wash at a turn's peak (0.8: the wash reads as the next phase's colour while the player's cyan keeps 20 % of its channel through the 0.1 s peak)
common.turnFlip_why: at a turn's peak the split toning's shadow and highlight colours swap by this share (the JoJo duotone flip; 1 = fully swapped)
common.openScale_why: a stagger window opening (the boss's big moment between phases) turns at this share of a phase turn's strength, into the same phase
common.rimMinFilter_why: the floor of the colour filter's channel the player's rim colour is divided by (the rim is pre-compensated so it reads as cyan after the grade)
common.coreGain_why: the player's tracer cores (WeaponFx's bounce line, the laser) x this in a graded fight: a brighter core against a darker arena (value contrast)
common.proofMinHue_why: a254: the graded frame's mean hue moved at least this many degrees from the ungraded one (or proofMinV / proofMinS)
common.proofMinV_why: a254: or the mean value (HSV V, 0..1) moved this much
common.proofMinS_why: a254: or the mean saturation moved this much
