move54._why: View row (NightRows.ViewOn(cfg, "move54")). Builder M: the camera's smoothness (the view only: hitstop's camera hold, the step-down pop, stepped views). Off = NIGHT53's camera.
move54.enabled_why: ON at the NIGHT54 freeze: M: a354 GREEN on / RED off on n52-foundry and n52-iceline (n54-r2): camera held 0.250 -> 0.150 s over 4 kill freezes, jitter 0.246 -> 0.191 / 0.189; golden and fingerprints EQUAL

numbers._why: Builder M (Game/Move54.cs, SurvivalGame.Move54.cs). The view only: no Mover, no sim step result, no Core number changes (golden 0 mismatches, fingerprints EQUAL). impact: the impact director's (Game/ImpactFrames) config view re-reads only these paths; step: the grounded step's camera height spring.

impact._why: The kill freezes are the loop's most frequent hold of the camera (the world stops, the mouse keeps turning): in a horde fight a 0.085 s hold every design.impact.cooldown.any 0.5 s reads as a stop-start chop. Only the gun-kill tiers get shorter (about 60 % of NIGHT53's); the parries (design.impact.freeze.parry 0.25 / perfectParry 0.3), the gauntlet (design.n42.impact42.gauntlet*), the punch kill, the heavy hit and the budget and gap stay NIGHT53's (the crunch GG asked for on earlier nights; the gauntlet's 0.16-0.24 s is budgeted beside the kills, so the budget is not lowered). The sim's own kill request (feel.hitstopTime 0.04) still floors a kill (the longest request wins).
impact.killS_why: Read as design.n42.impact42.killS (Move54.ImpactPaths): a gun kill holds 0.05 s (6 sim steps, 3 frames at 60 fps; NIGHT53 0.085): still above the sim's 0.04 floor, the bottom of hitfeel-web.md number 4's band (an ordinary kill, not a finisher).
impact.headshotKillS_why: As design.n42.impact42.headshotKillS: a headshot kill holds 0.08 s (NIGHT53 0.12): it keeps its rank over a body kill (1.6x), shorter so a KESTREL headshot streak does not stall the run.
impact.killCapS_why: As design.n42.impact42.killCapS: a multi-kill step holds at most 0.12 s (NIGHT53 0.18): killS + design.impact.freeze.killPerExtra 0.025 x (N - 1) reaches it at 4 kills, so a THUNDERCLAP blast still reads bigger than one kill.
impact.tableKill_why: As design.impact.freeze.kill (the table read with impact42 off; NIGHT53 0.058): the sim's floor 0.04.

slowMo._why: Every slow-mo (design.impact.slowMo's last kill / perfect parry / multi-kill, the core punch, the debut, the BULWARK finisher, the arena room's last kill, slowAim27) started at its full slowness in one frame: the world's pace dropped from 1 to 0.2-0.35 between two frames (a stop). The world's slow share (after the freeze's run share; a freeze untouched) now eases down toward it; a slow-mo's end is its own source's ease (unchanged).
slowMo.easeInS_why: s: the ease's time constant (1 - e^-dt / 0.05 a frame: 63 % of the way in 0.05 s, 95 % in 0.15 s): short against the holds (design.impact.slowMo hold 0.3 s and up), so the slow moment keeps its length and depth, entered in 3-9 frames at 60 fps instead of 1.

look._why: The aim assist's pull and the lock's turn change the look once a sim step (SurvivalSim.Run.cs: assist.Step then input.SetLook), so on a 144-240 Hz display the camera turned in a 120 Hz staircase (some frames a whole step's pull, some none). The last step's own turn is now presented across the step at the frame's alpha, as the feet are (SurvivalGame.Move54.cs); the sim's yaw, the shots and the assist are unchanged.
look.maxStepPull_why: rad (5.7 degrees): a step's own turn larger than this is a snap (a lock taking a target, a scripted turn) and is shown at once, not spread; the assist's per-step pull is far under it (a lock turning 360 degrees a second is 0.05 rad a step).

quality._why: AUTO's dynamic resolution (quality.dynamic, the web's numbers) stepped the render scale 0.1 at a time after 2 s over 18 ms p95 and back up after 4 s under 13 ms: in a heavy fight the image visibly popped sharper and softer every few seconds. The row re-reads four of its paths (Game/Quality.cs): half the step, longer holds both ways (a wider hysteresis in time), a longer lockout. The thresholds, the floor (minScale 0.6) and the help ratio are the web's.
quality.step_why: Render scale change per decision (web 0.1): half the visible pop; a large overload still drops 0.1 in two decisions (holdTime apart).
quality.holdTime_why: s over quality.dynamic.highMs before a drop (web 2): a short spike (a burst of particles, a boss's tell) no longer drops the scale.
quality.holdUpTime_why: s under quality.dynamic.lowMs before a rise (web 4): the scale does not climb back mid-fight between two heavy moments (the up-down cycle that popped).
quality.lockoutTime_why: s with no drop after a drop that did not help (the CPU bound case; web 20): one undo per fight at most.

step._why: Mover's ground snap (collision.groundSnap 0.35) drops the feet up to 0.35 m in one 120 Hz step, and a step up (collision.stepHeight 0.4) lifts them in one; the camera followed in one frame (a pop). A grounded step (both ends on the ground or sliding) that moved the feet stepMin or more opens a window of gateFrames frames in which the drawn height's change beyond keepRate is held as a camera offset; a critically damped spring returns it to 0. Jumps, falls, landings and wall rides never open it.
step.omega_why: rad/s: the critically damped spring's rate. A held offset x0 is (1 + w t) e^-wt of itself at t: 9 % at 0.1 s, 2 % at 0.15 s (the ask: the true eye height within ~80-120 ms), starting with zero slope (the camera eases, never kicks).
step.stepMin_why: m in one sim step (12 m/s vertical at 120 Hz): above a run up or down a ramp (10 m/s on a 45 degree ramp is 7 m/s vertical), so only snaps and step ups open the window; a smaller pop is under 0.1 m.
step.keepRate_why: m/s: the vertical rate a frame keeps unsmoothed inside the window (a ramp's own motion beside the snap is not lagged).
step.maxOffset_why: m: at most collision.stepHeight 0.4 held (the largest one-step change a grounded step makes).
step.resetJump_why: m: a frame or a step that moves the feet farther vertically is a teleport, a respawn or a level start: the offset is dropped, never smoothed.
step.gateFrames_why: Frames the window stays open after the step: the step is drawn over the frames its interpolation spans (1 at 60 fps; 2-3 at 144-240 fps where a frame shows part of a step).

decor54._why: View row (NightRows.ViewOn(cfg, "decor54")). Builder D (Decor54.cs): GG 2026-10-20 "a lot of the decorative elements in several arenas are poorly executed and lack strong color direction". Every level spent cyan (CLAUDE.md rule 8: player-usable) on pure decor and painted its walls one flat tone. With it on, each level gets its own colour script (numbers.levels): the decor that marks nothing usable (LightPlan33's floor-perimeter trims, RoofView27's ceiling strips (the boundary's pale violet-white on a ceiling that bounds nothing, and the cyan ones lights49 gave a strip within 1.5 m of a ride panel: a ceiling strip marks nothing usable), DoorFrames29's static door lines, PropsView29's prop collars / console panels / floor strips) takes the level's accent (only a cyan or boundary-white piece: a danger-orange floor strip stays), and the map stone's side faces take the level's wall tone with a value ramp (a darker base, a lighter upper band). Usable cyan keeps its colour and stays the brightest accent (ride strips / dashes, ledge rims, pads, grapple rings, pickups, the guide lamps under the exit lintels and Look43's exit frames (the route)). Colours and emission strengths only: no geometry, collider, level file or sim change. Off = NIGHT53's look exactly.
decor54.enabled_why: ON at the NIGHT54 freeze: D: [decor54] on n54-r2: cyan decor pieces 2-3 -> 0 and floor trims 12-17 -> 0 per level, usable cyan the brightest; round 2 (lenses, wall-top rims, the off switch) re-checked on the freeze build

numbers._why: Unity-side view numbers (the web never had a per-level decor script: its levels were one survival map with one palette). Hexes are sRGB, written as numbers like the other *Hex keys (0x.. in each _why).
numbers.accentScale_why: x the decor's own luminance (0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B of its HDR colour) when it moves to the accent: the accent is scaled to that luminance x 0.8, not to the same RGB (brass, citrine and ivory are brighter than cyan at equal channels: ivory 0.95 vs cyan 0.75), so every decor piece ends under the usable cyan it sat at (the brief: usable cyan stays the brightest accent in the room).
numbers.usableCap_why: a moved decor piece's luminance is also capped at this share of the brightest usable cyan renderer under the map (measured each pass): RoofView27's strips were drawn at roof27.stripBrightness, brighter than some usable pieces; 0.9 keeps cyan the brightest thing in every room.
numbers.rimDecorKinds_why: map box kinds whose top rim (SurvivalBuilder's world.rimKinds neon, one cyan mesh with the ride strips and node cubes) moves to the level's accent: a room wall's top is where it meets the ceiling, a line nobody stands on (the lead's n54-r2 frames: the cyan ceiling-edge and pillar-top lines). Ledges, bridges, islands, cover, slabs and spires keep their cyan lip: you land on those.
numbers.onSurfaceM_why: m: a lit lens (sconce, recessed strip, pole, flood) that lights49 coloured cyan keeps cyan only when its box is within this of a usable surface (a ride panel, a climb step, a pad, a grapple node: lights49's own read, LightPlan33.Cached49): ON the surface, mounted on it. lights49's 1.5 m reach also coloured the lenses on the room wall beside a ride panel; those move to the accent.
numbers.toneMix_why: share of the level's wall tone mixed into a stone side face's existing vertex colour (look52's tiers and look43's drain stay 40 % visible: the kinds still read apart).
numbers.bandM_why: m above each side face's own base (MeshKit's uv3.y) where the face reaches the upper tone: a room wall is 8-12 m, so its top quarter reads as the lighter band; a 1-2 m ledge stays near the base tone; a wall standing on a 15 m spire floor ramps from its own foot, not from y = 0.
numbers.rampGamma_why: the ramp's curve (t^gamma, t = y / bandM): above 1 holds the base dark over the lower half and lifts the upper band, so the wall reads as a dark plinth under a lit band, not an even gradient.
numbers.hueGapMinDeg_why: the least hue gap each saturated accent keeps from the role tokens (usable 186, danger 12, parry 44, RIVAL 311, boundary 250; UnityTuning.Look49): 5 more than Look49AccentMinHueGapDeg (20). Pale accents (s < 0.45) are told apart by saturation. The [decor54] line prints each level's least gap.

levels._why: keyed by the level id after its 'nNN-' prefix (n52-foundry -> foundry), so every cut of a level reads its script. Each: accentHex (the decor), wallBaseHex (a side face at its own base), wallUpperHex (at bandM above it).

foundry._why: THE FOUNDRY: pale brass (0xd9be84, hue 41, s 0.39) on dark umber walls (0x2a1e17 -> 0x7a5e44). Brass fittings on a sooty foundry: the warm accent sits far under the parry's saturated yellow (s 0.77) and the lava's red-orange (hue 12); cyan, the complement of umber, pops hardest here.

iceline._why: THE ICE LINE: cobalt (0x467eff, hue 222, s 0.73) on slate steel (0x161e2c -> 0x5c6c84). A deep cold blue 36 deg from cyan and 28 from the boundary's violet-white, half cyan's luminance (0.24 vs 0.52 linear): the usable cyan reads as the bright one; no warm accent on a cold level.

kiln._why: THE KILN: oxidised copper patina (0x6fb884, hue 137, s 0.40) on dark fired clay (0x241a20 -> 0x6a4c56). Green against the kiln's red-orange heat is the complement (danger reads hotter); 49 deg from cyan and desaturated, far from the health pickup's saturated green.

span._why: THE SPAN: emerald (0x64d94c, hue 110, s 0.65) on indigo (0x161530 -> 0x46447e). Green on indigo at dusk over a bridge: 76 deg from cyan, 27 from the kiln's patina and 33 from the spire's citrine; the indigo walls keep the violet family without touching the boundary's pale violet-white or RIVAL's magenta.

spire._why: THE SPIRE: citrine (0xb4d85a, hue 77, s 0.58) on bone stone (0x24221e -> 0x8a8474). A yellow-green 33 deg past the parry's yellow and far from cyan; bone walls keep the tall shaft's value ramp the strongest of the six.

finale._why: THE FINALE: warm ivory (0xf2e6d0, s 0.14) on dark mauve-brown (0x1a1418 -> 0x5e5058). The last level is the quietest: a near-white warm accent (warm, so never the boundary's violet-white) lets cyan and the bosses' own palettes (grade54) carry the colour.

numbers.chainGapS_why: s of PLAY time (sim seconds, freezes excluded): a kill within this of the one before continues a chain. NIGHT56 G (G2): 0.45 -> 0.55. The KESTREL's LIVE interval is 0.483 s (weapons.revolver.fireInterval 0.4 x design.n39.p39.intervalMult 1.2 = 58 steps at 120 Hz; `n56 kestrel --scheme alt`), so NIGHT55's 0.45 (set for a 0.4 s interval) never chained a KESTREL kill: n56-r1's a355 read chain 1 on every kill, its taps 0.508-0.516 s apart. 0.55 chains the KESTREL at its own rate and a tap a frame or two late (0.517 s: `--scheme tap`), and stays under a355's spaced pass (40 frames, ~0.62 s of play). a354's spacing (0.483-0.492 s) IS the KESTREL's own rate, so any gap that chains the KESTREL chains it too: a354 measures move54 alone with -skygrindOff55. ULTRAKILL counts a multikill within 0.5 s (web.md section 3.3, the wiki's Style page).

numbers._why: Builder V's numbers for BossMotion63 (Game/BossMotion63.Layer.cs; NIGHT63.md section 3 V; Research/2026-10-22-forge63/research-boss-animation.md). View only: the sim never reads them (no tape bit; the hitboxes, the damage frames and every fingerprint untouched). Distances are SHARES of each boss's own size, its collider radius from the sim's own config (THE WICK design.n37.wick37.boss.cageR 1.7 m, THE ICEBREAKER design.n40.brawl40.body.radius 1.2 m, THE KILN WYRM half its head design.n24.wyrm.body.headW / 2 = 1.5 m, THE LOOM design.n37.loom37.bodyHalfH 1.6 m, THE CROWN design.n37.crown37.crown.ringRadius 3 m), so one table fits five bosses of different sizes. The springs are t3ssel8r's second-order system (k1 = z / (pi f), k2 = 1 / (2 pi f)^2, k3 = r z / (2 pi f); f the natural frequency in Hz, z the damping, r the initial response: r > 1 overshoots, r < 0 dips first), stepped on the world's frame time (slow motion and the sim's hitstop apply: the view freezes with the sim) in sub-steps under the system's safe step; the flinch's envelope runs on the frame clock so it shows inside the sim's hitstop (no second freeze). The web has no such numbers: it has no campaign bosses.

follow._why: The drawn body follows the sim's rigid pose through a spring instead of copying it: it lags a little as the boss moves off, overshoots as it stops (momentum).
follow.f_why: Hz. The research's 1.5-3 Hz band for a body that trails; 2.2 Hz settles in about 0.4 s, quick enough that a walk's lag stays a few centimetres.
follow.z_why: Damping: under-damped (the research's 0.4-0.7) so a stop overshoots once and settles, never wobbles.
follow.r_why: Initial response > 1: the body answers a start or a stop with a small overshoot (the research's r 1-2 for trailing parts).
follow.snap_why: A rigid jump larger than this share of the boss's size in one frame (a teleport, a leg change, a retry) resets the spring to the rigid pose: never a long slide across the room.

lean._why: The lean spring the wind-up and the strike drive: -1 is the full wind-up lean back, + the strike's lunge forward. Its overshoot past rest after the strike is the follow-through.
lean.f_why: Hz: faster than the body's follow so the pose reads as the boss's own action.
lean.z_why: Damping: lightly under-damped so the strike snaps through rest and swings back once (follow-through, overshoot). Simulated (the layer's own step, 60 fps): a 0.55 s wind-up's pose shows 0.45 s before its hit; the strike peaks at 1.18 of the full lean forward and swings back only to -0.22 (at z 0.42, r 1.5, hold 0.16 s it swung to 1.29 and -0.34: a wobble).
lean.r_why: Initial response > 1: the strike's step change kicks the lean forward at once (a snap, not an ease); 1.2, not 1.5, so the snap does not slam into the guard's tilt.

windup._why: The anticipation pose before each attack, driven by the sim's own attack state (BossAttackClock63: the wind-up's progress toward its hit): the boss leans back away from the player, pulls back and crouches. Eased in over the first riseShare of the wind-up and then held, so the pose is up long before the hit (B1's doneWhen: visible >= 250 ms before every hit; the shortest wind-up in config is about 0.55 s).
windup.riseShare_why: The share of the wind-up over which the pose eases in (then it is held to the hit): 0.3 of a 0.55 s wind-up is 165 ms, so the pose is visible about 0.35 s or more before the hit.
windup.deg_why: Degrees the boss leans back (its top away from the player) at the full wind-up: readable at 20 m (a 4 m boss's top moves about 0.9 m).
windup.back_why: The pull back away from the player at the full wind-up, a share of the boss's size.
windup.crouch_why: The squash at the full wind-up (height x (1 - crouch), the width kept volume-equal): a coiled spring.
windup.sideDeg_why: Degrees the boss cocks to one side at the full wind-up (the side alternates attack by attack). A lean toward or away from the player turns mostly in depth from where the player stands; a side lean turns in the screen's plane, so the wind-up reads on screen.
windup.breathMute_why: How much of the idle breathing the wind-up mutes (1: all of it), so the wind-up is the one motion on screen (the research's pitfall: wobble drowning the telegraph).

strike._why: The strike: the lean target jumps forward for holdS, then back to rest; the lean spring overshoots and settles (follow-through).
strike.lunge_why: The lean target at the strike, a share of the wind-up's full lean, forward (top toward the player, body lunged by lunge x windup.back).
strike.holdS_why: s the strike's forward target holds after the strike's first step (15 frames at 60 fps): long enough that the lean has reached it before the release, so the swing back stays small.

flinch._why: A hit flinch on each damage event (the boss's health falls): a volume-keeping squash, a recoil away from the player and a tip back, all on Quilez's impulse envelope h exp(1 - h), h = t / peakS, which peaks at 1 at peakS and is near 0 by lifeS. Its clock is the frame clock: it shows inside the sim's hitstop, adding no second freeze.
flinch.peakS_why: s from the hit to the squash's peak (the research's 40 ms): 2.4 frames at 60 fps, so the first drawn frame already shows 0.75 of it (B1's doneWhen: within 2 frames).
flinch.lifeS_why: s the envelope lives (it is 0.001 of its peak by then).
flinch.squash_why: The squash at the peak: height x (1 - squash), width x 1 / sqrt(1 - squash) (the volume kept). 0.26, not 0.2 (NIGHT63's rule-8 round: THE WICK's flinch changed 22,253 px on n63-b4's same-run pair; the squash is the flinch's one part in the screen's plane).
flinch.recoil_why: The recoil away from the player at the peak, a share of the boss's size.
flinch.deg_why: Degrees the boss tips back (away from the player) at the peak.
flinch.minShare_why: The smallest flinch a hit draws, a share of the full one: a chip still reads as a hit.
flinch.fullAt_why: A hit that takes this share of the boss's pool or more draws the full flinch (between, linear from minShare).

slump._why: A slump while staggered (a CYAN window, THE ICEBREAKER stuck or dazed, THE KILN WYRM staggered): the boss sinks, droops forward and squashes, and sways slowly side to side, through its own spring (it sags in, and rises back when the stagger ends). B1's SPOT pose: 0.6 s into a stagger.
slump.f_why: Hz: a heavy, slow sag (settled by about 0.6 s, the reel's stagger frame).
slump.z_why: Damping: one soft bounce at the bottom of the sag.
slump.r_why: Initial response: a little drop past the hold as it gives way.
slump.sink_why: The sink at the full slump, a share of the boss's size (THE WICK 1.02 m, its raised limit; THE ICEBREAKER into its knees, capped at its 0.6 m): the slump's biggest on-screen move. NIGHT63's rule-8 round: 0.6, not 0.45 (n63-b4's same-run pair on THE WICK's stagger changed 37,345 px, under 41,472; the cage is about 200 x 300 px at boss63's 12.5 m).
slump.deg_why: Degrees the boss droops forward (its top toward the player: beaten, its weak point offered). 12, not 22: a droop toward the player turns about the screen's horizontal axis, mostly in depth from where the player stands, so the rule-8 round moved the tilt into the side keel.
slump.sideDeg_why: Degrees the boss keels to one side at the full slump (the side alternates stagger by stagger): the keel turns in the screen's plane, so a player sees it. 26, not 14 (the rule-8 round); with the droop and the sway it stays under THE WICK's 30 deg guard and is scaled to a tighter boss's.
slump.squash_why: The squash at the full slump (height x (1 - squash), the volume kept): in the screen's plane. 0.22, not 0.12 (the rule-8 round).
slump.swayDeg_why: Degrees of the slow side-to-side sway while slumped (dazed).

breath._why: Idle breathing: a slow pulse in height and lift, so a boss is never a statue (muted through a wind-up: windup.breathMute).
breath.hz_why: Breaths a second: a slow, heavy breath (2.5 s).
breath.scale_why: The pulse in height (x 1 +- scale, the width kept volume-equal).
breath.lift_why: The rise and fall with the breath, a share of the boss's size.

limit._why: THE GUARD (B1's doneWhen): every view offset capped so the drawn body never leaves its collider: the body's offset from its rigid pose at most `share` of the boss's size (its collider radius), its tilt at most `deg`, its squash at most `squash` from 1 on any axis. Per boss below where its hitboxes need it tighter.
limit.share_why: The largest offset, a share of the boss's collider radius: the drawn centre stays inside the inner half of its collider.
limit.deg_why: The largest tilt in degrees (a full slump 22 deg plus a sway).
limit.squash_why: The largest squash or stretch on any axis (a full flinch 0.26 on a breath; a full slump 0.22 on a breath). 0.32, not 0.28 (the rule-8 round).

bosses._why: Per boss: gain (every amplitude x gain), follow (the follow spring's share: 0 = the drawn body sits on its sim pose), limitShare / limitDeg (the guard, tighter where the drawn body is its hitbox). Read by the bossRise id.

numbers.lines_why: A boss order's raw text -> its line while it names a weapon not held. THE KILN WYRM (design.n43.wick43.bosses wyrmIdle / wyrmStagger, design.n30.wyrm30.linePunch, design.n61.bossRule61 wyrm): only the gauntlet staggers its head (wyrmTell48 OFF), so the line names the gauntlet as the hand to take, never {punch} (the fist does nothing to it); staggered, every weapon lands open (bossRule61's wyrm_why), so the slug order becomes the window's own words. THE ICEBREAKER (bossRule61 brawl40, design.n40.brawl40 line.entry): the gauntlet's swing and the punch both land x1 at any range and drain its meter (bossRule61's brawl40_why), so the line offers the punch or the swap.

wyrm71._why: B3 (T-154): a wyrm motion that reads (BossMotion63 wyrm numbers; render only)

numbers._why: Builder B (NIGHT71 B3; Game/Wyrm71.cs). View only: the sim never reads them (THE KILN WYRM's segments, hitboxes and damage frames untouched; WyrmView draws the sim's boxes, only their drawing moves). With the row on, BossMotion63 draws THE KILN WYRM with these numbers over its own (design.n63.bossMotion63.numbers: the shared block, then bosses.wyrm); a number not given here keeps bossMotion63's. THE GUARD IS NEVER WIDENED: bosses.wyrm's limitShare 0.25 of the head's 1.5 m half width (0.375 m), limitDeg 14 and the shared limit.squash 0.32 stay in force, because the wyrm's drawn boxes are its hitboxes (WyrmView.N63V.cs: 'a shot finds what you see'); Wyrm71.Params holds every limit at bossMotion63's own even if a limit is written here (NIGHT71 B3 critic, Logs/n71/verdict-B3.md point 3: 0.5 / 26 read 2.00 of BossMotion63's own guard). The motion this row adds is inside that guard: the gain, a deeper squash, the body wave to the tail. Why: under bosses.wyrm's numbers the breath was 2.4 cm and the gain 0.6, so the b10 pairs read stagger 16,649 px against rule 8's 41,472 and idle 389 (Logs/n63/verdict-B1.md:69,73). The web has no such numbers: it has no boss motion layer.
numbers.gain_why: Every amplitude x this (bosses.wyrm 0.6; the other four bosses 1). The guard still holds the head's offset at 0.375 m and its turn at 14 deg.
numbers.slumpSquash_why: The stagger's squash (shared slump.squash 0.22 x gain 0.6 = 0.13): 0.3 x gain 1 squashes the head to 0.70 of its height (inside limit.squash 0.32: 0.68), and the body pieces by 0.3 x their share to the tail, so a staggered wyrm slumps inside the guard.
numbers.tail_why: The motion's share left at the tail (bosses.wyrm 0.35): the body wave and the sag reach the far body, so the whole worm reads alive, not only its head.
numbers.breathHz_why: The body wave's rate (shared breath.hz 0.4): a slow slither, 2 s a cycle.
numbers.breathLift_why: The body wave's rise and fall, a share of each piece's half width (shared breath.lift 0.04 x gain 0.6 = 2.4 cm on the head): 0.18 m on the head, travelling down the body at bosses.wyrm.wave 0.45 rad a piece.
numbers.breathScale_why: The pieces' swell with the wave (shared breath.scale 0.04).
numbers.slumpDeg_why: The stagger's droop toward the player in degrees (shared slump.deg 12): with the side keel the head's turn is held at bosses.wyrm's limitDeg 14; the droop takes a larger share of those 14 deg (toward the player, not sideways).

numbers._why: Builder F (NIGHT71 F3; Game/Kicks71.cs, Feel46View.cs). With the row on (feel46 on), feel46's G2-G4 run with these numbers whatever design.n46.feel46.numbers.kicks says. deg: view pitch-up (kicks) or FOV (the punch-in), x EFFECTS INTENSITY x CAMERA SHAKE / FOV KICK, none under REDUCED MOTION; s: KickStack's attack and recover on frame time. BIGGER: every kill kick above the KESTREL tap's own 1.2 + 1.8 deg fire kick (body < head < punch kept), recovered over 0.22 s (the fire kick's is shorter), the body kill's FOV punch-in 0.7 -> 1.2 deg (below the headshot kill's 1.5). RARER: a hit kick at most once per hitGapS (feel46 kicked every hit); a kill within killGapS of a kill kick adds only what its tier has over that kick (a multi-kill is one kick); the THUNDERCLAP's own shot keeps heavyFireKeep of its shake (feel46: 0.6). View only: no sim read, no tape bit. The web has no such numbers: its feel.js had no kill ladder on camera.
